entities.summary: Wrote nothing, was executed by his own city, and set the shape of philosophical argument since.

entities.name: Aristotle
entities.summary: Attempted a systematic account of everything, and his errors held authority nearly as long as his insights.

entities.name: Archimedes
entities.summary: Came nearer to calculus than anyone would for eighteen centuries.

entities.name: Al-Khwarizmi
entities.summary: His name became algorithm and his book's title became algebra.

entities.name: Ibn Sina
entities.summary: His medical canon was the standard text in Europe and the Islamic world for six hundred years.

entities.name: Aryabhata
entities.summary: Gave a place-value system, an accurate value for pi, and a rotating Earth.

entities.name: Johannes Gutenberg
entities.summary: Combined movable type, oil ink and the press into something that made copying cheap enough to change what could be thought.

entities.name: Iron Smelting
entities.summary: Pre-Hittite Anatolian bloomery iron; the metal that made tools cheap rather than precious.

entities.name: Alphabetic Writing
entities.summary: One sign per sound rather than per syllable or word, which made literacy learnable in weeks.

entities.name: Zero as a Number
entities.summary: Brahmagupta gave rules for arithmetic with zero and with negatives, not merely a placeholder.
entities.search_phrase: Brahmagupta zero as a number Brahmasphutasiddhanta

entities.name: Papermaking
entities.summary: Cheap writing material from plant fibre, in China centuries before it reached the west.

entities.name: Woodblock Printing
entities.summary: Text carved and reproduced in quantity in Tang China, long before movable type.

entities.name: Movable Type
entities.summary: Bi Sheng's ceramic type; reusable characters four centuries before Gutenberg.
entities.search_phrase: Bi Sheng movable type Song dynasty

entities.name: Gunpowder
entities.summary: A Chinese alchemical accident that ended the military logic of the walled city.

entities.name: Magnetic Compass
entities.summary: Made open-water navigation repeatable rather than lucky.

entities.name: The Printing Press
entities.summary: Movable metal type and a screw press in Mainz; the first information technology with a mass market.

entities.name: The Telescope
entities.summary: Turned the sky into something to be examined rather than contemplated.

entities.name: The Steam Engine
entities.summary: Newcomen's atmospheric engine; work no longer limited by muscle, wind or falling water.

entities.name: Vaccination
entities.summary: Jenner's cowpox inoculation, and the beginning of deliberate control of infectious disease.

entities.name: Germ Theory of Disease
entities.summary: Established that specific microbes cause specific diseases, which made surgery survivable.

entities.name: Practical Electric Lighting
entities.summary: Decoupled the working day from daylight.

entities.name: Powered Flight
entities.summary: Twelve seconds at Kitty Hawk.

entities.name: Antibiotics
entities.summary: Fleming's penicillin; bacterial infection stopped being a common cause of death.

entities.name: Controlled Nuclear Fission
entities.summary: The first self-sustaining chain reaction, under a squash court in Chicago.

entities.name: The Transistor
entities.summary: The switch that made computing small, cheap and eventually universal.

entities.name: The Integrated Circuit
entities.summary: Many components on one wafer, which is why computing kept getting cheaper.

entities.name: Packet-Switched Networking
entities.summary: The first ARPANET link; messages broken into pieces that route themselves.

entities.name: The Human Genome Sequenced
entities.summary: A species reading its own instructions.

entities.name: San Lorenzo Tenochtitlán
entities.summary: First great Olmec capital and earliest monumental centre in Mesoamerica, source of the colossal stone heads.

entities.name: La Venta
entities.summary: Olmec ceremonial city with the earliest large clay pyramid in Mesoamerica and buried serpentine offerings.

entities.name: Tres Zapotes
entities.summary: Late Olmec and Epi-Olmec centre; Stela C carries one of the earliest Long Count dates known.

entities.name: Laguna de los Cerros
entities.summary: Olmec centre controlling basalt quarries of the Tuxtlas that supplied monumental sculpture elsewhere.

entities.name: Chalcatzingo
entities.summary: Highland trade town whose Olmec-style cliff reliefs show interregional elite culture far from the Gulf coast.

entities.name: Cuicuilco
entities.summary: First city of the Basin of Mexico, with a great circular pyramid, buried by the Xitle lava flow.

entities.name: Tlatilco
entities.summary: Large Preclassic village-town in the Basin of Mexico known for its figurines and rich burials.

entities.name: Cholula
entities.summary: Continuously occupied pilgrimage city holding the largest pyramid by volume on Earth, the Tlachihualtepetl.

entities.name: Mitla
entities.summary: Zapotec religious capital and burial place of high priests, famed for geometric stone mosaic facades.

entities.name: Yagul
entities.summary: Fortified Postclassic Zapotec town with palace complex and one of Mesoamerica's largest ballcourts.

entities.name: Dainzú
entities.summary: Zapotec valley town whose carved slabs depict helmeted ballplayers in an early distinctive style.

entities.name: El Tajín
entities.summary: Classic Veracruz capital with the niched Pyramid and seventeen ballcourts, centre of a ballgame cult.

entities.name: Xochicalco
entities.summary: Fortified Epiclassic hilltop city that rose after Teotihuacan, with an observatory cave and calendar reform stelae.

entities.name: Cacaxtla
entities.summary: Epiclassic hilltop citadel whose battle murals fuse highland and Maya painting traditions.

entities.name: Teotenango
entities.summary: Walled Matlatzinca hill city of the Toluca valley, abandoned soon after the Spanish conquest.

entities.name: Tula
entities.summary: Toltec capital whose Atlantean warrior columns and legend of Tollan shaped later Aztec political claims.

entities.name: Tenayuca
entities.summary: First Chichimec capital in the Basin of Mexico, with a serpent-ringed twin-stair pyramid prototype.

entities.name: Azcapotzalco
entities.summary: Tepanec imperial capital that dominated the Basin of Mexico until the Aztec Triple Alliance destroyed it in 1428.

entities.name: Tlatelolco
entities.summary: Twin city of Tenochtitlan and site of the greatest market in the Americas, absorbed by conquest in 1473.

caveats.text: Traditional founding date from Mexica annals.

entities.name: Texcoco
entities.summary: Acolhua capital and intellectual centre of the Triple Alliance under the poet-king Nezahualcoyotl.

entities.name: Tlacopan
entities.summary: Third and junior partner of the Aztec Triple Alliance, successor to Tepanec power west of the lake.

entities.name: Malinalco
entities.summary: Aztec ritual town with temples cut directly into living rock for eagle and jaguar warrior orders.

entities.name: Tzintzuntzan
entities.summary: Capital of the Purépecha (Tarascan) empire, with five round yácata platforms above Lake Pátzcuaro.

entities.name: Ihuatzio
entities.summary: Earlier Purépecha capital of the Pátzcuaro basin, with walled causeways and yácata pyramids.

entities.name: Pátzcuaro
entities.summary: Founding seat of Purépecha kingship and later the first colonial capital of Michoacán.

entities.name: Cempoala
entities.summary: Totonac capital and the first large city Cortés entered, whose ruler allied against the Aztecs.

entities.name: Quiahuiztlán
entities.summary: Totonac cliff town above the Gulf with a hillside cemetery of miniature temple tombs.

entities.name: Nakbé
entities.summary: Earliest large Maya centre, with monumental triadic architecture centuries before the Classic period.

entities.name: El Mirador
entities.summary: Preclassic Maya megacity whose La Danta complex is among the largest structures ever built, linked by causeways.

entities.name: Uaxactún
entities.summary: Maya city with the earliest known astronomical E-Group, conquered by Teotihuacan-backed Tikal in 378.

entities.name: Calakmul
entities.summary: Seat of the Snake Kingdom that built the largest Maya hegemony through vassal alliances against Tikal.

entities.name: Dos Pilas
entities.summary: Petexbatún war capital founded by a Tikal splinter dynasty, abandoned amid Late Classic warfare.

entities.name: Aguateca
entities.summary: Fortified Maya centre burned and abandoned so abruptly that whole household assemblages survive in place.

entities.name: Piedras Negras
entities.summary: Usumacinta kingdom whose stela series let Proskouriakoff prove Maya glyphs record real dynastic history.

entities.name: Yaxchilán
entities.summary: Riverbend Maya capital famed for carved lintels showing royal bloodletting and captive-taking.

entities.name: Bonampak
entities.summary: Small Maya court whose unfinished murals give the most vivid surviving images of Maya war and ritual.

entities.name: Palenque
entities.summary: Western Maya capital of K'inich Janaab' Pakal, with the tomb-bearing Temple of the Inscriptions.

entities.name: Toniná
entities.summary: Terraced acropolis city that captured Palenque's king and carries one of the latest Long Count dates.

entities.name: Comalcalco
entities.summary: Westernmost Maya city, built of fired brick because the delta had no stone.

entities.name: Copán
entities.summary: Southeastern Maya capital whose Hieroglyphic Stairway and sculpture record a 16-king dynasty.

entities.name: Quiriguá
entities.summary: Motagua valley city that beheaded Copán's king and raised the tallest stelae in the Maya world.

entities.name: Caracol
entities.summary: Sprawling low-density Maya city of agricultural terraces and causeways that defeated Tikal in 562.

entities.name: Xunantunich
entities.summary: Belize River valley centre that grew as neighbouring Maya capitals collapsed, crowned by El Castillo.

entities.name: Lamanai
entities.summary: One of the longest continuously occupied Maya towns, lasting from the Preclassic into the Spanish mission era.

entities.name: Altun Ha
entities.summary: Coastal Maya trading town whose tomb yielded the great jade head of the sun god K'inich Ahau.

entities.name: Cerros
entities.summary: Late Preclassic Maya coastal trading centre that built early painted temple facades then was abandoned.

entities.name: Cuello
entities.summary: Among the earliest known Maya villages, key evidence for the Preclassic origins of Maya society.

entities.name: Cobá
entities.summary: Northern Maya city of lakes and the longest sacbe causeway network, reaching 100 km to Yaxuná.

entities.name: Dzibilchaltún
entities.summary: Very long-lived Yucatec city with the equinox-aligned Temple of the Seven Dolls and a sacred cenote.

entities.name: Uxmal
entities.summary: Greatest Puuc-style Maya city, with the oval Pyramid of the Magician and elaborate lattice mosaic facades.

entities.name: Kabah
entities.summary: Puuc city linked to Uxmal by causeway, its Codz Poop facade covered in hundreds of rain-god masks.

entities.name: Sayil
entities.summary: Dispersed Puuc garden-city whose household survey reshaped views of Maya urban density.

entities.name: Labná
entities.summary: Puuc town dependent on chultun cisterns, known for its ornate corbelled arch gateway.

entities.name: Edzná
entities.summary: Maya city with a vast hydraulic canal and reservoir system and a five-storey palace-pyramid.

entities.name: Chichén Itzá
entities.summary: Cosmopolitan Terminal Classic capital fusing Maya and central Mexican styles around the Sacred Cenote.

entities.name: Mayapán
entities.summary: Last great walled Maya capital, ruling northern Yucatán by confederacy until factional revolt destroyed it.

entities.name: Tulum
entities.summary: Walled Maya seaport on Caribbean cliffs, a hub of the late canoe trade in salt, obsidian and cotton.

entities.name: Kaminaljuyú
entities.summary: Highland Maya capital controlling El Chayal obsidian, with early monumental sculpture and canal irrigation.

entities.name: Izapa
entities.summary: Pacific piedmont cacao centre whose narrative stelae bridge Olmec and Maya art and calendrics.

entities.name: Takalik Abaj
entities.summary: Pacific slope city with both Olmec-style boulders and early Maya stelae, a cultural transition point.

entities.name: Iximché
entities.summary: Kaqchikel Maya capital on a defensive plateau, briefly the first Spanish capital of Guatemala.

entities.name: Q'umarkaj
entities.summary: K'iche' Maya capital of the Popol Vuh lineages, burned by Pedro de Alvarado in 1524.

entities.name: Zaculeu
entities.summary: Mam Maya highland capital, surrendered after a Spanish siege by starvation in 1525.

entities.name: Joya de Cerén
entities.summary: Maya farming village buried by volcanic ash, preserving ordinary houses and gardens like a New World Pompeii.

entities.name: Chalchuapa
entities.summary: Long-lived southeastern centre on the cacao and obsidian routes, disrupted by the Ilopango eruption.

entities.name: Quelepa
entities.summary: Lenca-area centre east of the Lempa marking the non-Maya southeastern frontier of Mesoamerica.

entities.name: Guayabo de Turrialba
entities.summary: Largest known chiefly centre of Costa Rica, with cobbled causeways, aqueducts and stone mounds.

entities.name: Sitio Conte
entities.summary: Panamanian chiefly burial centre whose gold-rich graves define Coclé elite culture on the isthmus.

entities.name: En Bas Saline
entities.summary: Large Taíno chiefly village on Hispaniola, likely the seat of Guacanagarí who met Columbus in 1492.

entities.name: Caguana
entities.summary: Principal Taíno ceremonial plaza complex with petroglyph-lined bateyes for the ball game.

entities.name: Áspero
entities.summary: Fishing port of the Caral complex with the earliest monumental platform mounds on the Peruvian coast.

entities.name: Caral
entities.summary: Oldest known city in the Americas, with sunken circular plazas and pyramids and no evidence of warfare.

entities.name: Bandurria
entities.summary: Late Archaic coastal centre contemporary with Caral, evidence that early urbanism was regional not singular.

entities.name: Sechín Bajo
entities.summary: Holds one of the oldest monumental plazas in the Americas, a sunken circular court dated near 3500 BCE.

entities.name: Cerro Sechín
entities.summary: Casma valley temple faced with carved warrior and dismemberment reliefs, early monumental violence imagery.

entities.name: El Paraíso
entities.summary: Enormous Late Preceramic stone complex in the Chillón valley, an early experiment in monumental civic space.

entities.name: Kotosh
entities.summary: Highland ritual site whose Temple of the Crossed Hands marks early Andean religious architecture.

entities.name: La Galgada
entities.summary: Preceramic highland temple complex of superimposed ritual chambers in the Kotosh tradition.

entities.name: Chankillo
entities.summary: Fortified ceremonial centre with the oldest known solar observatory in the Americas, the Thirteen Towers.

entities.name: Chavín de Huántar
entities.summary: Pilgrimage centre whose underground galleries and Lanzón spread the first pan-Andean religious style.

entities.name: Pukara
entities.summary: First urban centre of the northern Titicaca basin, ancestor of Tiwanaku sculpture and sunken-court design.

entities.name: Chiripa
entities.summary: Early Titicaca village-temple complex with sunken courts that prefigure Tiwanaku's civic form.

entities.name: Huacas de Moche
entities.summary: Capital of the Moche state, dominated by the adobe Huaca del Sol and the mural-covered Huaca de la Luna.

entities.name: Sipán
entities.summary: Moche royal centre whose intact Lord of Sipán tomb transformed understanding of Andean kingship.

entities.name: Pampa Grande
entities.summary: Late Moche capital of nucleated urban compounds, burned and abandoned within two centuries.

entities.name: Galindo
entities.summary: Late Moche walled city marking the shift to defensive, class-segregated urbanism after the coastal collapse.

entities.name: Dos Cabezas
entities.summary: Moche pyramid town known for elite burials of unusually tall men with elaborate copper-gold regalia.

entities.name: Cahuachi
entities.summary: Nasca pilgrimage capital of adobe mounds, a ceremonial city largely empty between festivals.

entities.name: Ventilla
entities.summary: Largest Nasca habitation settlement, the residential counterpart to ceremonial Cahuachi.

entities.name: Lukurmata
entities.summary: Second city of the Tiwanaku state on Titicaca's shore, centre of raised-field farming.

entities.name: Khonkho Wankane
entities.summary: Pre-Tiwanaku altiplano civic-ceremonial centre with monoliths and sunken courts.

entities.name: Wari
entities.summary: Capital of the first Andean empire, a dense walled city of orthogonal compounds and administrative colonies.

entities.name: Conchopata
entities.summary: Wari secondary city and ceramic workshop centre known for oversized ritual urns and offering smashes.

entities.name: Pikillacta
entities.summary: Vast rigidly planned Wari provincial city near Cusco, apparently abandoned before completion.

entities.name: Viracochapampa
entities.summary: Unfinished Wari administrative city in the northern highlands, a template of imperial planning.

entities.name: Marcahuamachuco
entities.summary: Fortified highland ridge city of great galleries and round halls, independent neighbour of Wari.

entities.name: Batán Grande
entities.summary: Sicán religious and metalworking capital whose tombs and arsenical bronze industry dominated the north coast.

entities.name: Túcume
entities.summary: Late Sicán capital of 26 adobe pyramids around a sacred hill, later absorbed by Chimú and Inca.

entities.name: Chan Chan
entities.summary: Largest adobe city in the world, Chimú capital of ten walled royal ciudadelas and deep sunken wells.

entities.name: Farfán
entities.summary: Chimú provincial administrative centre later reused by the Inca to govern the north coast.

entities.name: Pachacamac
entities.summary: Great oracle city of the central coast, a pilgrimage centre respected by Wari, Ychsma and Inca alike.

entities.name: Cajamarquilla
entities.summary: Large adobe city of the Rímac valley, a major inland urban node beside Pachacamac.

entities.name: La Centinela
entities.summary: Capital of the Chincha kingdom, whose maritime merchants traded by balsa raft along the Pacific coast.

entities.name: Kuélap
entities.summary: Chachapoya cloud-forest citadel of hundreds of round houses behind twenty-metre walls.

entities.name: Gran Pajatén
entities.summary: Chachapoya montane centre of round buildings with mosaic stone figures on the eastern Andean slope.

entities.name: Cusco
entities.summary: Inca imperial capital and ritual navel of Tawantinsuyu, laid out with ceque lines and Sacsayhuamán above.

entities.name: Sacsayhuamán
entities.summary: Monumental Inca ceremonial fortress above Cusco, built of megalithic interlocking stonework.

entities.name: Ollantaytambo
entities.summary: Inca planned town still lived in on its original grid, with terraced temple works and a 1537 battle site.

entities.name: Pisac
entities.summary: Inca royal estate guarding the Sacred Valley entrance, with terraces, sun temple and cliff tombs.

entities.name: Choquequirao
entities.summary: Remote Inca ceremonial complex with llama mosaics in its terraces, a refuge in the Vilcabamba resistance.

entities.name: Vitcos
entities.summary: Capital of the neo-Inca state of Vilcabamba, with the oracle rock of Ñusta Hispana nearby.

entities.name: Huánuco Pampa
entities.summary: Purpose-built Inca provincial capital with 500 storehouses and a vast plaza for state hospitality.

entities.name: Vilcashuamán
entities.summary: Inca administrative city with a stepped ushnu platform where the emperor sat to review the province.

entities.name: Tambo Colorado
entities.summary: Well-preserved Inca coastal administrative centre built in painted adobe rather than stone.

entities.name: Raqchi
entities.summary: Inca way-station city on the Collasuyu road, dominated by the great Temple of Wiracocha.

entities.name: Tomebamba
entities.summary: Northern Inca capital and Huayna Capac's birth city, wrecked in the civil war before the Spanish arrived.

entities.name: Ingapirca
entities.summary: Cañari centre rebuilt as Ecuador's principal Inca complex around an elliptical sun temple.

entities.name: Quito
entities.summary: Northern highland centre that became an Inca administrative seat and Atahualpa's base in the civil war.

entities.name: Tumbes
entities.summary: Inca frontier port and temple town, the first Andean city Pizarro saw and the gateway to the conquest.

entities.name: Cajamarca
entities.summary: Inca provincial city with baths and plaza where Atahualpa was seized in November 1532.

entities.name: El Fuerte de Samaipata
entities.summary: Carved sandstone ritual rock and settlement on the Inca eastern frontier facing the Chiriguano lowlands.

entities.name: Incallajta
entities.summary: Largest Inca site east of the Andes, a frontier garrison city with a vast kallanka great hall.

entities.name: Aldea de Tulor
entities.summary: Oldest known village of the Atacama oases, clustered circular adobe rooms buried by desert sand.

entities.name: Quilmes
entities.summary: Largest pre-Columbian settlement in Argentina, a Calchaquí stone hill city that resisted Spain for decades.

entities.name: El Shincal de Quimivil
entities.summary: Southern Inca provincial capital of Kollasuyu, with paired ceremonial hills flanking a great plaza.

entities.name: Ciudad Perdida
entities.summary: Tairona stone-terraced city in the Sierra Nevada, hub of a network of some 200 linked settlements.

entities.name: Pueblito
entities.summary: Tairona coastal town of stone terraces and staircases, abandoned under Spanish pressure.

entities.name: Hunza
entities.summary: Seat of the Zaque, northern ruler of the Muisca confederation of the Colombian highlands.

entities.name: Bacatá
entities.summary: Capital of the Zipa and largest Muisca centre, a town of cane-and-clay enclosures rather than stone.

entities.name: Sugamuxi
entities.summary: Muisca sacred city whose great Sun Temple was the confederation's chief pilgrimage shrine.

entities.name: San Agustín
entities.summary: Dispersed funerary and ceremonial landscape with the largest group of megalithic statues in South America.

entities.name: Tierradentro
entities.summary: Andean ceremonial zone of painted underground shaft tombs cut into hilltops.

entities.name: Upano Valley complexes
entities.summary: Amazonian garden-city network of platform mounds and sunken roads, revealed by lidar in the Upano valley.

entities.name: Marajó mound complexes
entities.summary: Amazonian chiefdom of artificial habitation mounds and elaborate funerary urns at the mouth of the Amazon.

entities.name: Santarém
entities.summary: Large Tapajó town on terra preta soils at the Tapajós-Amazon junction, described as densely populated in 1542.

entities.name: Kuhikugu
entities.summary: Cluster of plaza towns joined by roads and moats, evidence of garden urbanism in the southern Amazon.

entities.name: Llanos de Mojos earthworks
entities.summary: Casarabe low-density urban network of causeways, canals and stepped mound centres on seasonal floodplain.

entities.name: Acre geoglyphs
entities.summary: Hundreds of geometric ditched enclosures in western Amazonia, ceremonial not defensive, cut into managed forest.

entities.name: Hopewell Ceremonial Earthworks
entities.summary: Geometric earthwork complexes of the Scioto valley, ritual gathering places for a continental exchange network.

entities.name: Newark Earthworks
entities.summary: Largest geometric earthwork complex on Earth, aligned to the 18.6-year lunar standstill cycle.

entities.name: Fort Ancient
entities.summary: Hopewell hilltop enclosure of 5.7 km of embankment walls with solar and lunar gateway alignments.

entities.name: East St. Louis Mound Center
entities.summary: Second largest mound precinct of greater Cahokia, a burned and abandoned satellite city.

entities.name: Moundville
entities.summary: Mississippian political and religious capital of 29 mounds on the Black Warrior River, later a necropolis.

entities.name: Etowah
entities.summary: Fortified Mississippian town whose marble effigy statues and copper plates define the Southeastern Ceremonial Complex.

entities.name: Spiro Mounds
entities.summary: Western Mississippian gateway centre whose Craig Mound held an unmatched trove of shell, copper and textiles.

entities.name: Ocmulgee
entities.summary: Early Mississippian town with a reconstructed earth lodge council chamber, ancestral to Muscogee history.

entities.name: Aztalan
entities.summary: Palisaded northern outpost of Mississippian culture, far up the Rock River from Cahokia.

entities.name: Angel Mounds
entities.summary: Palisaded Mississippian town on the Ohio River, a regional capital of the middle Ohio valley.

entities.name: Kincaid Mounds
entities.summary: Major Mississippian centre of the lower Ohio, key to the concept of a Cahokia-linked political sphere.

entities.name: Toltec Mounds
entities.summary: Plum Bayou culture mound and embankment centre laid out on solar alignments, pre-dating Mississippian towns.

entities.name: Winterville
entities.summary: Mississippian mound capital of the Yazoo basin, a ceremonial centre with few permanent residents.

entities.name: Emerald Mound
entities.summary: Second largest earthwork platform in the United States, ceremonial centre of the ancestral Natchez.

entities.name: Town Creek
entities.summary: Pee Dee culture palisaded ceremonial town on the Mississippian northeastern edge.

entities.name: Crystal River
entities.summary: Long-lived Gulf coast mound and stelae complex, a burial and trade centre of Woodland Florida.

entities.name: Mount Royal
entities.summary: St. Johns River mound town with a long causeway to a pond, linked by trade to distant Mississippian centres.

entities.name: Aztec Ruins
entities.summary: Planned great house on the Animas River, a successor centre after Chaco's decline.

entities.name: Salmon Ruins
entities.summary: Chacoan outlier great house on the San Juan, later reoccupied by Mesa Verde communities.

entities.name: Mesa Verde
entities.summary: Ancestral Pueblo cliff-dwelling towns of the Mesa Verde plateau, depopulated within a generation after 1280.

entities.name: Yellow Jacket Pueblo
entities.summary: Largest known Ancestral Pueblo village in the Mesa Verde region, with over a hundred kivas.

entities.name: Canyon de Chelly
entities.summary: Continuously inhabited canyon of Ancestral Pueblo cliff villages, later a Navajo heartland.

entities.name: Wupatki
entities.summary: Multi-storey pueblo built after the Sunset Crater eruption, where Pueblo, Sinagua and Hohokam traits met.

entities.name: Betatakin and Keet Seel
entities.summary: Short-lived Kayenta cliff villages abandoned wholesale during the late 13th-century migrations.

entities.name: Snaketown
entities.summary: Principal Hohokam town, with ballcourts and the canal irrigation that made the Sonoran desert farmable.

entities.name: Pueblo Grande
entities.summary: Hohokam platform-mound town controlling the largest canal system in the prehistoric Americas.

entities.name: Casa Grande
entities.summary: Classic Hohokam great house of caliche walls with astronomical apertures, abandoned by about 1450.

entities.name: Paquimé
entities.summary: Adobe city linking the Southwest and Mesoamerica, with macaw pens, ballcourts and piped water.

entities.name: La Quemada
entities.summary: Fortified hilltop city on Mesoamerica's northern frontier, with causeways and a hall of columns.

entities.name: Guachimontones
entities.summary: Teuchitlán capital of unique concentric circular pyramid complexes in western Mexico.

entities.name: Acoma Pueblo
entities.summary: Mesa-top pueblo among the oldest continuously inhabited settlements in North America.

entities.name: Taos Pueblo
entities.summary: Multi-storey adobe pueblo lived in for a millennium, a northern Rio Grande trade hub with the Plains.

entities.name: Oraibi
entities.summary: Hopi mesa village, one of the oldest continuously occupied settlements in the United States.

entities.name: Hawikuh
entities.summary: Largest Zuni town, mistaken for a city of gold by Coronado's expedition in 1540.

entities.name: Pecos Pueblo
entities.summary: Fortified frontier pueblo controlling trade between the Rio Grande farmers and Plains bison hunters.

entities.name: Paako
entities.summary: Tiwa pueblo of the Sandia foothills, abandoned during the colonial disruptions of the 17th century.

entities.name: Huff Village
entities.summary: Fortified Mandan earthlodge town on the Missouri, an early plains village-urban form.

entities.name: Double Ditch Village
entities.summary: Large Mandan earthlodge town with successive defensive ditches, depopulated by smallpox.

entities.name: Ozette
entities.summary: Makah whaling town whose mudslide-buried plank houses preserved an entire Northwest Coast village.

entities.name: SGang Gwaay
entities.summary: Haida plank-house town with standing mortuary poles, emblem of Northwest Coast village urbanism.

entities.name: Cathlapotle
entities.summary: Chinookan plankhouse town on the lower Columbia, a hub of the Northwest riverine trade.

entities.name: Talepakemalai
entities.summary: Earliest well-documented Lapita stilt-house village, starting point of the Pacific settlement expansion.

entities.name: Teouma
entities.summary: Oldest Lapita cemetery in the Pacific, the founding population evidence for Remote Oceania.

entities.name: Bourewa
entities.summary: Earliest known settlement in Fiji, the Lapita beachhead for colonising the central Pacific.

entities.name: Nukuleka
entities.summary: Founding Lapita village of Tonga, the first human settlement in Polynesia proper.

entities.name: Mulifanua
entities.summary: Only known Lapita site in Samoa, now submerged, marking the eastern limit of the first Polynesian push.

entities.name: Mangaasi
entities.summary: Long-occupied post-Lapita village that gave its name to a distinct central Vanuatu ceramic tradition.

entities.name: Chief Roi Mata's Domain
entities.summary: Residence, cave and mass burial island of a paramount chief whose peace-making order survives in oral tradition.

entities.name: Mu'a
entities.summary: Capital of the Tu'i Tonga maritime chiefdom, with terraced langi tombs of dressed coral slabs.

entities.name: Heketā and Haʻamonga ʻa Maui
entities.summary: Earlier Tu'i Tonga seat with a coral trilithon gateway, abandoned when the court moved to Mu'a.

entities.name: Pulemelei
entities.summary: Largest ancient structure in Polynesia's west, a stepped stone platform at the heart of a settlement complex.

entities.name: Nan Madol
entities.summary: Saudeleur capital of nearly 100 artificial islets built of basalt logs, a ceremonial city on a reef lagoon.

entities.name: Leluh
entities.summary: Walled basalt city of chiefly compounds and canal streets, Kosrae's counterpart to Nan Madol.

entities.name: House of Taga
entities.summary: Chamorro latte-stone village whose megalithic pillar houses defined Mariana settlement architecture.

entities.name: Gachpar
entities.summary: High-ranking Yapese village of stone platforms, paths and rai stone money, head of a tributary network.

entities.name: Badrulchau
entities.summary: Monolith and terrace complex of Palau's earthwork era, evidence of large organised pre-contact settlement.

entities.name: Taputapuātea
entities.summary: Central marae of the Polynesian world and node of the Oro cult, from which voyages and lineages radiated.

entities.name: Rapa Nui
entities.summary: Island society of dispersed hamlets and ahu platforms that carved and moved nearly a thousand moai.

entities.name: Orongo
entities.summary: Ceremonial village of stone-slab houses on a crater rim, used seasonally for the birdman competition.

entities.name: Wailua
entities.summary: Royal seat of Kaua'i, a sacred river district chaining heiau, birthstones and a place of refuge.

entities.name: Hōnaunau
entities.summary: Chiefly compound and walled place of refuge where kapu-breakers were granted sanctuary.

entities.name: Kahikinui
entities.summary: Dryland Hawaiian settlement district of hundreds of house sites and shrines, a study in intensive rain-fed farming.

entities.name: Kohala field system settlements
entities.summary: Dense coastal-to-upland Hawaiian villages tied to a vast walled dryland field system supporting chiefdoms.

entities.name: Taipivai
entities.summary: Marquesan valley polity of stone paepae platforms and tohua plazas with monumental tiki.

entities.name: Meʻae Iipona
entities.summary: Marquesan ceremonial site with the largest stone tiki in Polynesia outside Rapa Nui.

entities.name: Ara Metua settlements
entities.summary: Ring-road and marae network organising Rarotonga's districts, a rare paved road system in Polynesia.

entities.name: Maungakiekie
entities.summary: Largest Māori pā, a terraced volcanic cone fortress-town holding several thousand people.

entities.name: Wairau Bar
entities.summary: Earliest substantial settlement in New Zealand, a founding East Polynesian village and burial ground.

entities.name: Kohika
entities.summary: Waterlogged Māori lake village whose preserved wooden houses and canoes document pre-contact life.

entities.name: Budj Bim
entities.summary: Gunditjmara aquaculture landscape of eel channels, weirs and stone house clusters, a sedentary Aboriginal settlement.

entities.name: Brewarrina fish traps
entities.summary: Vast stone fish-trap complex on the Barwon that hosted large intertribal gatherings and shared harvests.

entities.name: Kuk Swamp
entities.summary: Independent centre of agricultural origins, with drained garden mounds supporting dense highland populations.

entities.name: Palembang
entities.summary: Riverine capital of Srivijaya, the thalassocracy that controlled the Malacca and Sunda straits.

entities.name: Muara Jambi
entities.summary: Largest Buddhist temple-city complex in Sumatra, a monastic and trading centre of the Malayu polity.

entities.name: Trowulan
entities.summary: Brick city of canals and reservoirs that served as capital of the Majapahit maritime empire.

entities.name: Prambanan
entities.summary: Royal temple-city of Hindu Mataram on the Kewu plain, abandoned when the court moved east.

entities.name: Temasek
entities.summary: Fortified 14th-century port settlement on Fort Canning hill, precursor to modern Singapore.

entities.name: Kota Batu
entities.summary: Early Bruneian capital and China-trade port on Borneo's north coast, forerunner of the sultanate.

entities.name: Butuan
entities.summary: Balangay-building trading polity of northern Mindanao with early gold work and Song-era China links.

entities.name: Sugbu
entities.summary: Visayan port polity and regional entrepôt where Magellan's expedition landed in 1521.

entities.name: Pejeng
entities.summary: Capital district of early Balinese kingdoms, with rock-cut sanctuaries and the great Moon of Pejeng drum.

entities.name: Zhengzhou
entities.summary: Vast walled early Shang capital whose Erligang phase defines the first Chinese urban expansion.

caveats.text: Modern Zhengzhou occupies the site and is still inhabited

entities.name: Anyang
entities.summary: Last Shang capital; source of the oracle-bone archive that begins Chinese written history.

entities.name: Haojing
entities.summary: Western Zhou royal capital and ritual centre of the Zhou mandate.

entities.name: Fenghao
entities.summary: Twin Zhou capital complex of Feng and Hao on the Feng River, sacked by the Quanrong.

entities.name: Luoyang
entities.summary: Capital of thirteen dynasties and eastern terminus of the Silk Road.

entities.name: Chang'an
entities.summary: Han and Tang imperial capital, at its height the largest city on earth and Silk Road head.

entities.name: Xianyang
entities.summary: First capital of a unified China under Qin Shi Huang.

entities.name: Linzi
entities.summary: Capital of the state of Qi and the largest, richest commercial city of the Warring States.

entities.name: Handan
entities.summary: Capital of Zhao, major iron-working and military centre of the Warring States.

entities.name: Ying
entities.summary: Long-lived capital of the southern state of Chu, sacked by Qin in 278 BCE.

entities.name: Jingzhou
entities.summary: Strategic middle-Yangtze fortress city controlling river traffic through the Three Kingdoms era.

entities.name: Qufu
entities.summary: Capital of the state of Lu and birthplace of Confucius; enduring Chinese pilgrimage city.

entities.name: Kaifeng
entities.summary: Northern Song capital, possibly the world's largest city c. 1100, hub of a commercial revolution.

entities.name: Hangzhou
entities.summary: Southern Song capital at the Grand Canal's southern end; Marco Polo's greatest city.

entities.name: Nanjing
entities.summary: Southern capital of six dynasties and first Ming capital, seat of the Yangtze cultural south.

entities.name: Beijing
entities.summary: Mongol Khanbaliq then Ming-Qing imperial capital; northern frontier city turned world capital.

entities.name: Suzhou
entities.summary: Canal city and silk capital, byword for wealth and garden urbanism in late imperial China.

entities.name: Guangzhou
entities.summary: China's principal southern seaport, terminus of the maritime route to India and Arabia.

entities.name: Quanzhou
entities.summary: Song-Yuan world emporium, the greatest port of maritime Asia and rival to Alexandria.

entities.name: Chengdu
entities.summary: Sichuan basin metropolis, birthplace of printed books and the world's first paper money.

entities.name: Dunhuang
entities.summary: Silk Road gateway city whose Mogao cave library preserved medieval Inner Asian Buddhism.

entities.name: Turpan
entities.summary: Oasis city of the Turpan depression, centre of the Uyghur Buddhist and Manichaean kingdom.

entities.name: Gaochang
entities.summary: Walled Silk Road capital of the Uyghur Qocho kingdom, abandoned after the Mongol wars.

entities.name: Jiaohe
entities.summary: Capital of the Jushi kingdom, a whole city carved down into a river-island plateau.

entities.name: Kashgar
entities.summary: Junction of the northern and southern Tarim routes, first great Turkic-Islamic learning centre.

entities.name: Khotan
entities.summary: Silk Road jade and silk kingdom, key conduit of Buddhism and Indic script into China.

entities.name: Loulan
entities.summary: Desert entrepot on the Lop Nur route, abandoned when its river shifted.

entities.name: Niya
entities.summary: Tarim oasis town whose Kharosthi wooden documents record daily Gandharan-influenced life.

entities.name: Kucha
entities.summary: Largest northern Tarim kingdom, home of Kumarajiva and of Central Asian Buddhist art and music.

entities.name: Karashahr
entities.summary: Tocharian-speaking oasis kingdom guarding the road between Turpan and Kucha.

entities.name: Yarkand
entities.summary: Southern Tarim caravan city and later Yarkand khanate capital on the route to Ladakh.

entities.name: Miran
entities.summary: Fort and monastery town whose winged-angel murals show Roman-Gandharan artistic reach.

entities.name: Beshbalik
entities.summary: Tang protectorate seat and Uyghur summer capital north of the Tianshan.

entities.name: Liangzhu
entities.summary: Walled Neolithic city with monumental dams and jade elite, China's earliest state-scale settlement.

entities.name: Sanxingdui
entities.summary: Bronze Age Shu capital whose giant bronze masks reveal a civilisation outside the Shang world.

entities.name: Jinsha
entities.summary: Successor centre to Sanxingdui and ritual heart of the Shu kingdom in the Chengdu plain.

entities.name: Taosi
entities.summary: Huge walled Longshan city with an astronomical observatory, a candidate for legendary Yao's capital.

entities.name: Shimao
entities.summary: Stone-walled 4 sq km citadel on the Ordos loess, the largest known Neolithic city in China.

entities.name: Shijiahe
entities.summary: Great middle-Yangtze walled settlement cluster and rice-farming rival to northern Longshan centres.

entities.name: Banpo
entities.summary: Type site of the Yangshao culture; a planned Neolithic village with a communal great house.

caveats.text: Village rather than city

entities.name: Chengtoushan
entities.summary: Oldest known walled and moated settlement in China, with the earliest excavated paddy fields.

entities.name: Yanshi Shang City
entities.summary: Early Shang garrison capital built beside Erlitou, evidence of dynastic replacement.

entities.name: Ye
entities.summary: Capital of six northern dynasties and template of axial Chinese city planning; razed in 580.

entities.name: Pingcheng
entities.summary: Northern Wei capital where Buddhist cave sculpture and steppe-Chinese synthesis took form.

entities.name: Jinyang
entities.summary: Northern military capital and springboard of the Tang founders' rebellion.

entities.name: Yangzhou
entities.summary: Grand Canal salt and tea entrepot with large Persian and Arab merchant communities.

entities.name: Ningbo
entities.summary: Chief port for trade with Japan and Korea and for Song maritime customs.

entities.name: Xiangyang
entities.summary: Fortress guarding the Han River corridor; its six-year siege decided the Mongol conquest of Song.

entities.name: Chongqing
entities.summary: Upper-Yangtze river city and Song mountain-fortress network hub against the Mongols.

entities.name: Taihe
entities.summary: Capital of the Nanzhao kingdom that defeated Tang armies and dominated upland Southeast Asia.

entities.name: Dali
entities.summary: Capital of the Dali kingdom, Buddhist and horse-trade hub linking Tibet, Burma and China.

entities.name: Kunming
entities.summary: Yuan-era Yunnan capital and node on the Burma road described by Marco Polo.

entities.name: Yinchuan
entities.summary: Capital of the Tangut Western Xia empire with its own script and Buddhist canon.

entities.name: Shangjing Linhuang
entities.summary: Twin-walled Khitan Liao supreme capital, half steppe camp and half Chinese city.

entities.name: Shangjing Huining
entities.summary: First capital of the Jurchen Jin empire, abandoned after the Mongol invasions.

entities.name: Shangdu
entities.summary: Kublai Khan's summer capital, the Xanadu of European legend.

entities.name: Khara-Khoto
entities.summary: Tangut desert garrison city whose buried library was recovered from the sands in 1908.

entities.name: Changsha
entities.summary: Xiang River city, Chu regional centre and later Changsha-kiln ceramics export hub.

entities.name: Fuzhou
entities.summary: Min kingdom capital and shipbuilding port from which Zheng He's fleets partly sailed.

entities.name: Xuzhou
entities.summary: Strategic canal-and-road crossroads fought over in nearly every Chinese civil war.

entities.name: Guilin
entities.summary: Administrative centre of Guangxi controlling the Lingqu canal link between Yangtze and Pearl.

entities.name: Wuwei
entities.summary: Hexi Corridor capital of several Liang states and a major Buddhist translation centre.

entities.name: Zhangye
entities.summary: Hexi Corridor garrison city and later Ganzhou Uyghur capital on the road to Central Asia.

entities.name: Pyongyang
entities.summary: Capital of Gojoseon, Han Lelang commandery and later Goguryeo; oldest continuous Korean city.

entities.name: Gyeongju
entities.summary: Capital of Silla for a millennium and of unified Korea; a city of royal tumuli and Buddhist art.

caveats.text: Founding date 57 BCE is traditional

entities.name: Seoul
entities.summary: Baekje's first capital and Joseon's capital from 1394; enduring political centre of Korea.

entities.name: Kaesong
entities.summary: Capital of Goryeo, source of the name Korea, and centre of celadon and ginseng trade.

entities.name: Buyeo
entities.summary: Last Baekje capital, a planned Buddhist city that transmitted continental culture to Japan.

caveats.text: Modern Buyeo town occupies the site

entities.name: Gongju
entities.summary: Baekje capital after the fall of Hanseong; site of King Muryeong's tomb.

entities.name: Guknaeseong
entities.summary: Goguryeo capital on the Yalu with the great stele of King Gwanggaeto and painted tombs.

entities.name: Gimhae
entities.summary: Leading Gaya confederacy city-state, iron exporter to Japan and the Han commanderies.

caveats.text: Traditional founding of 42 CE

entities.name: Goryeong
entities.summary: Late Gaya paramount centre, absorbed by Silla in 562.

entities.name: Ganghwa
entities.summary: Island refuge capital of Goryeo during the Mongol wars, where the Tripitaka Koreana was carved.

entities.name: Cheorwon
entities.summary: Capital of Gung Ye's short-lived Taebong kingdom, precursor to Goryeo.

entities.name: Jeonju
entities.summary: Capital of Later Baekje and later a Joseon provincial and printing centre.

entities.name: Naju
entities.summary: Southwestern grain and cotton centre and Goryeo naval base.

entities.name: Nara
entities.summary: Japan's first enduring grid capital, modelled on Chang'an, and cradle of state Buddhism.

entities.name: Kyoto
entities.summary: Imperial capital for over a thousand years and the definitive centre of Japanese court culture.

entities.name: Asuka
entities.summary: Seat of the earliest Japanese palace capitals and of Buddhism's introduction to Japan.

entities.name: Fujiwara-kyo
entities.summary: First Chinese-style grid capital of Japan, abandoned after only sixteen years.

entities.name: Nagaoka-kyo
entities.summary: Short-lived capital between Nara and Heian, abandoned amid omens and political murder.

caveats.text: Modern city of the same name now occupies part of the site

entities.name: Kamakura
entities.summary: Seat of Japan's first shogunate and of Zen Buddhism's institutional rise.

entities.name: Naniwa
entities.summary: Ancient imperial port capital and later the commercial kitchen of Japan.

entities.name: Dazaifu
entities.summary: Government seat for Kyushu and Japan's gateway for diplomacy with China and Korea.

entities.name: Hakata
entities.summary: Japan's principal medieval international port and target of the Mongol invasions.

entities.name: Sakai
entities.summary: Self-governing merchant port city, Japan's freest and richest trading town.

entities.name: Hiraizumi
entities.summary: Northern Fujiwara capital, a golden Buddhist city built to rival Kyoto, destroyed in 1189.

caveats.text: Small town remains on the site

entities.name: Otsu
entities.summary: Brief imperial capital of Emperor Tenji on Lake Biwa, lost in the Jinshin War.

caveats.text: Modern Otsu still inhabited

entities.name: Yoshinogari

entities.name: Kabul

entities.name: Kunduz

entities.name: Dahistan

entities.name: Akhsikath

entities.name: Kalyani
entities.summary: Western Chalukya capital and birthplace of the Virashaiva Lingayat movement.

entities.name: Belur

entities.summary: Second Bahmani capital, famed for its madrasa and bidriware metal inlay.

entities.name: Athens

entities.name: Piraeus

entities.name: Eleusis

entities.name: Megara

entities.name: Sparta

entities.name: Corinth

entities.name: Argos

entities.name: Nemea

entities.name: Mantinea

entities.name: Tegea
entities.summary: Leading Arcadian city and site of the great temple of Athena Alea.

entities.name: Messene

entities.name: Olympia

entities.name: Delphi

entities.name: Plataea

entities.summary: Guadalquivir river port, Almohad capital and later gateway to the Atlantic.

entities.name: Corduba
entities.summary: Umayyad caliphal capital, the largest and most learned city in tenth-century Europe.

entities.name: Madinat al-Zahra
entities.summary: Palace city of Abd al-Rahman III, sacked and abandoned within a century.

entities.name: Granada
entities.summary: Nasrid capital and last Muslim state in Iberia, with the Alhambra.

entities.name: Almería
entities.summary: Andalusi silk port and naval arsenal of the caliphate.

entities.name: Murcia
entities.summary: Andalusi foundation on the Segura, a taifa capital and silk centre.

entities.name: Caesaraugusta
entities.summary: Ebro Roman colony and later brilliant taifa court of the Banu Hud.

entities.name: Olisipo
entities.summary: Tagus estuary port, Roman municipium and launch point of Atlantic exploration.

entities.name: Bracara Augusta
entities.summary: Roman capital of Gallaecia and oldest Portuguese archbishopric.

entities.name: Conimbriga
entities.summary: Best-preserved Roman city in Portugal, abandoned after Suevi attacks.

entities.name: Coimbra
entities.summary: Successor to Conimbriga and first capital of the kingdom of Portugal.

entities.name: Porto
entities.summary: Douro-mouth port whose name became Portugal.

entities.name: Évora
entities.summary: Roman and Moorish walled city, later a royal Portuguese residence.

entities.name: Silves
entities.summary: Capital of the Algarve taifa, a wealthy Andalusi river port.

entities.name: Asturica Augusta
entities.summary: Roman gold-administration city of northwest Iberia and Camino waypoint.

entities.name: Lucus Augusti
entities.summary: Roman Galician city with fully intact circuit walls.

entities.name: Legio
entities.summary: Legionary base that became the capital of the kingdom of León.

entities.name: Oviedo
entities.summary: Capital of the Asturian kingdom and cradle of pre-Romanesque architecture.

entities.name: Santiago de Compostela
entities.summary: Shrine of St James and the greatest pilgrimage destination of medieval Europe.

entities.name: Burgos
entities.summary: Castilian royal city and wool-trade capital on the Camino.

entities.name: Valladolid
entities.summary: Castilian court city and administrative centre.

entities.name: Zamora
entities.summary: Duero frontier fortress city with dense Romanesque churches.

entities.name: Badajoz
entities.summary: Capital of a large Andalusi taifa on the Guadiana.

entities.name: Los Millares
entities.summary: Fortified Copper Age town with bastioned walls and tholos cemetery.

entities.name: Valencina de la Concepción
entities.summary: Enormous Copper Age ditched mega-settlement of the Guadalquivir.

entities.name: El Argar
entities.summary: Type site of the Bronze Age Argaric culture with hilltop fortified towns.

entities.name: La Bastida de Totana
entities.summary: Argaric fortified town with the most advanced Bronze Age defences in Europe.

entities.name: Zambujal
entities.summary: Heavily bastioned Copper Age fortified settlement of the Tagus estuary.

entities.name: Citânia de Briteiros
entities.summary: Large Castro-culture hill town of northwest Iberia with paved streets.

entities.name: Ulaca
entities.summary: Vettonian oppidum with a rock-cut sanctuary and sauna.

entities.name: Eridu
entities.summary: Sumerian tradition's first city, seat of Enki and a stacked sequence of temples.

entities.name: Ur
entities.summary: Third-Dynasty imperial capital with a great ziggurat and lavish royal tombs.

entities.name: Lagash
entities.summary: Sumerian city-state whose kings left the earliest detailed records of war and land.

entities.name: Girsu
entities.summary: Religious capital of Lagash state and source of Gudea's statues and the Stele of the Vultures.

entities.name: Nippur
entities.summary: Sacred city of Enlil where Mesopotamian kingship was legitimised, never an imperial capital.

entities.name: Kish
entities.summary: First city to hold kingship after the flood in Sumerian tradition; Sargon's launching point.

entities.name: Umma
entities.summary: Sumerian rival of Lagash in the earliest recorded border war.

entities.name: Shuruppak
entities.summary: Home of the flood hero Ziusudra and of the earliest wisdom instructions.

entities.name: Isin
entities.summary: Successor dynasty to Ur that claimed Sumerian kingship and rebuilt its cult centres.

entities.name: Larsa
entities.summary: Sun-god city and dominant southern power until Hammurabi absorbed it.

entities.name: Sippar
entities.summary: Cult city of Shamash with a temple archive central to Babylonian law and scholarship.

entities.name: Borsippa
entities.summary: Nabu's city and Babylon's twin, home to a huge unfinished ziggurat and scribal schools.

entities.name: Babylon
entities.summary: Hammurabi's law city and Nebuchadnezzar's imperial capital, the archetype of the ancient metropolis.

entities.name: Akkad
entities.summary: Capital of the world's first territorial empire, and still not securely located.

caveats.text: Site unidentified; dates from textual references only.

entities.name: Eshnunna
entities.summary: Diyala kingdom whose law code predates Hammurabi's.

entities.name: Adab
entities.summary: Early Sumerian city-state of the goddess Ninhursag.

entities.name: Kutha
entities.summary: Cult city of the underworld god Nergal.

entities.name: Dilbat
entities.summary: Babylonian city of the god Urash with rich land-sale archives.

entities.name: Marad
entities.summary: Sumerian city founded by Naram-Sin's line for the god Lugal-Marada.

entities.name: Zabalam
entities.summary: Early cult centre of Inanna listed among the oldest Sumerian towns.

entities.name: Bad-tibira
entities.summary: One of the five antediluvian cities of the Sumerian King List.

entities.name: Larak
entities.summary: Antediluvian city of the king list, location still disputed.

caveats.text: Location uncertain.

entities.name: Akshak
entities.summary: Northern Sumerian city-state that briefly held hegemony.

entities.name: Mashkan-shapir
entities.summary: Second city of Larsa, abandoned intact and so a rare full Old Babylonian town plan.

entities.name: Tell al-Ubaid
entities.summary: Type-site of the Ubaid culture that seeded southern Mesopotamian urbanism.

entities.name: Tell es-Sawwan
entities.summary: Walled Samarran village showing the first irrigation farming on the Tigris; not a city.

entities.name: Jarmo
entities.summary: Early Neolithic farming village, a founding site of Zagros agriculture; not a city.

entities.name: Tell Samarra (Samarran culture)
entities.summary: Type-site of painted-ware culture that pioneered canal irrigation; a village, not a city.

entities.name: Choga Mami
entities.summary: Samarran village with the earliest known irrigation canals; not a city.

entities.name: Tepe Gawra
entities.summary: Northern Mesopotamian mound documenting the rise of temples and seals before writing.

entities.name: Tell Brak
entities.summary: One of the oldest cities anywhere, with the Eye Temple and a Hurrian-Akkadian palace.

entities.name: Tell Leilan
entities.summary: Shamshi-Adad's Upper Mesopotamian capital, abandoned after a drought collapse.

entities.name: Urkesh
entities.summary: Hurrian royal city with the earliest Hurrian inscriptions and a necromantic pit.

entities.name: Tell Halaf
entities.summary: Type-site of Halaf painted pottery, later an Aramaean capital of carved orthostats.

entities.name: Mari
entities.summary: Euphrates trade capital whose palace archive of 25,000 tablets illuminates the age of Hammurabi.

entities.name: Terqa
entities.summary: Middle Euphrates town of Dagan's temple, closely tied to Mari.

entities.name: Emar
entities.summary: Hittite-period Euphrates trading city with large private legal and ritual archives.

entities.name: Tuttul
entities.summary: Bronze Age city at the Balikh confluence, a cult seat of Dagan.

entities.name: Habuba Kabira
entities.summary: Planned Uruk colony far up the Euphrates, evidence of the first urban expansion.

entities.name: Assur
entities.summary: Religious heart and first capital of Assyria, home of the god Ashur.

entities.name: Nineveh
entities.summary: Sennacherib's vast capital and site of Ashurbanipal's library.

entities.name: Kalhu
entities.summary: Ashurnasirpal II's capital, palace of colossal lamassu and the Black Obelisk.

entities.name: Dur-Sharrukin
entities.summary: Sargon II's purpose-built capital, abandoned almost immediately after his death.

entities.name: Kar-Tukulti-Ninurta
entities.summary: Short-lived Middle Assyrian royal city opposite Assur, abandoned on its founder's murder.

entities.name: Imgur-Enlil
entities.summary: Assyrian town whose palace gates carry the finest surviving bronze narrative reliefs.

entities.name: Arrapha
entities.summary: Ancient Hurrian-Assyrian centre continuously occupied as modern Kirkuk.

entities.name: Nuzi
entities.summary: Hurrian provincial town whose family archives are our best window on Mitanni-era society.

entities.name: Arbela
entities.summary: Ishtar cult city and one of the longest continuously inhabited citadels on earth.

entities.name: Dur-Kurigalzu
entities.summary: Kassite royal capital with a towering ziggurat, founded and abandoned with its dynasty.

entities.name: Opis
entities.summary: Tigris crossing town where Cyrus defeated the Babylonians in 539 BCE.

entities.name: Der
entities.summary: Frontier city of the god Ishtaran, buffer between Babylonia and Elam.

entities.name: Hatra
entities.summary: Fortified Parthian-era caravan and temple city that twice repulsed Rome before Sasanian destruction.

entities.name: Seleucia on the Tigris
entities.summary: Seleucid eastern capital and one of the largest cities of the Hellenistic world.

entities.name: Ctesiphon
entities.summary: Parthian and Sasanian imperial capital, whose brick Taq Kasra vault still stands.

entities.name: Veh-Ardashir
entities.summary: Sasanian round city facing Ctesiphon, a major Christian and Jewish centre.

entities.name: Charax Spasinou
entities.summary: Capital of Characene and the head of the Gulf sea route to India.

entities.name: Baghdad
entities.summary: Abbasid round city that became the largest city in the world and the hub of Islamic science.

entities.name: Samarra
entities.summary: Vast Abbasid capital for half a century, with the spiral Malwiya minaret.

entities.name: Kufa
entities.summary: Garrison city that became a centre of Arabic grammar, Shi'i politics and early Islamic law.

entities.name: Basra
entities.summary: Garrison port that grew into the Abbasid world's gateway to the Indian Ocean.

entities.name: Wasit
entities.summary: Umayyad administrative city midway on the Tigris, abandoned as the river shifted.

entities.name: Al-Anbar
entities.summary: Sasanian then early Abbasid Euphrates city, briefly capital before Baghdad.

entities.name: Mosul
entities.summary: Tigris city that inherited Nineveh's role and anchored the Zangid and Atabeg states.

entities.name: Tikrit
entities.summary: Fortress town on the Tigris, a Syriac Christian seat and Saladin's birthplace.

entities.name: Nisibis
entities.summary: Roman-Persian frontier fortress and seat of the great School of the Persians.

entities.name: Edessa
entities.summary: Cradle of Syriac Christianity and literature, capital of Osrhoene.

entities.name: Harran
entities.summary: Moon-god city of Sin that kept its pagan cult and astronomy into Islamic times.

entities.name: Carchemish
entities.summary: Hittite viceregal seat that survived as the leading Neo-Hittite kingdom.

entities.name: Raqqa
entities.summary: Harun al-Rashid's residence and a major Abbasid ceramic and garrison city.

entities.name: Jericho
entities.summary: Earliest known walled settlement, with a stone tower a thousand years before farming villages spread.

entities.name: Beidha
entities.summary: Pre-Pottery Neolithic village showing the shift from round to rectangular houses; not a city.

entities.name: Damascus
entities.summary: Aramaean royal city and Umayyad imperial capital, plausibly the oldest continuously inhabited city.

entities.name: Aleppo
entities.summary: Capital of Yamhad and later northern Syria's great caravan metropolis.

entities.name: Ebla
entities.summary: Early Syrian kingdom whose 17,000-tablet archive rewrote the map of third-millennium politics.

entities.name: Alalakh
entities.summary: Palace city of the Amuq plain, a hinge between Anatolia, Syria and the Aegean.

entities.name: Qatna
entities.summary: Bronze Age kingdom whose intact royal tomb held gold, ivory and ancestor cult remains.

entities.name: Kadesh
entities.summary: Orontes stronghold where Ramesses II and Muwatalli fought the best-documented Bronze Age battle.

entities.name: Hamath
entities.summary: Neo-Hittite and Aramaean royal city on the Orontes, later famed for its norias.

entities.name: Emesa
entities.summary: Sun-god city that gave Rome the emperor Elagabalus and later anchored Syrian trade routes.

entities.name: Palmyra
entities.summary: Desert caravan metropolis that under Zenobia briefly ruled the Roman East.

entities.name: Dura-Europos
entities.summary: Euphrates garrison town preserving the earliest church and synagogue paintings, sealed by siege.

entities.name: Apamea
entities.summary: Seleucid military capital with a two-kilometre colonnaded avenue.

entities.name: Antioch
entities.summary: Seleucid capital and one of the four great cities of the Roman world, cradle of Christian mission.

entities.name: Seleucia Pieria
entities.summary: Antioch's port, with a rock-cut tunnel dug to keep the harbour clear.

entities.name: Laodicea ad Mare
entities.summary: Seleucid port that became coastal Syria's main outlet.

entities.name: Ugarit
entities.summary: Canaanite port whose alphabetic cuneiform archives preserved West Semitic myth; destroyed in the Bronze Age collapse.

entities.name: Berytus
entities.summary: Phoenician port that became the Roman East's leading school of law.

entities.name: Tripoli
entities.summary: Phoenician federal port, later a Crusader county and Mamluk centre of paper and sugar.

entities.name: Heliopolis (Baalbek)
entities.summary: Sanctuary city of Jupiter Heliopolitanus with the largest temple stones ever quarried.

entities.name: Sumur
entities.summary: Egyptian administrative base on the Canaanite coast, prominent in the Amarna letters.

entities.name: Akko
entities.summary: Great natural harbour, Canaanite port and capital of the later Crusader kingdom.

entities.name: Dor
entities.summary: Sikil and Phoenician harbour town controlling the Carmel coast.

entities.name: Megiddo
entities.summary: Fortress guarding the Via Maris pass, fought over so often it named the apocalypse.

entities.name: Hazor
entities.summary: The largest Canaanite city in the southern Levant, with a huge lower town and archive.

entities.name: Beth Shean
entities.summary: Continuously occupied mound turned Decapolis city at the Jordan-Jezreel crossroads.

entities.name: Dan
entities.summary: Israelite cult city with a mudbrick gate arch and the earliest extrabiblical mention of David.

entities.name: Shechem
entities.summary: Hill-country covenant city and first Israelite northern capital.

entities.name: Samaria
entities.summary: Purpose-built capital of the kingdom of Israel, famed for its ivories.

entities.name: Shiloh
entities.summary: Pre-monarchic Israelite sanctuary that housed the Ark before Jerusalem.

entities.name: Tirzah
entities.summary: Early capital of the northern Israelite kingdom before Samaria.

entities.name: Jerusalem
entities.summary: Temple city sacred to three faiths and the political heart of Judah.

entities.name: Gezer
entities.summary: Fortified gateway between the coast and the hills, subject of the oldest Hebrew calendar text.

entities.name: Lachish
entities.summary: Judah's second city, whose siege Sennacherib carved in relief at Nineveh.

entities.name: Gath
entities.summary: Largest Philistine city in its heyday, Goliath's traditional home.

entities.name: Ekron
entities.summary: Philistine pentapolis city and an industrial-scale olive oil producer.

entities.name: Ashdod
entities.summary: Philistine city and port, later a Hellenistic and Islamic coastal town.

entities.name: Ashkelon
entities.summary: Great Canaanite-Philistine seaport, razed by the Mamluks to deny it to Crusaders.

entities.name: Gaza
entities.summary: Terminus of the incense road and Egypt's gateway to the Levant for five millennia.

entities.name: Jaffa
entities.summary: Ancient harbour serving the Judaean hinterland, mentioned in Egyptian and biblical sources.

entities.name: Beersheba
entities.summary: Planned Iron Age Negev town with a horned altar and a great water system.

entities.name: Arad
entities.summary: Early Bronze desert city and later Judahite fort with a sanctuary and Hebrew ostraca.

entities.name: Ein Gedi
entities.summary: Dead Sea oasis town making balsam perfume, with a mosaic synagogue.

entities.name: Masada
entities.summary: Herodian desert palace-fortress and site of the Zealots' last stand; a fortress, not a city.

entities.name: Qumran
entities.summary: Sectarian settlement linked to the Dead Sea Scrolls; a community compound, not a city.

entities.name: Caesarea Maritima
entities.summary: Herod's artificial-harbour city, Roman capital of Judaea and a Christian scholarly centre.

entities.name: Tiberias
entities.summary: Rabbinic capital where the Jerusalem Talmud and Masoretic text were codified.

entities.name: Sepphoris
entities.summary: Galilean city where the Mishnah was redacted, rich in mosaics.

entities.name: Gerasa
entities.summary: Best-preserved Decapolis city, with oval forum and colonnaded cardo.

entities.name: Rabbath Ammon
entities.summary: Ammonite royal capital, later a Decapolis city and modern Jordan's capital.

entities.name: Bosra
entities.summary: Nabataean northern capital, then capital of Roman Arabia and an early Arab caravan stop.

entities.name: Gadara
entities.summary: Decapolis hill city known for its philosophers and poets.

entities.name: Heshbon
entities.summary: Moabite-Ammonite frontier town on the King's Highway.

entities.name: Dibon
entities.summary: Moabite capital of King Mesha, whose stele is the longest Moabite text.

entities.name: Kir-Hareseth
entities.summary: Moabite stronghold, later a great Crusader and Mamluk castle town.

entities.name: Petra
entities.summary: Nabataean rock-cut capital that taxed the incense trade and mastered desert hydraulics.

entities.name: Hegra
entities.summary: Nabataean southern city of monumental rock tombs on the incense road.

entities.name: Oboda
entities.summary: Nabataean then Byzantine Negev caravan town with terraced desert farming.

entities.name: Timna
entities.summary: Industrial copper-smelting camp complex, not a city.

entities.name: Ayla
entities.summary: Red Sea head-of-gulf port linking the Levant to Arabia and Africa.

entities.name: Karahan Tepe
entities.summary: Contemporary of Göbekli Tepe with carved pillars and head sculptures; ceremonial, not a city.

entities.name: Nevalı Çori
entities.summary: Early Neolithic village with cult building and terrazzo floors; not a city.

entities.name: Çayönü
entities.summary: Neolithic village documenting early domestication and skull cults; not a city.

entities.name: Aşıklı Höyük
entities.summary: Central Anatolia's earliest dense village, precursor to Çatalhöyük; not a city.

entities.name: Hacılar
entities.summary: Neolithic-Chalcolithic village known for fine painted pottery and figurines; not a city.

entities.name: Can Hasan
entities.summary: Konya plain Neolithic mound with early copper use; not a city.

entities.name: Yumuktepe
entities.summary: Long-lived Cilician mound with one of the earliest fortified settlements.

entities.name: Arslantepe
entities.summary: Site of the world's earliest known palace and earliest swords, later Neo-Hittite Melid.

entities.name: Kanesh
entities.summary: Assyrian merchant colony whose letters document the first documented long-distance trade network.

entities.name: Acemhöyük
entities.summary: Old Assyrian-period palace town with ivories, possibly the Purushanda of legend.

entities.name: Alacahöyük
entities.summary: Early Bronze royal tombs with sun-disc standards, later a Hittite town.

entities.name: Kussara
entities.summary: Original royal seat of the Hittite dynasty; site not yet identified.

caveats.text: Location unknown.

entities.name: Sarissa
entities.summary: Planned Hittite provincial city with temple archives, founded and abandoned inside the empire's life.

entities.name: Yazılıkaya
entities.summary: Rock sanctuary of the Hittite pantheon beside Hattusa; ceremonial, not a city.

entities.name: Beycesultan
entities.summary: Western Anatolian palace town of the Arzawa sphere.

entities.name: Gordion
entities.summary: Phrygian capital of Midas with monumental tumulus burials and early alphabetic texts.

entities.name: Sardis
entities.summary: Lydian capital of Croesus where coinage was invented, later a Roman provincial city.

entities.name: Miletus
entities.summary: Ionian trading power, mother of dozens of colonies and birthplace of Greek philosophy.

entities.name: Ephesus
entities.summary: Great Ionian port of the Artemision, later Roman Asia's capital and an early Christian centre.

entities.name: Priene
entities.summary: Model Hellenistic grid city on terraces above the Maeander.

entities.name: Didyma
entities.summary: Oracle sanctuary of Apollo attached to Miletus; ceremonial, not a city.

entities.name: Halicarnassus
entities.summary: Carian capital of Mausolus and site of the Mausoleum, one of the seven wonders.

entities.name: Cnidus
entities.summary: Dorian port city known for its Aphrodite statue and its medical school.

entities.name: Smyrna
entities.summary: Aegean port with a claim on Homer, refounded by Alexander's successors as a great Roman city.

entities.name: Phocaea
entities.summary: Ionian seafaring city that founded Massalia and much of the western Greek coast.

entities.name: Pergamon
entities.summary: Attalid capital of the Great Altar and a library rivalling Alexandria's.

entities.name: Assos
entities.summary: Aeolian acropolis city where Aristotle taught.

entities.name: Aphrodisias
entities.summary: Marble-carving city of Asia Minor with a famous sculpture school and stadium.

entities.name: Hierapolis
entities.summary: Thermal spa and healing city abandoned after an earthquake.

entities.name: Laodicea ad Lycum
entities.summary: Wealthy banking and wool city, one of the seven churches of Revelation.

entities.name: Xanthos
entities.summary: Chief city of Lycia, famed for pillar tombs and its own written language.

entities.name: Perge
entities.summary: Pamphylian city of colonnaded streets and monumental nymphaeum.

entities.name: Side
entities.summary: Pamphylian port that grew rich as a Cilician pirate market and grain harbour.

entities.name: Attaleia
entities.summary: Attalid foundation that became southern Anatolia's principal harbour.

entities.name: Tarsus
entities.summary: Cilician capital, a great school city and Paul's birthplace.

entities.name: Karatepe
entities.summary: Neo-Hittite hilltop citadel with a bilingual inscription that cracked hieroglyphic Luwian.

entities.name: Sam'al
entities.summary: Aramaean-Luwian royal city with a circular wall and Aramaic funerary stelae.

entities.name: Iconium
entities.summary: Ancient Phrygian town that became the Seljuk sultanate's capital and Rumi's home.

entities.name: Ancyra
entities.summary: Galatian and Roman provincial capital, keeper of Augustus's own testament in stone.

entities.name: Pessinus
entities.summary: Cult city of Cybele whose sacred stone was carried to Rome.

entities.name: Nicaea
entities.summary: Site of the first ecumenical council and later a Byzantine capital in exile.

entities.name: Nicomedia
entities.summary: Diocletian's eastern imperial capital before Constantinople.

entities.name: Cyzicus
entities.summary: Wealthy Propontis port on an isthmus, ruined by earthquakes.

entities.name: Chalcedon
entities.summary: Bosphorus city that hosted the council defining Christian orthodoxy.

entities.name: Sinope
entities.summary: Best harbour on the Black Sea's south coast and Mithridates' birthplace.

entities.name: Amisos
entities.summary: Pontic port exporting Anatolian metals and timber.

entities.name: Trapezus
entities.summary: Black Sea silk-route terminus and capital of the last Byzantine successor empire.

entities.name: Amaseia
entities.summary: Pontic royal capital and birthplace of the geographer Strabo.

entities.name: Caesarea Mazaca
entities.summary: Cappadocian royal capital, later home of Basil the Great.

entities.name: Melitene
entities.summary: Euphrates frontier legionary city guarding the Anatolian passes.

entities.name: Amida
entities.summary: Black-basalt walled Tigris fortress city contested by Rome, Persia and Islam.

entities.name: Tushpa
entities.summary: Rock-citadel capital of Urartu with royal cuneiform annals and vast canal works.

entities.name: Ayanis
entities.summary: Urartian fortress-city built by Rusa II and destroyed within a generation.

entities.name: Erebuni
entities.summary: Urartian fortress founded in 782 BCE from which Yerevan claims descent.

entities.name: Teishebaini
entities.summary: Last great Urartian administrative citadel, burned by Scythians or Medes.

entities.name: Argishtihinili
entities.summary: Urartian twin-citadel city that later became an Armenian royal seat.

entities.name: Artaxata
entities.summary: Hellenistic Armenian capital said to have been laid out on Hannibal's advice.

entities.name: Tigranocerta
entities.summary: Tigranes the Great's showpiece capital, sacked by Lucullus soon after founding.

entities.name: Dvin
entities.summary: Armenian catholicosate and caravan capital, destroyed by the Mongols.

entities.name: Ani
entities.summary: Bagratid Armenian capital of a thousand and one churches, abandoned after Mongol and earthquake damage.

entities.name: Mtskheta
entities.summary: Ancient Iberian capital where Georgia adopted Christianity.

entities.name: Tbilisi
entities.summary: Kura crossing capital of Georgia and a Silk Road meeting point.

entities.name: Derbent
entities.summary: Sasanian wall-and-gate city sealing the Caspian pass between Europe and Asia.

entities.name: Barda
entities.summary: Caucasian Albanian and then Islamic capital of Arran.

entities.name: Shamakhi
entities.summary: Shirvanshah capital and silk-trade centre on the Caspian route.

entities.name: Chogha Mish
entities.summary: Large proto-Elamite centre of the Susiana plain preceding Susa's rise.

entities.name: Anshan
entities.summary: Highland Elamite capital and the title Cyrus's ancestors claimed.

entities.name: Kabnak
entities.summary: Middle Elamite royal centre with vaulted tombs and a craft quarter.

entities.name: Tepe Sialk
entities.summary: Long-lived plateau mound with a ziggurat-like platform and early metallurgy.

entities.name: Shahr-e Sukhteh
entities.summary: Large eastern Iranian city with craft workshops, an artificial eye and early animation vessel.

entities.name: Konar Sandal
entities.summary: Monumental centre of the Halil Rud culture, a possible independent Bronze Age civilisation.

entities.name: Tepe Yahya
entities.summary: Chlorite-working town linking Mesopotamia, Elam and the Indus.

entities.name: Tepe Hissar
entities.summary: Northern Iranian craft and metal town on the route to Central Asia.

entities.name: Godin Tepe
entities.summary: Zagros citadel that yielded the earliest chemical evidence for wine and beer.

entities.name: Hasanlu
entities.summary: Fortified Iron Age citadel violently destroyed, source of the famous gold bowl.

entities.name: Tepe Nush-i Jan
entities.summary: Median temple-and-fort complex, the best evidence for Median architecture.

entities.name: Ecbatana
entities.summary: Median capital and Achaemenid summer residence beneath modern Hamadan.

entities.name: Pasargadae
entities.summary: Cyrus the Great's first Persian capital, garden palace complex and his tomb.

entities.name: Persepolis
entities.summary: Achaemenid ceremonial capital of the Apadana reliefs, burned by Alexander.

entities.name: Istakhr
entities.summary: Sasanian-era Fars capital and early Islamic city near Persepolis, later eclipsed by Shiraz.

entities.name: Gor
entities.summary: Ardashir I's perfectly circular Sasanian foundation city.

entities.name: Bishapur
entities.summary: Shapur I's victory city with Roman-influenced mosaics and rock reliefs.

entities.name: Gundeshapur
entities.summary: Sasanian city whose academy and hospital transmitted Greek and Indian medicine to Islam.

entities.name: Shiraz
entities.summary: Islamic-era Fars capital of poets, gardens and wine.

entities.name: Siraf
entities.summary: Gulf port that dominated Abbasid trade with India and China until an earthquake ruined it.

entities.name: Hormuz
entities.summary: Strait-controlling emporium that moved to Jarun island and taxed all Gulf shipping.

entities.name: Isfahan
entities.summary: Seljuk capital with a great congregational mosque, later Safavid Iran's showpiece.

entities.name: Ray
entities.summary: One of the plateau's greatest ancient cities, ruined by the Mongols and absorbed by Tehran.

entities.name: Qom
entities.summary: Shrine city of Fatima Masumeh and a centre of Shi'i learning.

entities.name: Qazvin
entities.summary: Sasanian fortress town, later a frontier city against the Daylamites and Assassins.

entities.name: Tabriz
entities.summary: Ilkhanid capital and the greatest Silk Road market of the Mongol west.

entities.name: Ardabil
entities.summary: Azerbaijani caravan city and cradle of the Safavid order.

entities.name: Yazd
entities.summary: Desert silk city of wind-catchers and a stronghold of Zoroastrianism.

entities.name: Kashan
entities.summary: Oasis town of lustre ceramics and tiles, next to Neolithic Sialk.

entities.name: Kerman
entities.summary: Sasanian foundation controlling the southeast trade route to India.

entities.name: Nishapur
entities.summary: Sasanian foundation that became Khorasan's greatest city until the Mongols destroyed it.

entities.name: Tus
entities.summary: Khorasani city of Firdawsi and al-Ghazali, ruined by Timurid warfare.

entities.name: Gorgan
entities.summary: Caspian gateway city behind the great Sasanian Gorgan Wall.

entities.name: Ahvaz
entities.summary: Sasanian sugar and irrigation city on the Karun.

entities.name: Shushtar
entities.summary: City built around a monumental Sasanian hydraulic system of canals and mills.

entities.name: Kermanshah
entities.summary: Zagros road city beside Darius's Bisotun inscription.

entities.name: Shiz
entities.summary: Sasanian fire-temple sanctuary city around a volcanic lake; largely ceremonial.

entities.name: Gurganj
entities.summary: Khwarazmian capital destroyed by the Mongols and abandoned when the Amu Darya shifted.

entities.name: Hecatompylos
entities.summary: Early Parthian capital on the Khorasan road.

entities.name: Mecca
entities.summary: Sanctuary and caravan town that became Islam's holiest city and pilgrimage focus.

entities.name: Medina
entities.summary: Oasis town that hosted Muhammad's community and became the first Islamic capital.

entities.name: Ta'if
entities.summary: Highland fruit-growing town and summer refuge for Mecca's elite.

entities.name: Khaybar
entities.summary: Fortified oasis of date palms and Jewish settlement in the Hijaz.

entities.name: Jeddah
entities.summary: Red Sea port of Mecca and the main gateway for pilgrims.

entities.name: Tayma
entities.summary: Walled north Arabian oasis where Nabonidus of Babylon lived in self-exile.

entities.name: Dedan
entities.summary: Capital of the Dedanite and Lihyanite kingdoms on the incense road.

entities.name: Dumat al-Jandal
entities.summary: Oasis stronghold of the Qedarite Arabs, a key desert junction.

entities.name: Qaryat al-Faw
entities.summary: Caravan city and Kindah capital at the mouth of the Wadi al-Dawasir pass.

entities.name: Thaj
