entities.summary: Walled Hellenistic-era eastern Arabian city, possibly the Gerrha of Greek sources.

entities.name: Gerrha
entities.summary: Fabulously rich Gulf entrepôt of the incense trade, its site still debated.

caveats.text: Identification with Thaj or al-Uqayr disputed.

entities.name: Qal'at al-Bahrain
entities.summary: Capital of Dilmun, the Gulf trade hub between Mesopotamia and the Indus.

entities.name: Failaka
entities.summary: Dilmun then Seleucid island settlement guarding the head of the Gulf.

entities.name: Ed-Dur
entities.summary: Large Gulf coastal trading town of the Parthian era.

entities.name: Mleiha
entities.summary: Inland southeast Arabian centre with monumental tombs and its own coinage.

entities.name: Sohar
entities.summary: Oman's copper and Indian Ocean trading port, Sindbad's traditional home.

entities.name: Julfar
entities.summary: Pearl and Indian Ocean port of the lower Gulf, base of the navigator Ibn Majid.

entities.name: Sumhuram
entities.summary: Hadrami frankincense port shipping Dhofar resin to Rome and India.

entities.name: Ubar
entities.summary: Caravan waterhole and fort of the incense route, identified with legendary Iram.

caveats.text: Identification with legendary Ubar/Iram is speculative.

entities.name: Marib
entities.summary: Sabaean capital whose great dam irrigated a desert kingdom for over a millennium.

entities.name: Sirwah
entities.summary: Early Sabaean centre with the Karib'il Watar inscription and oval temple.

entities.name: Shabwa
entities.summary: Hadramawt capital where all frankincense had to be taxed before export.

entities.name: Qana
entities.summary: Hadrami port of the Periplus shipping incense to Egypt and India.

entities.name: Najran
entities.summary: Caravan oasis and Christian centre martyred under the Himyarite king Dhu Nuwas.

entities.name: Zafar
entities.summary: Highland capital of Himyar, which unified Yemen and adopted monotheism.

entities.name: Sana'a
entities.summary: Highland capital of tower houses, seat of Yemeni states from Himyar onward.

entities.name: Aden
entities.summary: Volcanic-crater harbour controlling the Red Sea entrance for Indian Ocean trade.

entities.name: Zabid
entities.summary: Tihama city whose university spread Islamic learning and algebra in Yemen.

entities.name: Shibam
entities.summary: Mudbrick high-rise city, the earliest example of vertical urban planning.

entities.name: Tarim
entities.summary: Hadrami centre of Sufi scholarship that seeded Islam across the Indian Ocean.

entities.name: Naqada
entities.summary: Predynastic centre that named the culture out of which pharaonic Egypt emerged.

entities.name: Abydos
entities.summary: Royal cemetery of Egypt's first kings and the great cult centre of Osiris.

entities.name: Thinis
entities.summary: Traditional home of the Thinite kings who unified Egypt; site not securely located.

entities.name: Buto
entities.summary: Predynastic Lower Egyptian capital of the cobra goddess Wadjet.

entities.name: Sais
entities.summary: Delta cult city of Neith and capital of the 26th Dynasty renaissance.

entities.name: Memphis
entities.summary: Egypt's founding capital at the Delta apex, administrative heart for three millennia.

entities.name: Heit el-Ghurab
entities.summary: Barracks and bakery town that housed pyramid builders; a support settlement, not a city.

entities.name: Saqqara
entities.summary: Memphis's vast necropolis with the first pyramid; a cemetery complex, not a city.

entities.name: Heliopolis
entities.summary: Solar theology's home city, its priesthood shaping Egyptian religion and obelisks.

entities.name: Herakleopolis Magna
entities.summary: Rival capital to Thebes during Egypt's first collapse.

entities.name: Hermopolis Magna
entities.summary: Cult city of Thoth and of the Ogdoad creation myth.

entities.name: Akhetaten
entities.summary: Akhenaten's purpose-built monotheist capital, occupied barely two decades.

entities.name: Lycopolis
entities.summary: Upper Egyptian nome capital and later a major Coptic centre.

entities.name: Akhmim
entities.summary: Cult city of Min and a famous weaving town into Islamic times.

entities.name: Dendera
entities.summary: Temple city of Hathor with a near-complete Ptolemaic temple and zodiac ceiling.

entities.name: Coptos
entities.summary: Desert-road hub linking the Nile to Red Sea ports and the Eastern Desert quarries.

entities.name: Deir el-Medina
entities.summary: Village of the tomb-builders whose records reveal daily life and the first strike; not a city.

entities.name: Elkab
entities.summary: Walled cult city of the vulture goddess Nekhbet, twin of Hierakonpolis.

entities.name: Edfu
entities.summary: Home of Egypt's best-preserved temple, dedicated to Horus.

entities.name: Esna
entities.summary: Nile temple town of the god Khnum.

entities.name: Ombos
entities.summary: Double temple town shared between Sobek and Horus.

entities.name: Elephantine
entities.summary: Island fortress and trade gateway to Nubia, home to a Jewish garrison and its Aramaic papyri.

entities.name: Syene
entities.summary: Granite quarry city where Eratosthenes measured the earth.

entities.name: Avaris
entities.summary: Hyksos capital in the eastern Delta, with Levantine and Aegean-style palaces.

entities.name: Pi-Ramesses
entities.summary: Ramesses II's Delta capital and chariot-manufacturing city, abandoned as the branch silted.

entities.name: Tanis
entities.summary: Delta capital built from Pi-Ramesses' stones, with intact silver royal burials.

entities.name: Bubastis
entities.summary: Cat-goddess festival city and Libyan-dynasty capital.

entities.name: Mendes
entities.summary: Delta ram-cult city and briefly a Late Period capital.

entities.name: Athribis
entities.summary: Delta nome capital, birthplace of a 30th Dynasty line.

entities.name: Leontopolis
entities.summary: Delta lion-cult city and seat of a rival Libyan dynasty.

entities.name: Naukratis
entities.summary: Greek treaty port in the Delta, Egypt's controlled window on Aegean trade.

entities.name: Thonis-Heracleion
entities.summary: Egypt's Mediterranean customs port, now submerged after subsidence.

entities.name: Canopus
entities.summary: Pleasure and temple city at the Nile's western mouth, partly underwater.

entities.name: Pelusium
entities.summary: Fortress port guarding Egypt's eastern gate, silted up and abandoned.

entities.name: Alexandria
entities.summary: Ptolemaic capital of the Library, Lighthouse and Mediterranean learning.

entities.name: Crocodilopolis
entities.summary: Faiyum capital at the centre of Egypt's greatest reclamation scheme.

entities.name: Kahun
entities.summary: Planned pyramid-workers' town, the best-preserved Middle Kingdom settlement plan; not a city.

entities.name: Oxyrhynchus
entities.summary: Provincial capital whose rubbish mounds yielded the largest ancient papyrus haul.

entities.name: Antinoöpolis
entities.summary: Hadrian's Greek foundation commemorating Antinous's drowning.

entities.name: Kellis
entities.summary: Desert oasis town preserving Manichaean and Christian papyri, abandoned to the sand.

entities.name: Siwa
entities.summary: Oracle oasis of Amun consulted by Alexander.

entities.name: Bahariya
entities.summary: Wine-producing oasis with a vast Greco-Roman gilded-mummy cemetery.

entities.name: Berenike Troglodytica
entities.summary: Ptolemaic elephant and Roman Indian Ocean port on the Red Sea.

entities.name: Myos Hormos
entities.summary: Chief Roman Red Sea harbour for the Indian trade.

entities.name: Fustat
entities.summary: Arab garrison city that became Egypt's Islamic capital and glass-and-ceramic hub, absorbed into Cairo.

entities.name: Cairo
entities.summary: Fatimid royal foundation that grew into the largest city of the medieval Islamic world.

entities.name: Al-Askar and Al-Qata'i
entities.summary: Successive Abbasid and Tulunid palace-cities north of Fustat, later merged into Cairo.

entities.name: Damietta
entities.summary: Delta port and Crusader target controlling the eastern Nile mouth.

entities.name: Rosetta
entities.summary: Western Nile mouth port, later namesake of the trilingual stone.

entities.name: Qus
entities.summary: Mamluk-era Nile city and staging point for the Red Sea spice route.

entities.name: Aydhab
entities.summary: Red Sea pilgrim and spice port, destroyed by the Mamluks.

entities.name: Kerma
entities.summary: First Nubian kingdom's capital, with the huge mudbrick Western Deffufa.

entities.name: Buhen
entities.summary: Egyptian fortress town at the second cataract, now under Lake Nasser.

entities.name: Mirgissa
entities.summary: Middle Kingdom fortress and trans-shipment depot with a boat slipway; a fort, not a city.

entities.name: Semna
entities.summary: Frontier fortress controlling Nubian trade and Nile levels; a fort, not a city.

entities.name: Sai
entities.summary: Egyptian colonial town on a Nile island, later a Christian Nubian centre.

entities.name: Sesebi
entities.summary: Planned Egyptian walled colonial town in Nubia.

entities.name: Napata
entities.summary: Kushite religious capital under Jebel Barkal, whence the 25th Dynasty conquered Egypt.

entities.name: Nuri
entities.summary: Kushite royal pyramid cemetery near Napata; a necropolis, not a city.

entities.name: Kawa
entities.summary: Kushite temple town of Amun, rebuilt by Taharqa.

entities.name: Meroë
entities.summary: Iron-smelting Kushite capital with hundreds of pyramids and its own Meroitic script.

entities.name: Naqa
entities.summary: Meroitic temple city of Amun and the lion god Apedemak.

entities.name: Musawwarat es-Sufra
entities.summary: Meroitic pilgrimage complex of the Great Enclosure; ceremonial, not a city.

entities.name: Qasr Ibrim
entities.summary: Cliff fortress-town, the only major Nubian site above the reservoir, with vast preserved documents.

entities.name: Faras
entities.summary: Capital of Christian Nobadia, whose cathedral frescoes were rescued before flooding.

entities.name: Old Dongola
entities.summary: Capital of Christian Makuria that held off Arab armies for six centuries.

entities.name: Soba
entities.summary: Capital of the Christian Nubian kingdom of Alwa on the Blue Nile.

entities.name: Yeha
entities.summary: Capital of the D'mt polity with a monumental Sabaean-style temple, Ethiopia's oldest standing building.

entities.name: Aksum
entities.summary: Capital of an Indian Ocean trading empire that minted coins, raised stelae and adopted Christianity early.

entities.name: Adulis
entities.summary: Aksum's Red Sea port, hub of ivory and incense trade with Rome and India.

entities.name: Matara
entities.summary: Pre-Aksumite and Aksumite inland town on the route from Adulis to Aksum.

entities.name: Qohaito
entities.summary: Aksumite highland town identified with Coloe, a stop on the ivory road.

entities.name: Lalibela
entities.summary: Zagwe capital of eleven rock-hewn churches, conceived as a new Jerusalem.

entities.name: Harar
entities.summary: Walled Islamic city of the Horn, a centre of trade, learning and coffee.

entities.name: Zeila
entities.summary: Red Sea port and gateway for Islam into the Ethiopian interior.

entities.name: Mogadishu
entities.summary: Leading Somali coast city-state trading gold, ivory and cloth across the Indian Ocean.

entities.name: Carthage
entities.summary: Phoenician sea empire's capital, Rome's great rival, refounded as a Roman metropolis.

caveats.text: 814 BCE founding is traditional.

entities.name: Utica
entities.summary: Oldest Phoenician colony in Africa, later a Roman city stranded by silting.

caveats.text: Traditional 1101 BCE founding date.

entities.name: Hadrumetum
entities.summary: Phoenician then Roman port at the heart of the olive-oil economy.

entities.name: Thapsus
entities.summary: Punic port where Caesar crushed the Pompeians in Africa.

entities.name: Kerkouane
entities.summary: Punic town abandoned and never rebuilt, so preserving pure Carthaginian domestic architecture.

entities.name: Thugga
entities.summary: Numidian then Roman hill city with a Libyco-Punic mausoleum and a fine theatre.

entities.name: Thysdrus
entities.summary: Olive-boom city that built Africa's greatest amphitheatre.

entities.name: Sufetula
entities.summary: Roman olive city with a triple-temple forum, briefly a Byzantine African capital.

entities.name: Cirta
entities.summary: Numidian royal capital of Massinissa on a gorge plateau.

entities.name: Hippo Regius
entities.summary: Numidian port and Augustine's bishopric, key to Latin Christian thought.

entities.name: Iol Caesarea
entities.summary: Punic port made Juba II's Hellenistic royal capital of Mauretania.

entities.name: Tipasa
entities.summary: Punic-Roman coastal town with major early Christian basilicas.

entities.name: Thamugadi
entities.summary: Trajan's perfectly gridded veteran colony, abandoned and buried by sand.

entities.name: Lambaesis
entities.summary: Legionary fortress-city headquarters of Rome's African army.

entities.name: Cuicul
entities.summary: Mountain colony with exceptionally preserved Roman streets and mosaics.

entities.name: Tahert
entities.summary: Capital of the Rustamid Ibadi imamate, a trans-Saharan trade node.

entities.name: Qal'at Bani Hammad
entities.summary: Hammadid mountain capital abandoned after Almohad conquest.

entities.name: Ashir
entities.summary: Early Zirid fortified capital in the Algerian highlands.

entities.name: Bejaia
entities.summary: Hammadid port that transmitted Arabic numerals to Europe through Fibonacci.

entities.name: Tlemcen
entities.summary: Zayyanid capital and northern terminus of the Sijilmasa gold road.

entities.name: Oea
entities.summary: Phoenician member of the Tripolis and the surviving one of the three.

entities.name: Leptis Magna
entities.summary: Punic port lavishly rebuilt by its native son Septimius Severus, then lost to sand.

entities.name: Sabratha
entities.summary: Tripolitanian port of the Saharan trade with a monumental seaside theatre.

entities.name: Cyrene
entities.summary: Greek colony that became the intellectual capital of Libya, home of Eratosthenes.

entities.name: Apollonia
entities.summary: Cyrene's harbour, later capital of Byzantine Libya, now partly submerged.

entities.name: Ptolemais
entities.summary: Pentapolis city with grand cisterns that became the Roman provincial seat.

entities.name: Barca
entities.summary: Cyrenaican inland city, later the region's Islamic administrative centre.

entities.name: Berenice
entities.summary: Pentapolis port refounded by the Ptolemies, ancestor of Benghazi.

entities.name: Garama
entities.summary: Garamantian capital in the Sahara sustained by foggara tunnel irrigation.

entities.name: Ghadames
entities.summary: Saharan caravan oasis of covered streets, a Roman outpost then a trade hub.

entities.name: Ghat
entities.summary: Tuareg Saharan caravan town on the route to Kano and Timbuktu.

entities.name: Kairouan
entities.summary: First great Islamic city of the Maghreb and base for the conquest of Iberia.

entities.name: Mahdia
entities.summary: Fortified peninsula capital founded by the first Fatimid caliph.

entities.name: Tunis
entities.summary: Punic town that replaced Carthage as the region's capital under the Hafsids.

entities.name: Raqqada
entities.summary: Aghlabid and early Fatimid palace-city outside Kairouan.

entities.name: Volubilis
entities.summary: Mauretanian and Roman city of olive presses and mosaics, later Idrisid base.

entities.name: Lixus
entities.summary: Phoenician Atlantic colony making purple dye and salt fish.

entities.name: Mogador
entities.summary: Atlantic island trading post for purple dye at the edge of the known world.

entities.name: Tingis
entities.summary: Strait of Gibraltar port and capital of Mauretania Tingitana.

entities.name: Sala Colonia
entities.summary: Southernmost Roman Atlantic city, later a Marinid necropolis.

entities.name: Ceuta
entities.summary: Strait fortress-port and Mediterranean gateway of the Maghreb.

entities.name: Fez
entities.summary: Idrisid foundation that became the Maghreb's intellectual capital with the Qarawiyyin.

entities.name: Marrakesh
entities.summary: Almoravid then Almohad imperial capital and northern gate of the Sahara trade.

entities.name: Meknes
entities.summary: Berber town that grew into an imperial Moroccan capital.

entities.name: Aghmat
entities.summary: Pre-Almoravid capital of the Marrakesh plain, eclipsed by its neighbour.

entities.name: Sijilmasa
entities.summary: Northern terminus of the Saharan gold road, minting the dinars that funded Mediterranean trade.

entities.name: Rabat
entities.summary: Almohad fortified camp-city built as a springboard for Iberian campaigns.

entities.name: Dhar Tichitt
entities.summary: Dry-stone settlement cluster, West Africa's earliest known urbanising complex.

entities.name: Awdaghost
entities.summary: Berber-Soninke caravan city where Saharan salt met Sahelian gold.

entities.name: Kumbi Saleh
entities.summary: Probable capital of the Ghana empire, a twin city of merchants and kings.

caveats.text: Identification as Ghana's capital is probable but not certain.

entities.name: Walata
entities.summary: Saharan caravan and scholarly town on the Timbuktu route.

entities.name: Djenné-Djenno
entities.summary: Africa's oldest known city south of the Sahara, built without centralised kingship.

entities.name: Djenné
entities.summary: Inland Niger Delta trade and scholarship city of great mudbrick mosques.

entities.name: Dia
entities.summary: Early Middle Niger urban cluster contemporary with and older than Jenne-jeno.

entities.name: Timbuktu
entities.summary: Saharan port of the Niger whose madrasas and manuscript libraries made it a legend.

entities.name: Gao
entities.summary: Songhai imperial capital on the Niger bend, controlling the eastern gold and salt roads.

entities.name: Tadmekka
entities.summary: Berber-Sahelian trade town that struck unstamped gold coins.

entities.name: Niani
entities.summary: Traditional capital of the Mali empire under Sundiata and Mansa Musa.

caveats.text: Identification as Mali's capital is debated.

entities.name: Takedda
entities.summary: Copper-producing Saharan town described by Ibn Battuta.

entities.name: Agadez
entities.summary: Tuareg sultanate city and southern gateway of the central Saharan routes.

entities.name: Njimi
entities.summary: Capital of the Kanem empire east of Lake Chad; its site remains unidentified.

caveats.text: Site not securely located.

entities.name: Kano
entities.summary: Walled Hausa city-state of indigo dyeing and the greatest Sahelian market.

entities.name: Katsina
entities.summary: Hausa city-state rivalling Kano for the trans-Saharan trade and Islamic learning.

entities.name: Zazzau
entities.summary: Hausa city-state, historically the southern slave-and-trade frontier.

entities.name: Ile-Ife
entities.summary: Yoruba spiritual capital that produced naturalistic bronze and terracotta heads.

entities.name: Oyo-Ile
entities.summary: Capital of the Oyo empire, the great Yoruba cavalry state.

entities.name: Benin City
entities.summary: Walled Edo capital of enormous earthworks and the Benin bronzes.

entities.name: Igbo-Ukwu
entities.summary: Site of astonishingly sophisticated cast bronzes and a rich burial; a ritual centre, not a city.

entities.name: Begho
entities.summary: Forest-edge market town where Akan gold entered the Saharan network.

entities.name: Bono Manso
entities.summary: Capital of the earliest Akan state, a gold and kola entrepôt.

entities.name: Sine-Ngayene
entities.summary: Vast megalithic burial complex of the Senegambia; ceremonial, not a city.

entities.name: Kilwa Kisiwani
entities.summary: Dominant Swahili sultanate, coral-stone city that monopolised the Zimbabwe gold trade.

entities.name: Manda
entities.summary: Early Swahili stone town trading with the Gulf and China.

entities.name: Shanga
entities.summary: Earliest excavated Swahili settlement with a sequence of timber-to-stone mosques.

entities.name: Lamu
entities.summary: Continuously inhabited Swahili stone town of the northern Kenya coast.

entities.name: Pate
entities.summary: Swahili city-state rival of Lamu, famed for silk weaving.

entities.name: Gedi
entities.summary: Prosperous Swahili coral town mysteriously abandoned in the 17th century.

entities.name: Unguja Ukuu
entities.summary: Early Indian Ocean trading settlement on Zanzibar, predating the Swahili stone towns.

entities.name: Sofala
entities.summary: Southernmost Swahili port, the outlet for Zimbabwean gold.

entities.name: Mapungubwe
entities.summary: First southern African class-based state capital, with gold rhinoceros burials on a sacred hill.

entities.name: Khami
entities.summary: Successor capital to Great Zimbabwe with decorated dry-stone terraces.

entities.name: Thulamela
entities.summary: Stone-walled Venda-linked settlement continuing the Mapungubwe tradition.

entities.name: Ingombe Ilede
entities.summary: Zambezi trading settlement with gold-and-copper burials linking interior to coast.

entities.name: African Union
entities.summary: Continental organisation succeeding the OAU, with a Peace and Security Council and free-trade area.

entities.name: Alaouite Sultanate of Morocco
entities.summary: Sharifian dynasty that has ruled Morocco since the 17th century, surviving colonial protectorate.

entities.name: Belgian Colonial Africa
entities.summary: Belgian Congo plus Ruanda-Urundi, decolonised abruptly in 1960-62.

entities.name: British Colonial Africa
entities.summary: British colonies and protectorates from the Cape to Egypt, decolonised mainly between 1956 and 1980.

entities.name: Burkina Faso
entities.summary: Independent as Upper Volta in 1960, renamed by Thomas Sankara in 1984, now facing jihadist war and coups.

entities.name: Republic of Cabo Verde
entities.summary: Atlantic island republic independent from Portugal in 1975, a stable multiparty democracy.

entities.name: Central African Republic
entities.summary: Independent in 1960, ruled briefly as an empire by Bokassa and repeatedly at civil war.

entities.name: Union of the Comoros
entities.summary: Indian Ocean state independent in 1975, with numerous coups and Mayotte remaining French.

entities.name: Decolonisation of Africa
entities.summary: Independence of more than fifty states, from Libya in 1951 to South Africa's democratic transition in 1994.

entities.name: Federal Democratic Republic of Ethiopia
entities.summary: Ethnic-federal republic established after the Derg's fall, later shaken by the Tigray war.

entities.name: Federal Republic of Nigeria
entities.summary: Africa's most populous state, independent in 1960, oil-rich and shaped by civil war and military rule.

entities.name: French Colonial Africa
entities.summary: French West and Equatorial Africa plus the Maghreb, mostly independent in 1960 and Algeria in 1962.

entities.name: Gabonese Republic
entities.summary: Oil-exporting republic independent in 1960, ruled by the Bongo family from 1967 until a 2023 coup.

entities.name: German Colonial Africa
entities.summary: Togo, Kamerun, South West Africa and East Africa, lost as mandates after the First World War.

entities.name: Italian Colonial Africa
entities.summary: Eritrea, Somalia, Libya and briefly Ethiopia, lost during the Second World War.

entities.name: Kingdom of Eswatini
entities.summary: Absolute monarchy independent in 1968, renamed from Swaziland in 2018.

entities.name: Kingdom of Lesotho
entities.summary: Mountain kingdom founded by Moshoeshoe I, a British protectorate then independent in 1966.

entities.name: Organisation of African Unity
entities.summary: Pan-African body founded in Addis Ababa that upheld colonial borders and backed liberation movements.

entities.name: Pan-Africanism
entities.summary: Movement for African unity and diaspora solidarity from the early congresses to Nkrumah and the AU.

entities.name: Portuguese Colonial Africa
entities.summary: Angola, Mozambique, Guinea-Bissau, Cape Verde and Sao Tome, held until the Carnation Revolution.

entities.name: People's Democratic Republic of Algeria
entities.summary: Independent from France in 1962, hydrocarbon-dependent and shaped by FLN rule and the 1990s civil war.

entities.name: Republic of Angola
entities.summary: Oil-rich state independent from Portugal in 1975, at civil war for most of its first three decades.

entities.name: Republic of Botswana
entities.summary: Diamond-rich republic independent in 1966, one of Africa's most durable democracies.

entities.name: Republic of Burundi
entities.summary: Independent in 1962, marked by mass killings in 1972 and 1993 and a long civil war.

entities.name: Republic of Cameroon
entities.summary: Former German then French and British territory, independent in 1960-61 and ruled by Paul Biya since 1982.

entities.name: Republic of Chad
entities.summary: Sahelian republic independent in 1960, with long civil wars and Libyan intervention.

entities.name: Republic of the Congo
entities.summary: Former French Congo independent in 1960, oil-exporting and long ruled by Denis Sassou Nguesso.

entities.name: Arab Republic of Egypt
entities.summary: Republic since 1953: Nasserism, wars with Israel, Sadat's peace, Mubarak's rule and the 2011 revolution.

entities.name: Republic of Ghana
entities.summary: First sub-Saharan colony to gain independence, on 6 March 1957, under Kwame Nkrumah.

entities.name: Republic of Guinea
entities.summary: Only French African colony to reject the 1958 community, independent under Sekou Toure.

entities.name: Republic of Kenya
entities.summary: Independent in 1963 under Jomo Kenyatta, later multiparty and shaped by the 2007-08 election violence.

entities.name: Republic of Liberia
entities.summary: Founded by freed American slaves and independent from 1847, later devastated by two civil wars.

entities.name: Republic of Madagascar
entities.summary: Indian Ocean island republic independent from France in 1960.

entities.name: Republic of Malawi
entities.summary: Independent in 1964, ruled for three decades by Hastings Banda before multiparty elections.

entities.name: Republic of Mali
entities.summary: Sahelian republic independent in 1960, since 2012 facing jihadist insurgency and coups.

entities.name: Republic of Mauritius
entities.summary: Independent in 1968 and a republic since 1992, with a diversified economy and stable democracy.

entities.name: Republic of Mozambique
entities.summary: Independent from Portugal in 1975 under FRELIMO, then torn by a long civil war.

entities.name: Republic of Namibia
entities.summary: Independent in 1990 after a UN-supervised transition following SWAPO's long struggle.

entities.name: Republic of Niger
entities.summary: Sahelian uranium-producing republic independent in 1960, with a 2023 coup ending civilian rule.

entities.name: Republic of Rwanda
entities.summary: Independent in 1962, site of the 1994 genocide and since then of state-led reconstruction under Paul Kagame.

entities.name: Republic of Senegal
entities.summary: West African republic independent in 1960, notable for stable civilian rule and Leopold Senghor's presidency.

entities.name: Republic of South Africa
entities.summary: Constitutional democracy since 1994, with a rights-based constitution and continuing inequality.

entities.name: Republic of the Sudan
entities.summary: Independent in 1956, marked by two civil wars, Darfur, Bashir's rule and renewed war from 2023.

entities.name: Republic of Tunisia
entities.summary: Independent republic under Bourguiba then Ben Ali, birthplace of the Arab Spring.

entities.name: Republic of Uganda
entities.summary: Independent in 1962, ravaged under Amin and Obote, ruled by Yoweri Museveni since 1986.

entities.name: Republic of Zambia
entities.summary: Copper-exporting republic independent in 1964 under Kenneth Kaunda.

entities.name: Republic of Zimbabwe
entities.summary: Independent in 1980 under Robert Mugabe, later hit by land seizures and hyperinflation.

entities.name: Sao Tome and Principe
entities.summary: Atlantic island republic independent from Portugal in 1975.

entities.name: Somali Republic
entities.summary: Union of British and Italian Somaliland in 1960, collapsed into statelessness after 1991.

entities.name: Republic of South Sudan
entities.summary: World's newest widely recognised state, independent by referendum in 2011 and soon at civil war.

entities.name: State of Eritrea
entities.summary: Independent by referendum in 1993, ruled since by Isaias Afwerki without elections.

entities.name: Togolese Republic
entities.summary: Former German then French territory independent in 1960, ruled by the Gnassingbe family since 1967.

entities.name: Indian Ocean and Trans-Saharan Slave Trades
entities.summary: Long-running slave trades across the Sahara and Indian Ocean, ended by gradual abolition and colonial rule.

entities.name: United Republic of Tanzania
entities.summary: Union of Tanganyika and Zanzibar, shaped by Nyerere's ujamaa socialism and later liberalisation.

entities.name: Year of Africa
entities.summary: Seventeen African countries became independent in 1960, transforming the United Nations.

entities.name: Argentine Republic
entities.summary: Federal republic constituted in 1853, transformed by mass European immigration and the grain and beef export boom.

entities.name: Commonwealth of The Bahamas
entities.summary: Archipelagic state independent from Britain in 1973.

entities.name: Barbados
entities.summary: Independent since 1966 and a republic since 2021, once a model English sugar colony.

entities.name: Belize
entities.summary: Former British Honduras, independent in 1981, the only English-speaking state in Central America.

entities.name: Bourbon Reforms
entities.summary: Administrative, fiscal and military reforms that increased extraction and provoked creole resentment and revolt.

entities.name: Federative Republic of Brazil
entities.summary: Democratic Brazil under the 1988 constitution, with the Real Plan, commodity boom and impeachment crises.

entities.name: Abolition of Slavery in the Caribbean
entities.summary: Successive emancipations from Haiti and the British colonies to Cuba, ending Atlantic plantation slavery.

entities.name: Caribbean Community
entities.summary: Regional integration organisation founded by the Treaty of Chaguaramas.

entities.name: Chaco War
entities.summary: Bolivia-Paraguay war over the Gran Chaco, won largely by Paraguay at great cost to both.

entities.name: Congress of Panama
entities.summary: Bolivar's attempt at a league of American republics, an ancestor of Pan-Americanism.

entities.name: Dominican Republic
entities.summary: Independent from Haiti in 1844, later occupied by the United States and ruled by Trujillo for three decades.

entities.name: Canada
entities.summary: Federal dominion of 1867 that grew to ten provinces and three territories and became fully sovereign by stages.

entities.name: French Guiana
entities.summary: French territory and now overseas department, once a penal colony and now home to the Kourou spaceport.

entities.name: Gran Colombia
entities.summary: Bolivar's union of Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador and Panama, dissolved by regional rivalries.

entities.name: Jamaica
entities.summary: Former Spanish then British sugar colony, independent within the Commonwealth since 1962.

entities.name: Oriental Republic of Uruguay
entities.summary: Buffer republic created by British mediation between Brazil and Argentina, later a pioneering welfare democracy.

entities.name: Paraguayan War
entities.summary: Triple Alliance of Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay devastated Paraguay, killing a large share of its population.

entities.name: Plurinational State of Bolivia
entities.summary: Andean republic named for Bolivar, which lost its coast and Chaco lands and elected its first Indigenous president in 2005.

entities.name: Republic of Chile
entities.summary: South American republic stabilised by Portales's 1833 constitution, later shaped by nitrates, copper and the Pinochet era.

entities.name: Republic of Colombia
entities.summary: Andean-Caribbean republic, successor to New Granada, marked by two-party civil wars and a long internal conflict.

entities.name: Republic of Costa Rica
entities.summary: Central American republic that abolished its army in 1949 and became the region's most stable democracy.

entities.name: Republic of Cuba
entities.summary: Cuban republic from 1902, under the Platt Amendment, then Batista, then communist rule since 1959.

entities.name: Republic of Ecuador
entities.summary: Andean-Pacific republic that left Gran Colombia in 1830; oil-exporting and dollarised since 2000.

entities.name: Republic of El Salvador
entities.summary: Central American republic marked by the 1932 Matanza, a brutal civil war and postwar gang violence.

entities.name: Republic of Guatemala
entities.summary: Central American republic of the 1944 October Revolution, the 1954 coup and a genocidal civil war.

entities.name: Republic of Guyana
entities.summary: Former British Guiana, independent in 1966 and transformed by offshore oil since 2019.

entities.name: Republic of Haiti
entities.summary: Independent since 1804, burdened by the French indemnity, US occupation, dictatorship and repeated state collapse.

entities.name: Republic of Honduras
entities.summary: Central American republic long dominated by banana companies and by military politics.

entities.name: Republic of Nicaragua
entities.summary: Central American republic shaped by US intervention, the Somoza dynasty and Sandinista rule.

entities.name: Republic of Panama
entities.summary: Seceded from Colombia with US backing in 1903; the canal returned to Panamanian control in 1999.

entities.name: Republic of Paraguay
entities.summary: Landlocked republic independent from 1811, devastated in the Triple Alliance war and ruled by Stroessner for 35 years.

entities.name: Republic of Peru
entities.summary: Andean republic independent from 1821, shaped by guano and nitrate booms, military rule and the Shining Path conflict.

entities.name: Republic of Suriname
entities.summary: Former Dutch Guiana, independent in 1975, with large emigration to the Netherlands.

entities.name: Republic of Venezuela
entities.summary: Caribbean-Andean republic that left Gran Colombia in 1830, later transformed by oil and by Chavismo.

entities.name: Campaigns of Jose de San Martin
entities.summary: Crossing of the Andes, liberation of Chile at Chacabuco and Maipu, and the proclamation of Peru's independence.

entities.name: Campaigns of Simon Bolivar
entities.summary: The Liberator's campaigns from Venezuela over the Andes to Boyaca, Carabobo, Junin and Ayacucho.

entities.name: Spanish American Wars of Independence
entities.summary: Continental struggle that ended Spanish rule in the mainland Americas and created some fifteen republics.

entities.name: Trinidad and Tobago
entities.summary: Oil- and gas-rich Caribbean state independent in 1962 and a republic since 1976.

entities.name: Viceroyalty of New Granada
entities.summary: Spanish viceroyalty covering Colombia, Venezuela, Ecuador and Panama, based at Bogota.

entities.name: Viceroyalty of the Rio de la Plata
entities.summary: Late Spanish viceroyalty based in Buenos Aires covering Argentina, Uruguay, Paraguay and Bolivia.

entities.name: War of the Pacific
entities.summary: Chile defeated Peru and Bolivia, taking nitrate provinces and leaving Bolivia landlocked.

entities.name: Kyrgyz Republic
entities.summary: Central Asian republic independent in 1991, with revolutions in 2005, 2010 and 2020.

entities.name: Republic of Kazakhstan
entities.summary: Largest Central Asian state, independent in 1991, oil-rich and ruled by Nazarbayev until 2019.

entities.name: Republic of Tajikistan
entities.summary: Independent in 1991 and scarred by a civil war from 1992 to 1997; ruled by Emomali Rahmon.

entities.name: Republic of Uzbekistan
entities.summary: Most populous Central Asian state, independent in 1991, ruled by Karimov until 2016.

entities.name: Turkmenistan
entities.summary: Gas-rich neutral state independent in 1991 under Niyazov's personality cult and his successors.

entities.name: Asian Financial Crisis
entities.summary: Currency and banking collapse from Thailand to Korea and Indonesia, with IMF programmes and political upheaval.

entities.name: First Sino-Japanese War
entities.summary: Japanese victory that took Taiwan and ended Chinese suzerainty over Korea.

entities.name: Manchukuo
entities.summary: Japanese puppet state in Manchuria nominally headed by the last Qing emperor Puyi.

entities.name: Mongolia
entities.summary: Democratic parliamentary republic since 1992 with a mining-based economy.

entities.name: Pacific War
entities.summary: War between Japan and the Allies from Pearl Harbor to the surrender aboard USS Missouri.

entities.name: Russo-Japanese War
entities.summary: Japan's victory over Russia at Port Arthur, Mukden and Tsushima, the first modern Asian defeat of a European power.

entities.name: Second Sino-Japanese War
entities.summary: Full-scale Japanese invasion of China, part of the Second World War, with 15-20 million Chinese deaths.

entities.name: Taiwan Strait Crises
entities.summary: Series of military confrontations between the PRC and Taiwan involving American intervention.

entities.name: Principality of Andorra
entities.summary: Pyrenean co-principality under the Spanish bishop of Urgell and the French head of state; parliamentary since 1993.

entities.name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
entities.summary: Independent state since 1992, governed since Dayton as a federation of two entities with international oversight.

entities.name: Concert of Europe
entities.summary: System of great-power consultation and congresses that limited general European war for a century.

entities.name: Congress of Vienna
entities.summary: Great-power settlement that redrew Europe's map, restored monarchies and created a balance of power lasting decades.

entities.name: Continental System
entities.summary: Napoleon's blockade of British trade, which damaged European economies and provoked the Peninsular and Russian wars.

entities.name: Council of Europe
entities.summary: Pan-European human rights body that created the European Convention and its court.

entities.name: EU Enlargement of 2004
entities.summary: Ten mostly post-communist states joined the European Union, the largest single enlargement.

entities.name: Introduction of the Euro
entities.summary: Single currency launched for accounting in 1999 and as cash in 2002, now used by 20 states.

entities.name: European Coal and Steel Community
entities.summary: Six-nation pooling of coal and steel, the first step of European integration.

entities.name: European Economic Community
entities.summary: Common market of six then twelve states that became the European Union at Maastricht.

entities.name: European Migrant Crisis
entities.summary: Arrival of over a million asylum seekers, mainly from Syria, straining EU cohesion and border policy.

entities.name: European Union
entities.summary: Union of 27 states with a single market, common currency for most members and supranational institutions.

entities.name: Eurozone Debt Crisis
entities.summary: Sovereign-debt crisis in Greece, Ireland, Portugal, Spain and Cyprus that tested monetary union.

entities.name: February Revolution
entities.summary: Petrograd bread riots and mutiny toppled the tsar and created a Provisional Government and soviets.

entities.name: First Chechen War
entities.summary: Russian invasion of separatist Chechnya ending in a humiliating ceasefire at Khasavyurt.

entities.name: Founding of St Petersburg
entities.summary: Peter I founded his new capital on the Neva as a window on Europe.

entities.name: French Invasion of Russia
entities.summary: Napoleon's Grande Armee reached Moscow and was destroyed in retreat, losing most of half a million men.

entities.name: Grand Duchy of Luxembourg
entities.summary: Grand duchy created at Vienna, fully independent since 1839-1890, a founding member of the European communities.

entities.name: Helsinki Final Act
entities.summary: Agreement recognising postwar borders while committing signatories to human rights, empowering dissidents.

entities.name: House of Romanov
entities.summary: Dynasty that ruled Russia for three centuries, from Michael I to Nicholas II.

entities.name: Ukraine
entities.summary: Independent since the 1991 referendum; the Orange Revolution, Euromaidan and war with Russia have shaped its statehood.

entities.name: Iron Curtain
entities.summary: Division of Europe between Soviet-dominated east and Western-aligned west, symbolised by Churchill's 1946 speech.

entities.name: Italian Republic
entities.summary: Republic established by the 1946 referendum, a founding member of NATO and the European communities.

entities.name: Kingdom of Belgium
entities.summary: Constitutional monarchy independent since 1830, twice invaded by Germany, now a federal state and EU seat.

entities.name: Kingdom of Denmark
entities.summary: Europe's oldest continuous monarchy, constitutional since 1849, occupied 1940-45, an EU member since 1973.

entities.name: Kingdom of Norway
entities.summary: Independent constitutional monarchy since the 1905 dissolution of the union with Sweden; oil wealth since the 1970s.

entities.name: Kingdom of Spain
entities.summary: Parliamentary monarchy since Franco's death, a member of the EU since 1986 and NATO since 1982.

entities.name: Kingdom of Sweden
entities.summary: Continuous Swedish state since 1523, neutral through both world wars, an EU member from 1995 and NATO from 2024.

entities.name: Principality of Liechtenstein
entities.summary: Alpine principality created in 1719, sovereign since 1806 and closely tied to Switzerland.

entities.name: Maastricht Treaty
entities.summary: Treaty creating the European Union, EU citizenship and the path to monetary union.

entities.name: Republic of Moldova
entities.summary: Former Soviet republic independent since 1991, with the breakaway Transnistria region and EU candidate status.

entities.name: Principality of Monaco
entities.summary: Grimaldi principality on the Riviera whose sovereignty was confirmed in 1861 under French protection.

entities.name: Munich Agreement
entities.summary: Britain, France, Germany and Italy ceded the Sudetenland to Hitler, the high point of appeasement.

entities.name: October Revolution
entities.summary: Bolshevik seizure of power in Petrograd under Lenin and Trotsky, creating the world's first communist state.

entities.name: Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe
entities.summary: Security and human-rights organisation growing out of the Helsinki process.

entities.name: Peace of Westphalia
entities.summary: Treaties of Munster and Osnabruck that ended the Thirty Years' War and framed the modern system of sovereign states.

entities.name: Portuguese Republic
entities.summary: Democratic republic under the 1976 constitution, an EU member since 1986 and euro founder.

entities.name: Reign of Charles X of France
entities.summary: Ultra-royalist king whose July Ordinances provoked the 1830 revolution; began the conquest of Algiers.

entities.name: Reign of Louis XVIII
entities.summary: Restored Bourbon king who accepted the Charter of 1814 and steered a moderate course between ultras and liberals.

entities.name: Republic of Albania
entities.summary: Post-communist democracy since 1992, a NATO member from 2009 and EU candidate.

entities.name: Republic of Belarus
entities.summary: Independent since 1991 and ruled by Alexander Lukashenko since 1994 in close alignment with Russia.

entities.name: Republic of Bulgaria
entities.summary: Democratic republic since 1990, in NATO from 2004 and the EU from 2007.

entities.name: Republic of Croatia
entities.summary: Independent since 1991, a NATO member from 2009, EU from 2013 and eurozone from 2023.

entities.name: Republic of Estonia
entities.summary: Baltic republic that restored independence in 1991 and joined the EU and NATO in 2004; a digital-government pioneer.

entities.name: Republic of Finland
entities.summary: Nordic republic that preserved independence against the USSR, joined the EU in 1995 and NATO in 2023.

entities.name: Hungary
entities.summary: Democratic republic since 1989, in NATO from 1999 and the EU from 2004; governed by Viktor Orban since 2010.

entities.name: Republic of Latvia
entities.summary: Baltic republic independent again from 1991, in the EU and NATO since 2004 and the euro since 2014.

entities.name: Republic of Lithuania
entities.summary: First Soviet republic to declare independence, in March 1990; EU and NATO member since 2004.

entities.name: Republic of Malta
entities.summary: Mediterranean island state independent from Britain in 1964, a republic from 1974 and EU member from 2004.

entities.name: Montenegro
entities.summary: Adriatic republic independent since a 2006 referendum, a NATO member since 2017.

entities.name: Romania
entities.summary: Democratic republic since 1989, in NATO from 2004 and the EU from 2007.

entities.name: Republic of Serbia
entities.summary: Independent Serbia since Montenegro's separation; an EU candidate that does not recognise Kosovo.

entities.name: Republic of Slovenia
entities.summary: First Yugoslav republic to secede successfully; joined the EU and NATO in 2004 and the euro in 2007.

entities.name: Revolutions of 1848
entities.summary: Liberal and nationalist uprisings across France, the German states, Italy, Austria and Hungary, mostly defeated.

entities.name: Revolutions of 1989
entities.summary: Peaceful collapse of communist regimes across Eastern Europe, from Poland to Romania.

entities.name: Russian Civil War
entities.summary: Reds defeated Whites, nationalists and Allied interventions at a cost of millions of lives and famine.

entities.name: Russian Conquest of Siberia
entities.summary: Cossack and merchant expansion across northern Asia to the Pacific, driven by the fur trade.

entities.name: Russian Provisional Government
entities.summary: Liberal-socialist government under Lvov then Kerensky that kept Russia in the war and fell in October.

entities.name: Schengen Agreement
entities.summary: Agreement abolishing internal border checks, implemented in 1995 and now covering most of the EU.

entities.name: Republic of Austria
entities.summary: Neutral democratic republic, sovereign from 1955 and an EU member since 1995.

entities.name: Second Chechen War
entities.summary: Renewed campaign that reasserted Moscow's control over Chechnya under Kadyrov.

entities.name: Slovakia
entities.summary: Independent Slovak republic since 1993, in NATO and the EU from 2004 and the euro from 2009.

entities.name: Swiss Confederation
entities.summary: Federal state created by the 1848 constitution, neutral, directly democratic and home to many international bodies.

entities.name: Hellenic Republic
entities.summary: Democratic Greece since the fall of the junta, an EU member since 1981 and euro member since 2001.

entities.name: Third Polish Republic
entities.summary: Democratic Poland since 1989, in NATO from 1999 and the EU from 2004.

entities.name: Time of Troubles
entities.summary: Dynastic vacuum, famine, false Dmitrys and Polish-Swedish intervention, ended by the election of the Romanovs.

entities.name: Treaty of Rome
entities.summary: Founding treaty of the European Economic Community and Euratom, creating a common market.

entities.name: War Communism
entities.summary: Forced grain requisitioning and nationalisation during the civil war, ended by famine and the New Economic Policy.

entities.name: Global Abolition of Slavery
entities.summary: Successive abolitions from revolutionary France and Britain to Brazil that ended legal chattel slavery in the Atlantic world.

entities.name: Age of Revolutions
entities.summary: Atlantic and European revolutions that spread republicanism, nationalism and abolition.

entities.name: Anthropogenic Climate Change
entities.summary: Industrial-era warming from greenhouse gases, now a central issue of international politics.

entities.name: Rise of Artificial Intelligence
entities.summary: Deep learning and large language models that moved AI into mainstream economic and political consequence.

entities.name: Atlantic Slave Trade
entities.summary: Forced transport of roughly 12.5 million Africans to the Americas, the foundation of the plantation economies.

entities.name: Bretton Woods System
entities.summary: Postwar monetary order of fixed exchange rates and dollar-gold convertibility, with the IMF and World Bank.

entities.name: BRICS
entities.summary: Grouping of major emerging economies, originally Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa, later expanded.

entities.name: Decolonisation
entities.summary: Dissolution of the European empires and the emergence of scores of new states across Asia, Africa and the Pacific.

entities.name: Early Modern Period
entities.summary: Era of gunpowder empires, printing, global commerce, scientific revolution and Atlantic slavery.

entities.name: End of the Cold War
entities.summary: Collapse of the Eastern bloc and dissolution of the USSR, leaving the United States as sole superpower.

entities.name: First Age of Globalisation
entities.summary: Steamships, telegraphs, gold standard and mass migration that integrated the world economy before 1914.

entities.name: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade
entities.summary: Postwar framework of trade negotiation rounds that lowered tariffs worldwide, replaced by the WTO.

entities.name: Genocide Convention
entities.summary: UN convention defining and criminalising genocide, drafted after the Holocaust.

entities.name: Global Silver Trade
entities.summary: American silver flowing via Europe and Manila to China, the first genuinely global commodity circuit.

entities.name: Contemporary Globalisation
entities.summary: Deepening integration of trade, finance, production and information, with container shipping and the internet.

entities.name: Age of Mass Migration
entities.summary: Roughly 55 million Europeans and millions of Asians migrated across oceans, reshaping settler societies.

entities.name: Green Revolution
entities.summary: High-yield crop varieties, fertiliser and irrigation that greatly increased food production in Asia and Latin America.

entities.name: HIV/AIDS Pandemic
entities.summary: Global epidemic that has killed tens of millions, transformed by antiretroviral therapy from the late 1990s.

entities.name: The Holocaust
entities.summary: Nazi genocide of about six million Jews, alongside the murder of Roma, disabled people and others.

entities.name: International Monetary Fund
entities.summary: Institution created at Bretton Woods to lend to countries in balance-of-payments difficulty.

entities.name: Information Revolution
entities.summary: Microprocessors, personal computing, the internet and mobile networks that reorganised economy and society.

entities.name: International Criminal Court
entities.summary: Permanent court for genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity, created by the Rome Statute.

entities.name: Interwar Period
entities.summary: Two decades of fragile peace: reparations, boom, depression, fascism and the collapse of collective security.

entities.name: Kyoto Protocol
entities.summary: First binding treaty on greenhouse-gas emissions, in force from 2005 without US ratification.

entities.name: League of Nations
entities.summary: First general international organisation for collective security, weakened by absences and its failures in the 1930s.

entities.name: Seventeenth-Century Crisis
entities.summary: Cooling climate, harvest failure, war and rebellion from Europe to China in a century of upheaval.

entities.name: League of Nations Mandate System
entities.summary: Administration of former German and Ottoman territories by the victors as trusteeships in name.

entities.name: Marshall Plan
entities.summary: American aid programme of about 13 billion dollars that rebuilt Western European economies and tied them together.

entities.name: North Atlantic Treaty Organization
entities.summary: Transatlantic military alliance founded in 1949 on collective defence under Article 5, now 32 members.

entities.name: New Imperialism
entities.summary: Intense European, American and Japanese colonial expansion into Africa, Asia and the Pacific.

entities.name: Non-Aligned Movement
entities.summary: Grouping of states refusing Cold War alignment, founded at Belgrade after the Bandung Conference.

entities.name: Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty
entities.summary: Treaty limiting the spread of nuclear weapons while recognising five nuclear-weapon states.

entities.name: 1973 Oil Crisis
entities.summary: Arab oil embargo that quadrupled prices, ending the postwar boom and reshaping energy policy.

entities.name: Paris Agreement
entities.summary: Universal climate accord committing states to limit warming well below two degrees Celsius.

entities.name: Paris Peace Conference and Treaty of Versailles
entities.summary: Settlement that redrew Europe and the Middle East, imposed reparations on Germany and created the League and mandates.

entities.name: Rise of Fascism
entities.summary: Spread of fascist and authoritarian movements in Italy, Germany, Spain, Japan and beyond between the wars.

entities.name: Eradication of Smallpox
entities.summary: WHO campaign that eliminated smallpox, the only human disease so far eradicated.

entities.name: Spanish Flu Pandemic
entities.summary: Influenza pandemic that infected a third of humanity and killed an estimated 50 million people.

entities.name: Third World and Global South
entities.summary: Category for states outside the Western and Soviet blocs, later reframed as the Global South.

entities.name: United Nations
entities.summary: Universal international organisation founded in San Francisco in 1945, with 193 member states.

entities.name: Universal Declaration of Human Rights
entities.summary: UN General Assembly declaration setting out a common standard of rights for all peoples.

entities.name: Spread of Universal Suffrage
entities.summary: Extension of the vote to women and excluded groups, from New Zealand in 1893 to South Africa in 1994.

entities.name: World Health Organization
entities.summary: UN agency for international health, which coordinated smallpox eradication and pandemic responses.

entities.name: World Bank
entities.summary: Development lender founded at Bretton Woods, originally for postwar reconstruction.

entities.name: Modern Population Explosion
entities.summary: Growth from about one billion people in 1800 to over eight billion, driven by falling mortality.

entities.name: World Trade Organization
entities.summary: Organisation governing world trade rules and disputes, founded in 1995 from GATT.

entities.name: World Wide Web
entities.summary: Berners-Lee's invention at CERN that made the internet a mass medium.

entities.name: French Polynesia
entities.summary: French overseas collectivity of 121 islands, site of nuclear testing at Mururoa.

entities.name: Independent State of Samoa
entities.summary: Polynesian state independent since 1962, with a fa'amatai chiefly political system.

entities.name: New Caledonia
entities.summary: French territory with a large Kanak population and repeated independence referendums under the Noumea Accord.

entities.name: Pacific Decolonisation
entities.summary: Successive independences from Samoa in 1962 to Palau in 1994, leaving some territories under metropolitan rule.

entities.name: Pacific Islands Forum
entities.summary: Regional political grouping of Pacific states, prominent in climate diplomacy.

entities.name: Nuclear Testing in the Pacific
entities.summary: American, British and French tests at Bikini, Christmas Island, Maralinga and Mururoa with lasting contamination.

entities.name: Republic of Fiji
entities.summary: Independent in 1970 and a republic since 1987, with four coups over ethnic and political disputes.

entities.name: Solomon Islands
entities.summary: Melanesian state independent from Britain in 1978, with ethnic conflict and a regional intervention from 2003.

entities.name: Tuvalu
entities.summary: Polynesian atoll state independent in 1978, among the most exposed to sea-level rise.

entities.name: Afghan Civil War of the 1990s
entities.summary: Factional war after Najibullah's fall, won largely by the Taliban from 1996.

entities.name: All-India Muslim League
entities.summary: Party founded in Dhaka that under Jinnah demanded and won Pakistan.

entities.name: Anglo-Afghan Wars
entities.summary: Three British wars that failed to control Afghanistan, which won full independence in 1919.

entities.name: Dominion of Ceylon and Sri Lanka
entities.summary: Independent in 1948, renamed Sri Lanka as a republic in 1972 after decades of communal tension.

entities.name: Durrani Empire
entities.summary: Ahmad Shah Durrani's empire stretching from Mashhad to Delhi, the foundation of modern Afghanistan.

entities.name: Federal Democratic Republic of Nepal
entities.summary: Republic declared in 2008 after the Maoist war and the 2001 royal massacre.

entities.name: First Kashmir War
entities.summary: War over Kashmir after the maharaja's accession to India, ending with the ceasefire line.

entities.name: Indian and Pakistani Nuclear Tests
entities.summary: Pokhran-II and Chagai tests made both states declared nuclear powers.

entities.name: Indo-Pakistani War of 1965
entities.summary: Second war over Kashmir, ended by the Soviet-brokered Tashkent Declaration.

entities.name: Islamic Republic of Afghanistan
entities.summary: Western-backed republic under Karzai and Ghani that collapsed as US forces left.

entities.name: Islamic Republic of Pakistan
entities.summary: Republic since 1956, alternating between civilian and military rule, nuclear-armed since 1998.

entities.name: Kargil War
entities.summary: High-altitude conflict after Pakistani infiltration into Indian-held Kashmir.

entities.name: Kingdom of Afghanistan
entities.summary: Monarchy under Amanullah, Nadir Shah and Zahir Shah, ended by Daoud's republican coup.

entities.name: Kingdom of Bhutan
entities.summary: Himalayan Wangchuck monarchy, constitutional since 2008 and known for Gross National Happiness.

entities.name: People's Republic of Bangladesh
entities.summary: Independent since 1971, one of the world's most densely populated states and a garment-export power.

entities.name: Republic of India
entities.summary: World's largest democracy, a federal republic under the 1950 constitution and the most populous country since 2023.

entities.name: Republic of Maldives
entities.summary: Indian Ocean island state independent from Britain in 1965, a republic from 1968.

entities.name: Saur Revolution
entities.summary: Communist coup that installed the PDPA and triggered rural revolt and Soviet intervention.

entities.name: Reign of Shivaji
entities.summary: Founder-king who built a Maratha state through guerrilla war against the Mughals and Bijapur.

entities.name: Soviet-Afghan War
entities.summary: Nine-year Soviet occupation opposed by US- and Pakistan-backed mujahideen, ending in withdrawal.

entities.name: Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan (first period)
entities.summary: Taliban rule imposing strict shari'a and sheltering al-Qaeda, ended by US-led intervention.

entities.name: Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan (restored)
entities.summary: Taliban government since August 2021, unrecognised and enforcing severe restrictions on women.

entities.name: United States War in Afghanistan
entities.summary: Twenty-year NATO-led war after 9/11, ending in Taliban restoration and Western withdrawal.

entities.name: Association of Southeast Asian Nations
entities.summary: Regional organisation founded in Bangkok, now ten member states pursuing economic and security cooperation.

entities.name: Bandung Conference
entities.summary: First large Asian-African conference, a founding moment of Third World solidarity and non-alignment.

entities.name: First Indochina War
entities.summary: Viet Minh war against France that ended with Dien Bien Phu and the Geneva Accords.

entities.name: Geneva Accords
entities.summary: Agreements partitioning Vietnam at the 17th parallel and recognising Laotian and Cambodian independence.

entities.name: Japanese Occupation of Indochina
entities.summary: Japanese control alongside Vichy French administration, ending in the 1945 coup and Vietnamese famine.

entities.name: Kingdom of Cambodia
entities.summary: Restored constitutional monarchy, dominated politically by Hun Sen and his family since 1985.

entities.name: Kingdom of Thailand
entities.summary: Constitutional monarchy renamed Thailand in 1939, with a modern history of frequent military coups.

entities.name: Lao People's Democratic Republic
entities.summary: Communist state proclaimed after the Pathet Lao victory, the world's most heavily bombed country per capita.

entities.name: Malaysia
entities.summary: Federation formed in 1963 with Sabah, Sarawak and briefly Singapore; a rotating elective monarchy.

entities.name: Republic of the Philippines
entities.summary: Southeast Asian republic independent since 1946, with the Marcos dictatorship and People Power in its history.

entities.name: Democratic Republic of Timor-Leste
entities.summary: Independent in 2002 after a UN-run referendum and transitional administration.

entities.name: Union of Burma and Myanmar
entities.summary: Independent from Britain in 1948, under military rule for most of its history and renamed Myanmar in 1989.

entities.name: Abraham Accords
entities.summary: Normalisation agreements between Israel and the UAE, Bahrain, Morocco and Sudan.

entities.name: 1948 Arab-Israeli War
entities.summary: War following Israel's declaration, ending in armistice lines and the displacement of most Palestinian Arabs.

entities.name: Arab League
entities.summary: Regional organisation of Arab states founded in Cairo in 1945.

entities.name: Arab Revolt
entities.summary: Hashemite rising against Ottoman rule, encouraged by Britain and aided by T. E. Lawrence.

entities.name: Arab Spring
entities.summary: Wave of uprisings from Tunisia to Bahrain that toppled four rulers and triggered wars in Libya, Syria and Yemen.

entities.name: Battle of Lepanto
entities.summary: Holy League naval victory over the Ottoman fleet that ended the myth of Ottoman invincibility at sea.

entities.name: Camp David Accords
entities.summary: Egyptian-Israeli peace brokered by Carter, returning Sinai to Egypt; Sadat was assassinated in 1981.

entities.name: First Nagorno-Karabakh War
entities.summary: War between Armenians and Azerbaijan over Karabakh that displaced about a million people.

entities.name: Gulf War
entities.summary: US-led coalition expelled Iraq from Kuwait after its August 1990 invasion.

entities.name: Iran-Iraq War
entities.summary: Eight-year war of attrition with chemical weapons and about a million casualties, ending in stalemate.

entities.name: Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan
entities.summary: Hashemite monarchy independent in 1946, host to large Palestinian refugee populations.

entities.name: Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
entities.summary: Absolute monarchy guarding Mecca and Medina, transformed by the world's largest conventional oil reserves.

entities.name: The Kurdish Question
entities.summary: Statelessness of the Kurds after Sevres, with insurgencies and autonomy struggles in Turkey, Iraq, Iran and Syria.

entities.name: Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries
entities.summary: Cartel founded in Baghdad that reshaped global energy politics, notably in the 1973 embargo.

entities.name: Oslo Accords
entities.summary: Israeli-Palestinian agreements creating the Palestinian Authority and mutual recognition.

entities.name: Republic of Armenia
entities.summary: Independent since 1991, shaped by the Nagorno-Karabakh conflict with Azerbaijan.

entities.name: Republic of Azerbaijan
entities.summary: Oil-rich Caspian republic independent in 1991, ruled by the Aliyev family since 1993.

entities.name: Republic of Cyprus
entities.summary: Independent from Britain in 1960, de facto divided since 1974 and an EU member since 2004.

entities.name: Georgia
entities.summary: Independent since 1991; the Rose Revolution, the 2008 war with Russia and EU aspirations have defined it.

entities.name: Republic of Iraq
entities.summary: Republic since 1958: Ba'athist rule, three wars, occupation and a federal constitution since 2005.

entities.name: Lebanese Republic
entities.summary: Independent confessional republic, shaped by civil war, Syrian tutelage and economic collapse.

entities.name: Republic of Turkey
entities.summary: Secular republic founded by Ataturk on 29 October 1923, a NATO member since 1952.

entities.name: Republic of Yemen
entities.summary: Unified in 1990, since 2014 divided by civil war and Saudi-led intervention.

entities.name: Russo-Georgian War
entities.summary: Five-day war over South Ossetia and Abkhazia that Russia won and followed by recognising both.

entities.name: Second Nagorno-Karabakh War
entities.summary: Forty-four-day Azerbaijani victory that recovered most occupied territory; Karabakh fell entirely in 2023.

entities.name: Six-Day War
entities.summary: Israeli victory over Egypt, Jordan and Syria that took Sinai, Gaza, the West Bank, Jerusalem and the Golan.

entities.name: State of Israel
entities.summary: Jewish state declared on 14 May 1948, which has fought repeated wars with its neighbours and Palestinians.

entities.name: State of Palestine
entities.summary: Declared in 1988 and recognised by most UN members; a UN observer state since 2012.

entities.name: State of Qatar
entities.summary: Gas-rich emirate independent in 1971, home to Al Jazeera and host of the 2022 World Cup.

entities.name: Sultanate of Oman
entities.summary: Al Bu Said sultanate that once ruled Zanzibar, modernised after Sultan Qaboos took power in 1970.

entities.name: Sykes-Picot Agreement
entities.summary: Secret Anglo-French plan to divide Ottoman Arab lands, the basis of later mandate borders.

entities.name: Syrian Arab Republic
entities.summary: Independent from France in 1946; Ba'athist from 1963, ruled by the Assads from 1970 to 2024.

entities.name: United Arab Emirates
entities.summary: Federation of seven emirates formed on British withdrawal, now a global trade and finance hub.

entities.name: Yom Kippur War
entities.summary: Egyptian and Syrian surprise attack on Israel that led to the oil embargo and eventually to peace talks.

entities.name: French and Spanish Protectorates in Morocco
entities.summary: Treaty of Fez protectorate with a Spanish zone, resisted in the Rif War and ended in 1956.

entities.name: Green March
entities.summary: Mass Moroccan civilian march into Spanish Sahara that secured Moroccan control.

entities.name: Kingdom of Morocco
entities.summary: Independent monarchy since 1956 under Mohammed V, Hassan II and Mohammed VI.

entities.name: Rif War
entities.summary: Abd el-Krim's republic defeated Spanish armies before falling to a Franco-Spanish offensive.

entities.name: Rule of Thomas Sankara
entities.summary: Revolutionary leader of literacy, vaccination and anti-imperial rhetoric, assassinated in 1987.

entities.name: Belgian Congo
entities.summary: Belgian state colony exploited for copper, rubber and uranium, decolonised abruptly in 1960.

entities.name: Congo Crisis
entities.summary: Post-independence collapse: Katangese secession, Lumumba's murder, UN intervention and Mobutu's rise.

entities.name: Congo Free State
entities.summary: Leopold II's personal colony whose rubber regime caused mass death and international scandal.

entities.name: Democratic Republic of the Congo
entities.summary: Vast mineral-rich state renamed in 1997, still troubled by conflict in its eastern provinces.

entities.name: Republic of Equatorial Guinea
entities.summary: Only Spanish-speaking African state, independent in 1968, oil-rich and highly repressive.

entities.name: First Congo War
entities.summary: Rwandan- and Ugandan-backed rebellion that overthrew Mobutu.

entities.name: Kingdom of Kongo (Kingdom Of Kongo)
entities.summary: Christianised Central African kingdom that traded with Portugal and declined under the slave trade.

entities.name: Rule of Mobutu Sese Seko
entities.summary: Thirty-two years of kleptocratic rule over the country he renamed Zaire.

entities.name: Republic of Zaire
entities.summary: Mobutu's renamed state, ended by Kabila's rebellion in the First Congo War.

entities.name: Ruanda-Urundi
entities.summary: Belgian mandate then trust territory that hardened Hutu-Tutsi categories through identity cards.

entities.name: Second Congo War
entities.summary: Africa's world war, involving nine countries and causing millions of deaths, mostly from disease and hunger.

entities.name: Republic of Djibouti
entities.summary: Former French Somaliland independent in 1977, now host to multiple foreign military bases.

entities.name: Eritrean-Ethiopian War
entities.summary: Border war over Badme that killed tens of thousands and froze relations until 2018.

entities.name: German East Africa
entities.summary: German colony covering Tanganyika, Rwanda and Burundi, site of the Maji Maji rebellion.

entities.name: Republic of Seychelles
entities.summary: Indian Ocean archipelago independent from Britain in 1976.

entities.name: Battle of Adwa
entities.summary: Ethiopian defeat of an Italian army, the only decisive African victory over a European colonial power.

entities.name: Derg
entities.summary: Marxist military junta under Mengistu: Red Terror, famine and war with Eritrea and Somalia.

entities.name: Ethiopian Famine of 1983-85
entities.summary: Drought and war famine that killed several hundred thousand and prompted global relief campaigns.

entities.name: Italian Occupation of Ethiopia
entities.summary: Five years of Italian East Africa rule with poison gas and reprisals, ended by British and Ethiopian forces.

entities.name: Tigray War
entities.summary: Federal and Eritrean campaign against Tigray's regional government, with mass atrocities and famine conditions.

entities.name: Boko Haram Insurgency
entities.summary: Jihadist conflict in the northeast with mass abductions and millions displaced across the Lake Chad basin.

entities.name: Colonial Nigeria
entities.summary: British protectorates amalgamated in 1914 and ruled through indirect rule over emirs and chiefs.

entities.name: Kingdom of Benin (late)
entities.summary: Powerful Edo kingdom famed for its bronzes, sacked and looted by a British punitive expedition in 1897.

entities.name: Nigerian Civil War
entities.summary: Biafra's secession and blockade, which killed one to two million people, mostly by starvation.

entities.name: Nigerian Fourth Republic
entities.summary: Civilian democracy since 1999, contending with Boko Haram, oil-delta conflict and rapid population growth.

entities.name: Nigerian Military Rule
entities.summary: Nearly three decades of coups and juntas, including Abacha's dictatorship, ending with the Fourth Republic.

entities.name: Rule of Muammar Gaddafi
entities.summary: Forty-two years of idiosyncratic rule under the Jamahiriya, ended by uprising and NATO intervention.

entities.name: Italian Libya
entities.summary: Italian colony whose pacification killed a large share of the Cyrenaican population.

entities.name: Kingdom of Libya
entities.summary: Senussi monarchy under Idris I, independent by UN resolution and transformed by oil.

entities.name: Libyan Civil Wars
entities.summary: Uprising and NATO campaign that killed Gaddafi, followed by a decade of rival governments and militias.

entities.name: Ottoman Tripolitania
entities.summary: Ottoman and Karamanli rule over the Libyan coast, ended by the Italian invasion.

entities.name: Algerian Civil War
entities.summary: War between the state and Islamist insurgents after cancelled elections, with about 150,000 to 200,000 dead.

entities.name: Algerian War of Independence
entities.summary: Eight-year FLN insurgency and French counterinsurgency that killed hundreds of thousands and toppled the Fourth Republic.

entities.name: Battle of Algiers
entities.summary: Urban campaign of bombings and systematic French torture that became emblematic of the war.

entities.name: French Algeria
entities.summary: Departments of France with a large settler population, ended by the war of independence.

entities.name: French Conquest of Algeria
entities.summary: Long, violent conquest and settlement, resisted by Abd al-Qadir and Kabyle revolts.

entities.name: Regency of Algiers
entities.summary: Ottoman-aligned corsair state on the Barbary coast, conquered by France in 1830.

entities.name: Angolan Civil War
entities.summary: Cold War proxy war among the MPLA, UNITA and FNLA with Cuban and South African intervention.

entities.name: Aswan High Dam
entities.summary: Soviet-aided dam that controlled the Nile flood, created Lake Nasser and displaced Nubian communities.

entities.name: British Occupation of Egypt
entities.summary: Occupation after the Urabi revolt, formalised as a protectorate in 1914 and ended by the 1956 evacuation.

entities.name: Egyptian Revolution of 1952
entities.summary: Free Officers' coup that deposed Farouk and brought Nasser to power.

entities.name: Egyptian Revolution of 2011
entities.summary: Eighteen days of protest centred on Tahrir Square that forced Mubarak's resignation.

entities.name: French Invasion of Egypt
entities.summary: Napoleon's campaign that shattered Mamluk power, produced the Description de l'Egypte and ended in British-Ottoman victory.

entities.name: Khedivate of Egypt
entities.summary: Autonomous Ottoman khedivate that built the Suez Canal, went bankrupt and fell under British control.

entities.name: Kingdom of Egypt
entities.summary: Nominally independent monarchy under Fuad I and Farouk, dominated by Britain and ended by revolution.

entities.name: Presidency of Hosni Mubarak
entities.summary: Thirty years of authoritarian stability, ended by the Tahrir Square uprising.

entities.name: Rule of Muhammad Ali of Egypt
entities.summary: Albanian-Ottoman officer who massacred the Mamluks and built a modern army, industry and cotton economy.

entities.name: Rule of Gamal Abdel Nasser
entities.summary: Pan-Arab leader who nationalised the canal, built the Aswan High Dam and lost the 1967 war.

entities.name: Ottoman Egypt
entities.summary: Ottoman province governed by Mamluk-Ottoman elites, briefly occupied by Napoleon in 1798.

entities.name: Presidency of Anwar Sadat
entities.summary: Launched the 1973 war, expelled Soviet advisers, made peace with Israel and was assassinated in 1981.

entities.name: Presidency of Abdel Fattah el-Sisi
entities.summary: Army chief who led the 2013 coup and has ruled since 2014 with severe restrictions on dissent.

entities.name: Opening of the Suez Canal
entities.summary: Waterway linking the Mediterranean and Red Sea, transforming global trade and Egypt's strategic value.

entities.name: Suez Crisis
entities.summary: British, French and Israeli attack on Egypt after Nasser nationalised the canal, reversed by US and Soviet pressure.

entities.name: United Arab Republic
entities.summary: Short-lived union of Egypt and Syria under Nasser, dissolved by a Syrian coup.

entities.name: Asante Empire
entities.summary: Akan gold and trading empire centred on Kumasi, annexed by Britain after five wars.

entities.name: Gold Coast
entities.summary: British colony built on gold, cocoa and the conquest of Asante, first in sub-Saharan Africa to independence.

entities.name: Rule of Kwame Nkrumah
entities.summary: Pan-Africanist founding leader who built the Akosombo Dam and was overthrown by a coup in 1966.

entities.name: East Africa Protectorate and Kenya Colony
entities.summary: British colony of settler highlands, the Uganda railway and land alienation from the Kikuyu and Maasai.

entities.name: Rule of Jomo Kenyatta
entities.summary: Founding leader who pursued capitalist development and centralised power in KANU.

entities.name: Mau Mau Uprising
entities.summary: Kikuyu-led rebellion met by mass detention camps and emergency rule, hastening independence.

entities.name: Rule of Daniel arap Moi
entities.summary: Twenty-four-year one-party then multiparty presidency marked by patronage and repression.

entities.name: Liberian Civil Wars
entities.summary: Two wars involving Charles Taylor that killed about 250,000 and destabilised the region.

entities.name: Kingdom of Madagascar
entities.summary: Merina kingdom that unified most of the island before French conquest.

entities.name: Mali War
entities.summary: Tuareg and jihadist rebellion, French intervention and successive military coups.

entities.name: Mozambican Civil War
entities.summary: War between FRELIMO and RENAMO, backed by Rhodesia and South Africa, with about a million deaths.

entities.name: German South West Africa
entities.summary: German colony where the Herero and Nama genocide of 1904-08 killed the majority of both peoples.

entities.name: Herero and Nama Genocide
entities.summary: German extermination campaign widely regarded as the twentieth century's first genocide.

entities.name: South West Africa under South African Rule
entities.summary: South African administration that extended apartheid and fought SWAPO's liberation war.

entities.name: Rule of Paul Kagame
entities.summary: RPF leader, president since 2000, credited with development and criticised for authoritarianism.

entities.name: Kingdom of Rwanda
entities.summary: Tutsi-led monarchy that colonial rule reinforced before the 1959 Hutu revolution abolished it.

entities.name: Rwandan Civil War
entities.summary: RPF invasion and war that led to the Arusha Accords and then to genocide.

entities.name: Rwandan Genocide
entities.summary: Roughly 800,000 to one million Tutsi and moderate Hutu killed in about a hundred days.

entities.name: Founding of the African National Congress
entities.summary: Formation of the movement that led the struggle against segregation and apartheid.

entities.name: Anglo-Zulu War
entities.summary: British invasion of Zululand, defeated at Isandlwana before winning at Ulundi.

entities.name: Apartheid
entities.summary: National Party system of racial classification, pass laws, bantustans and forced removals.

entities.name: British Cape Colony
entities.summary: British colony that abolished slavery, fought frontier wars and expanded north with diamonds and gold.

entities.name: Dutch Cape Colony
entities.summary: VOC settlement at the Cape whose expansion dispossessed Khoikhoi and San and imported slaves.

entities.name: Great Trek
entities.summary: Boer migration inland from the Cape that founded the Transvaal and Orange Free State republics.

entities.name: Presidency of Nelson Mandela
entities.summary: First democratically elected president, who pursued reconciliation and a new constitution.

entities.name: Presidency of Thabo Mbeki
entities.summary: Growth, African Renaissance diplomacy and controversy over HIV/AIDS policy.

entities.name: South African Mineral Revolution
entities.summary: Diamond and Witwatersrand gold discoveries that industrialised the region and created migrant labour systems.

entities.name: Natives Land Act
entities.summary: Law restricting African land ownership to about 7 percent of the country, the basis of later dispossession.

entities.name: Presidency of Cyril Ramaphosa
