entities.summary: President since 2018, facing energy shortages, corruption inquiries and coalition politics after 2024.

entities.name: Republic of South Africa (apartheid era)
entities.summary: Republic that left the Commonwealth in 1961 and faced sanctions, township revolt and regional wars.

entities.name: Rivonia Trial
entities.summary: Trial that sentenced Nelson Mandela and co-accused to life imprisonment.

entities.name: Second Anglo-Boer War
entities.summary: British conquest of the Boer republics using scorched earth and concentration camps.

entities.name: Sharpeville Massacre
entities.summary: Police killing of 69 anti-pass protesters, after which the ANC and PAC were banned and turned to armed struggle.

entities.name: South African Election of 1994
entities.summary: First universal-franchise election, won by the ANC, making Nelson Mandela president.

entities.name: South African Negotiated Transition
entities.summary: Mandela's release, unbanning of the ANC and CODESA talks that produced non-racial elections.

entities.name: South African Republic and Orange Free State
entities.summary: Boer republics of the Transvaal and Free State, annexed by Britain after the Second Anglo-Boer War.

entities.name: South African Truth and Reconciliation Commission
entities.summary: Tutu-chaired hearings on apartheid-era crimes, offering amnesty for full disclosure.

entities.name: Soweto Uprising
entities.summary: Student protest against Afrikaans instruction met with police fire, igniting a new phase of resistance.

entities.name: Union of South Africa
entities.summary: Self-governing dominion uniting four colonies with a whites-only franchise, forerunner of apartheid.

entities.name: Presidency of Jacob Zuma
entities.summary: Presidency marked by state capture scandals and economic stagnation, ended by ANC pressure.

entities.name: Anglo-Egyptian Sudan
entities.summary: Condominium administered largely by Britain, which governed the south separately.

entities.name: Rule of Omar al-Bashir
entities.summary: Islamist military ruler indicted by the ICC, overthrown by protests and the army in 2019.

entities.name: Darfur Conflict
entities.summary: Government and Janjaweed campaign against Darfuri rebels and civilians, described as genocide.

entities.name: First Sudanese Civil War
entities.summary: North-south conflict ended by the Addis Ababa Agreement's autonomy for the south.

entities.name: Mahdist State
entities.summary: Islamic state founded after the fall of Khartoum, destroyed by Kitchener at Omdurman.

entities.name: Second Sudanese Civil War
entities.summary: Twenty-two-year war with the SPLA that killed some two million and ended in a peace deal.

entities.name: Sudanese Civil War of 2023
entities.summary: War between the army and the Rapid Support Forces that produced the world's largest displacement crisis.

entities.name: Rule of Habib Bourguiba
entities.summary: Founding president who secularised law and advanced women's rights before being deposed for senility.

entities.name: French Protectorate of Tunisia
entities.summary: Protectorate established by the Treaty of Bardo, ended by Neo Destour's independence campaign.

entities.name: Husainid Beylik of Tunis
entities.summary: Dynasty that ruled Tunisia under Ottoman then French suzerainty until the republic.

entities.name: Tunisian Revolution
entities.summary: Protests after Mohamed Bouazizi's self-immolation that ousted Ben Ali and began the Arab Spring.

entities.name: Rule of Idi Amin
entities.summary: Brutal dictatorship that expelled Uganda's Asians and killed hundreds of thousands, ended by Tanzanian invasion.

entities.name: Kingdom of Buganda
entities.summary: Powerful lacustrine kingdom, the core of the Uganda Protectorate, abolished in 1966 and restored in 1993.

entities.name: Uganda Protectorate
entities.summary: British protectorate ruled indirectly through Buganda's institutions.

entities.name: Rule of Robert Mugabe
entities.summary: Thirty-seven years in power: Gukurahundi massacres, land reform and economic collapse, ended by a coup.

entities.name: Rhodesian Bush War
entities.summary: Liberation war by ZANLA and ZIPRA that forced the Lancaster House settlement.

entities.name: Rhodesian Unilateral Declaration of Independence
entities.summary: Ian Smith's white minority government declared independence, triggering sanctions and guerrilla war.

entities.name: Southern Rhodesia
entities.summary: Self-governing British settler colony named for Cecil Rhodes, based on land alienation and white minority rule.

entities.name: Rule of Siad Barre
entities.summary: Military socialist regime that fought the Ogaden War and fell to clan-based rebellion.

entities.name: Somali Civil War
entities.summary: State collapse, famine, US and UN interventions, Islamist insurgency and al-Shabaab.

entities.name: Republic of Somaliland
entities.summary: Self-declared unrecognised state in the northwest with relative stability and its own institutions.

entities.name: Mfecane
entities.summary: Period of upheaval, migration and state formation across southern Africa associated with Zulu expansion.

entities.name: Eritrean War of Independence
entities.summary: Thirty-year struggle against Ethiopian rule won by the EPLF in 1991.

entities.name: Maji Maji Rebellion
entities.summary: Mass revolt against German rule crushed by famine tactics with perhaps 250,000 deaths.

entities.name: Rule of Julius Nyerere
entities.summary: Founding president whose ujamaa villagisation failed economically but built national unity and literacy.

entities.name: Tanganyika
entities.summary: British mandate then trust territory, independent in 1961 and united with Zanzibar in 1964.

entities.name: Republic of Guinea-Bissau
entities.summary: Independent after Amilcar Cabral's PAIGC war against Portugal.

entities.name: Mali Federation
entities.summary: Short-lived union of Senegal and French Sudan that split within months of independence.

entities.name: Islamic Republic of Mauritania
entities.summary: Saharan republic independent in 1960, which formally abolished slavery only in 1981.

entities.name: Republic of Benin
entities.summary: Independent as Dahomey in 1960, Marxist from 1975 to 1990 and a pioneer of African democratic transition.

entities.name: Republic of Cote d'Ivoire
entities.summary: Cocoa-exporting republic independent in 1960 under Houphouet-Boigny, later split by civil war.

entities.name: Republic of Sierra Leone
entities.summary: Founded as a settlement for freed slaves, independent in 1961 and scarred by a diamond-fuelled civil war.

entities.name: Sierra Leone Civil War
entities.summary: Brutal war involving the RUF and blood diamonds, ended by British and UN intervention.

entities.name: Fall of the Songhai Empire
entities.summary: Moroccan musketeers defeated Songhai at Tondibi, ending the last great Sahelian empire.

entities.name: Republic of The Gambia
entities.summary: Small riverine state independent in 1965, ruled by Yahya Jammeh from 1994 to 2017.

entities.name: Western Sahara Conflict
entities.summary: Moroccan annexation after Spanish withdrawal, contested by the Polisario Front and a stalled UN referendum.

entities.name: Argentine Economic Crisis of 2001
entities.summary: Default, corralito bank freeze and five presidents in two weeks.

entities.name: Conquest of the Desert
entities.summary: Military campaigns that seized Indigenous Patagonian lands and opened them to settlement.

entities.name: Argentine Dirty War
entities.summary: Military junta's campaign of disappearances that killed up to 30,000 people.

entities.name: Argentine Declaration of Independence
entities.summary: Congress of Tucuman declared independence from Spain on 9 July 1816.

entities.name: Falklands War
entities.summary: Argentine invasion of the Falklands defeated by Britain, precipitating the junta's collapse.

entities.name: May Revolution
entities.summary: Buenos Aires cabildo abierto deposed the viceroy, beginning Argentine self-government.

entities.name: Peronism
entities.summary: Mass movement founded by Juan and Eva Peron combining labour rights, nationalism and personalist leadership.

entities.name: Rule of Juan Manuel de Rosas
entities.summary: Federalist caudillo who dominated the Argentine Confederation until defeat at Caseros.

entities.name: United Provinces of the Rio de la Plata
entities.summary: Post-revolutionary confederation that declared independence at Tucuman in 1816 amid unitarian-federalist civil war.

entities.name: Presidency of Jair Bolsonaro
entities.summary: Right-wing populist presidency marked by Amazon deforestation, COVID-19 denial and the 2023 Brasilia riot.

entities.name: First Brazilian Republic
entities.summary: Oligarchic 'coffee with milk' republic of Sao Paulo and Minas elites, ended by Vargas's revolution.

entities.name: Minas Gerais Gold Rush
entities.summary: Gold and diamond boom that shifted Brazil's centre south and funded Portuguese and British commerce.

entities.name: Golden Law
entities.summary: Abolition of slavery in Brazil, the last country in the Americas to end it.

entities.name: Brazilian Independence

entities.name: Brazilian Military Dictatorship
entities.summary: Twenty-one years of army rule with censorship, torture and the 'economic miracle', ending in a gradual opening.

entities.name: Brazilian Second Republic
entities.summary: Democratic period of developmentalism, the building of Brasilia and mounting political crisis.

entities.name: Portuguese Landing in Brazil

entities.name: Colonial Brazil
entities.summary: Portuguese colony built on sugar, gold and enslaved African labour, with its capital at Salvador then Rio.

entities.name: Dutch Brazil
entities.summary: Dutch West India Company colony in Pernambuco under Johan Maurits, expelled by Luso-Brazilian forces.

entities.name: Empire of Brazil
entities.summary: Constitutional monarchy of the Americas under Pedro I and Pedro II, which abolished slavery and fell to a coup.

entities.name: Estado Novo (Brazil)
entities.summary: Vargas's corporatist dictatorship, which nonetheless joined the Allies in 1942.

entities.name: Founding of Brasilia
entities.summary: Kubitschek's modernist capital inaugurated in the interior, designed by Costa and Niemeyer.

entities.name: Presidencies of Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva
entities.summary: Trade-unionist president 2003-2010 and again from 2023: Bolsa Familia, poverty reduction and diplomatic prominence.

entities.name: Plano Real
entities.summary: Currency stabilisation plan that ended hyperinflation and introduced the real.

entities.name: Quilombo dos Palmares
entities.summary: Large maroon polity of escaped enslaved people in Alagoas, destroyed after decades of resistance under Zumbi.

entities.name: Impeachment of Dilma Rousseff
entities.summary: Brazil's first woman president removed amid recession and the Lava Jato corruption investigation.

entities.name: Transfer of the Portuguese Court to Brazil

entities.name: United Kingdom of Portugal, Brazil and the Algarves

entities.name: Vargas Era

entities.summary: Rafael Trujillo's cult-of-personality regime, responsible for the 1937 Parsley Massacre of Haitians.

entities.summary: BC entered Confederation on the promise of a transcontinental railway.

entities.name: Canadian Indian Residential School System

entities.name: Truth and Reconciliation Commission of Canada
entities.summary: Inquiry into residential schools that documented cultural genocide against Indigenous peoples.

entities.name: Jacques Cartier's Voyages
entities.summary: Three French voyages that claimed the St Lawrence for France and named Canada.

entities.name: Constitution Act, 1982
entities.summary: Patriation of the constitution with the Charter of Rights and Freedoms, without Quebec's consent.

entities.name: Hudson's Bay Company
entities.summary: Royal-chartered fur-trade company that governed Rupert's Land until selling it to Canada in 1870.

entities.name: North-West Rebellion
entities.summary: Metis and Cree resistance led by Riel and Big Bear, defeated and followed by Riel's execution.

entities.name: Creation of Nunavut
entities.summary: New Inuit-majority territory established from the eastern Northwest Territories.

entities.summary: PEI entered Confederation in 1873, burdened by railway debt.

entities.name: Premiership of Alexander Mackenzie

entities.name: Premiership of Arthur Meighen

entities.name: Premiership of Brian Mulroney
entities.summary: Free trade with the United States, the GST, failed Meech Lake and Charlottetown accords, and anti-apartheid diplomacy.

entities.name: Premiership of Charles Tupper

entities.name: Premiership of Jean Chretien

entities.name: Premiership of John A. Macdonald

entities.summary: Conservative caretaker prime minister after Macdonald's death.

entities.name: Premiership of John Diefenbaker
entities.summary: Prairie Conservative: the Bill of Rights, Indigenous voting rights and the Avro Arrow cancellation.

entities.name: Premiership of John Thompson
entities.summary: Prime minister who codified the Criminal Code and died in office at Windsor Castle.

entities.name: Premiership of John Turner
entities.summary: Liberal prime minister for 79 days before a landslide defeat.

entities.name: Premiership of Justin Trudeau
entities.summary: Liberal prime minister: cannabis legalisation, carbon pricing, USMCA and the COVID-19 response.

entities.name: Premiership of Kim Campbell
entities.summary: Canada's first woman prime minister, in office for about four months.

entities.name: Premiership of Lester Pearson
entities.summary: Nobel peace laureate whose minority governments created medicare, the maple leaf flag and the Canada Pension Plan.

entities.name: Premiership of Mackenzie Bowell
entities.summary: Prime minister brought down by cabinet revolt over the Manitoba schools question.

entities.name: Premiership of William Lyon Mackenzie King

entities.name: Premiership of Mark Carney
entities.summary: Former central banker who became Liberal leader and prime minister in 2025.

entities.name: Premiership of Paul Martin
entities.summary: Prime minister who legalised same-sex marriage nationally and faced the sponsorship scandal.

entities.name: Premiership of Pierre Trudeau
entities.summary: Prime minister 1968-79 and 1980-84: bilingualism, multiculturalism, the October Crisis and patriation with the Charter.

entities.name: Premiership of R. B. Bennett
entities.summary: Depression-era Conservative prime minister who created the Bank of Canada and the CBC's predecessor.

entities.name: Premiership of Robert Borden
entities.summary: Wartime prime minister: conscription crisis, Union government and a separate Canadian seat at Versailles.

entities.name: Premiership of Stephen Harper
entities.summary: Conservative prime minister through the 2008 crisis, the residential schools apology and Afghan combat operations.

entities.name: Premiership of Wilfrid Laurier
entities.summary: First francophone prime minister: immigration boom, two new provinces and compromise on imperial questions.

entities.name: Province of Canada

entities.name: Apache Nations

entities.name: Cherokee Nation

entities.name: Cheyenne
entities.summary: Algonquian Plains nation of the Northern and Southern divisions, central to the Plains wars and the Sand Creek and Washita attacks.

entities.name: Chickasaw Nation

entities.name: Chinook

entities.name: Choctaw Nation

entities.name: Chumash
entities.summary: Maritime people of the southern California coast and Channel Islands, known for tomol plank canoes and shell-bead money.

entities.name: Voyages of Columbus

entities.name: Comanche Nation

entities.name: Confederate States of America

entities.name: Coronado Expedition

entities.name: Crow Nation

entities.name: De Soto Expedition

entities.name: Five Tribes of Indian Territory
entities.summary: Cherokee, Choctaw, Chickasaw, Muscogee and Seminole nations relocated to Indian Territory, later reorganised as sovereign governments in Oklahoma.

entities.summary: Continental commerce in beaver and other pelts that structured Indigenous-European relations and drove exploration.

entities.name: Hohokam

entities.name: Hopewell Tradition

entities.name: Wendat Confederacy

entities.name: Lakota (North America)

entities.name: Narragansett

entities.name: New France

entities.name: Nez Perce (North America)

entities.name: Ohlone

entities.name: Ojibwe

entities.name: Osage Nation

entities.name: Paiute

entities.name: Pawnee Nation

entities.name: Potawatomi

entities.name: Pueblo Peoples

entities.name: Founding of St. Augustine

entities.name: State of Franklin

entities.name: Vermont Republic

entities.name: Wampanoag

entities.name: Uruguayan Military Dictatorship

entities.name: Batista Regime

entities.name: Rule of Fidel Castro

entities.name: Presidency of Raul Castro

entities.name: Spanish Cuba

entities.name: Salvadoran Civil War

entities.summary: Alfredo Stroessner's anticommunist regime, the longest in 20th-century South America.

entities.summary: Communist Hungary under Rakosi then Kadar's 'goulash communism' after the crushed 1956 revolution.

entities.name: Hungarian Revolution of 1848
entities.summary: Kossuth's national revolution and war of independence, defeated by Austrian and Russian armies.

entities.name: Hungarian Revolution of 1956
entities.summary: National uprising against Soviet domination, crushed by Red Army intervention with thousands killed.

entities.name: Hungarian Soviet Republic
entities.summary: Bela Kun's 133-day communist regime, overthrown after Romanian invasion.

entities.name: Kingdom of Hungary under the Habsburgs
entities.summary: Hungarian crown held by the Habsburgs, partly Ottoman-occupied until 1699 and repeatedly in revolt.

entities.name: Ottoman Hungary
entities.summary: Central Hungary under Ottoman rule after Mohacs, recovered by the Habsburgs at Karlowitz.

entities.name: Rakoczi's War of Independence
entities.summary: Large anti-Habsburg revolt led by Francis II Rakoczi, ended by the Peace of Szatmar.

entities.name: Treaty of Trianon
entities.summary: Peace treaty that reduced Hungary to a third of its prewar territory, a lasting national grievance.

entities.name: Republic of Latvia (first period)
entities.summary: Independent Latvia between the wars, ended by Soviet annexation under the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact.

entities.name: Republic of Lithuania (first period)
entities.summary: Interwar Lithuania, which lost Vilnius to Poland and was annexed by the USSR in 1940.

entities.name: Hospitaller Malta
entities.summary: Rule of the Knights of St John, who withstood the Great Siege of 1565 and built Valletta.

entities.name: Principality and Kingdom of Montenegro
entities.summary: Independent mountain state under the Petrovic-Njegos dynasty, recognised in 1878 and merged into Yugoslavia.

entities.name: Kingdom of Romania
entities.summary: Kingdom that doubled in size as Greater Romania in 1918 and fell to communism after 1944.

entities.name: Wallachia and Moldavia
entities.summary: Ottoman tributary principalities, later under Phanariot then Russian-protected regimes, united in 1859.

entities.name: Romanian Revolution of 1989
entities.summary: Violent uprising that overthrew and executed Nicolae Ceausescu in December 1989.

entities.name: Socialist Republic of Romania
entities.summary: Communist Romania, independent-minded under Ceausescu's increasingly repressive personality cult.

entities.name: United Principalities of Romania
entities.summary: Union under Alexandru Ioan Cuza and then Carol I, independent from the Ottomans in 1878.

entities.name: First Serbian Uprising
entities.summary: Revolt under Karadjordje against Ottoman rule that began modern Serbian statehood.

entities.name: Kingdom of Serbia
entities.summary: Independent kingdom that won the Balkan Wars, suffered occupation in 1915 and became the core of Yugoslavia.

entities.name: Principality of Serbia
entities.summary: Autonomous then independent Serbian principality under the Obrenovic and Karadjordjevic houses.

entities.name: Slovenian Ten-Day War
entities.summary: Brief conflict after Slovenia's independence declaration, ending with Yugoslav withdrawal.

entities.name: Allied Occupation of Austria
entities.summary: Four-power occupation ended by the State Treaty, which restored sovereignty on condition of neutrality.

entities.name: Austrian Empire
entities.summary: Empire proclaimed by Francis II in response to Napoleon, dominant in the German Confederation until 1866.

entities.name: Federal State of Austria
entities.summary: Dollfuss and Schuschnigg's clerical-authoritarian state, ended by German annexation.

entities.name: First Austrian Republic
entities.summary: Rump Austrian republic of political violence between Social Democrats and Christian Socials.

entities.name: Metternich Era
entities.summary: Conservative order of censorship, congresses and repression of nationalism directed from Vienna.

entities.name: Silesian Wars
entities.summary: Three wars in which Prussia took and kept Silesia from Habsburg Austria.

entities.name: Slovak State
entities.summary: German client state under Jozef Tiso, which deported most Slovak Jews and faced the 1944 national uprising.

entities.name: Helvetic Republic
entities.summary: French-imposed centralised republic that replaced the cantonal confederacy.

entities.name: Old Swiss Confederacy
entities.summary: League of thirteen cantons whose independence from the Empire was recognised in 1648 and which pioneered armed neutrality.

entities.name: Sonderbund War
entities.summary: Brief civil war in which federal forces defeated a league of Catholic cantons, clearing the way for the 1848 constitution.

entities.name: Restored Swiss Confederation
entities.summary: Confederation of 22 cantons whose perpetual neutrality was guaranteed at the Congress of Vienna.

entities.name: Swiss Reformation
entities.summary: Zwingli in Zurich and later Calvin in Geneva made Switzerland a centre of Reformed Protestantism.

entities.name: Swiss Women's Suffrage
entities.summary: Federal referendum granting women the vote, among the last in Europe.

entities.name: Axis Occupation of Greece
entities.summary: German, Italian and Bulgarian occupation with famine, the destruction of Greek Jewry and mass resistance.

entities.name: First Hellenic Republic
entities.summary: Provisional revolutionary government under Kapodistrias until the powers imposed a monarchy.

entities.name: Greco-Turkish War
entities.summary: Greek invasion of Anatolia defeated by Kemal's forces, ending with the burning of Smyrna.

entities.name: Greek Civil War
entities.summary: Communist insurgency defeated by the government with British and then American support under the Truman Doctrine.

entities.name: Greek Government-Debt Crisis
entities.summary: Sovereign-debt collapse and three bailout programmes with severe austerity inside the eurozone.

entities.name: Greek Military Junta
entities.summary: Colonels' dictatorship that abolished the monarchy and fell after the Cyprus crisis.

entities.name: Greek-Turkish Population Exchange
entities.summary: Compulsory exchange under the Lausanne Convention that uprooted about 1.6 million people.

entities.name: Greek War of Independence
entities.summary: Revolt against Ottoman rule, won with British, French and Russian help at Navarino and by Russian invasion.

entities.name: Kingdom of Greece
entities.summary: Monarchy created by the great powers, which expanded through the Balkan Wars and collapsed after the Asia Minor defeat.

entities.name: Metaxas Regime
entities.summary: Authoritarian '4th of August' government that rejected Mussolini's 1940 ultimatum with 'Oxi'.

entities.name: Second Hellenic Republic
entities.summary: Interwar republic of coups and refugee resettlement, ended by the restoration of the monarchy.

entities.name: Kingdom of Poland (Congress Poland)

entities.name: Duchy of Warsaw
entities.summary: Napoleonic Polish state that revived hopes of independence and supplied troops for the Grande Armee.

entities.name: First Partition of Poland

entities.name: General Government
entities.summary: German occupation regime in central Poland, site of mass murder including the extermination camps.

entities.name: Invasion of Poland

entities.name: January Uprising
entities.summary: Largest Polish insurrection against Russia, followed by Russification and the abolition of serfdom.

entities.name: Kosciuszko Uprising
entities.summary: National insurrection led by Tadeusz Kosciuszko, defeated by Russia and Prussia.

entities.name: November Uprising
entities.summary: Polish revolt against Russian rule, crushed with the loss of the kingdom's army and constitution.

entities.name: Polish Martial Law
entities.summary: General Jaruzelski's crackdown that interned Solidarity leaders and suspended civil liberties.

entities.name: Polish People's Republic
entities.summary: Communist Poland, shaken by 1956, 1968, 1970 and 1980 protests and by martial law in 1981.

entities.name: Polish Round Table Talks
entities.summary: Negotiations that produced semi-free elections and the first non-communist government in the bloc.

entities.name: Polish-Soviet War
entities.summary: War ended by Poland's victory at the Vistula in 1920 and the Treaty of Riga.

entities.name: Second Partition of Poland
entities.summary: Russia and Prussia took further large territories after the war in defence of the 1791 constitution.

entities.name: Second Polish Republic

entities.name: Solidarity
entities.summary: Independent trade union born in Gdansk under Lech Walesa that led the peaceful end of communist rule.

entities.name: Third Partition of Poland

entities.name: Union of Lublin
entities.summary: Treaty creating a single Commonwealth with one monarch, diet and currency.

entities.name: Warsaw Ghetto Uprising
entities.summary: Jewish armed revolt against deportations to Treblinka, crushed with the ghetto's destruction.

entities.name: Warsaw Uprising
entities.summary: Home Army rising for 63 days, defeated while Soviet forces halted; Warsaw was razed in reprisal.

entities.name: Anglo-Irish Treaty
entities.summary: Treaty of December 1921 creating the Irish Free State as a dominion, with Northern Ireland opting out.

entities.name: Anglo-Saxon England
entities.summary: The era of Germanic-speaking kingdoms in lowland Britain, from the traditional adventus Saxonum to the Norman Conquest. The start date is received tradition, not a fixed event.

entities.name: Austrian Netherlands
entities.summary: Habsburg Austrian rule over the southern Low Countries, disrupted by the Brabant Revolution and French annexation.

entities.name: Channel Islands (Bailiwicks of Jersey and Guernsey)

entities.name: Commonwealth of England

entities.name: Dal Riata
entities.summary: Gaelic kingdom of Argyll and northern Ireland whose dynasty gave rise to the kings of Alba. Dates are received tradition.

entities.name: Gaelic Ireland
entities.summary: The network of Irish kingdoms and lordships under Gaelic law, ending with the Nine Years War and the Flight of the Earls. Dates are approximate and received.

entities.name: House of Stuart

entities.name: Interregnum

entities.name: Irish Free State
entities.summary: Dominion established by the Anglo-Irish Treaty, covering twenty-six counties, replaced by the constitution of Ireland in 1937.

entities.name: Lordship and Crown Dependency of the Isle of Man
entities.summary: Norse-Gaelic kingdom ceded to Scotland in 1266, later an English lordship and today a Crown Dependency with its own ancient parliament.

entities.name: Jacobite line of succession

entities.name: Kingdom of Deheubarth

entities.name: Kingdom of England
entities.summary: The English kingdom from AEthelstan's unification of the Anglo-Saxon realms to its merger with Scotland in the Kingdom of Great Britain in 1707.

entities.name: Kingdom of Great Britain
entities.summary: State created by the Acts of Union of 1707 uniting England and Scotland under one parliament at Westminster, until the union with Ireland in 1801.

entities.name: Kingdom of Gwynedd

entities.name: Kingdom of Ireland
entities.summary: Created by the Crown of Ireland Act of 1542, a client kingdom under the English and then British crown until the Union of 1801.

entities.name: Kingdom of Powys

entities.name: Kingdom of Scotland
entities.summary: The Scottish kingdom, from the traditional union of Picts and Gaels under Kenneth MacAlpin to the Union of 1707. The foundation date is received tradition.

entities.name: Kingdom of Strathclyde
entities.summary: Brittonic kingdom centred on Dumbarton and later Govan, absorbed into Scotland in the eleventh century. Dates are received and approximate.

entities.name: Lordship of Ireland
entities.summary: The papal-sanctioned lordship held by the kings of England after the Angevin invasion, effective authority often confined to the Pale.

entities.name: Peninsular War

entities.name: Pictland

entities.name: Principality of Wales

entities.name: Republic of Ireland
entities.summary: The sovereign Irish state under the 1937 constitution, formally declared a republic and outside the Commonwealth in 1949.

entities.name: Spanish Netherlands
entities.summary: Habsburg Spanish provinces of the southern Low Countries, roughly modern Belgium and Luxembourg.

entities.name: Sub-Roman Britain

entities.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland

entities.name: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

entities.name: United Kingdom of the Netherlands
entities.summary: Congress of Vienna state joining the Dutch and Belgian provinces under William I, split by Belgian independence.

entities.name: Wannsee Conference

entities.name: United Nations Security Council

entities.name: ANZAC Landing at Gallipoli
entities.summary: Landing of 25 April 1915 that became the founding national legend of both countries.

entities.name: Federation of Australia

entities.name: Premiership of Robert Menzies

entities.name: Republic of Palau

entities.name: Integration of the Princely States

entities.summary: Afghan victory over the Marathas that crippled the leading Indian power and eased British expansion.

entities.name: Premiership of Lee Kuan Yew

entities.name: French Protectorate of Cambodia

entities.summary: UN administration that organised elections and restored the monarchy.

entities.summary: British counterinsurgency against the Malayan Communist Party using resettlement and 'new villages'.

entities.name: Straits Settlements

entities.name: American Colonial Philippines

entities.name: Commonwealth of the Philippines
entities.summary: Transitional self-government under Manuel Quezon, interrupted by Japanese occupation.

entities.name: Presidency of Rodrigo Duterte
entities.summary: Presidency defined by a lethal anti-drug campaign and pivot toward China.

entities.name: First Philippine Republic

entities.name: Magellan's Arrival in the Philippines

entities.summary: American conquest of the islands, with an estimated 200,000 or more Filipino civilian deaths.

entities.name: Philippine Independence

entities.name: Indonesian Occupation of East Timor

entities.name: Rule of Ne Win
entities.summary: Coup leader whose Burmese Way to Socialism isolated and impoverished the country.

entities.name: Rohingya Crisis
entities.summary: Military campaigns that drove over 700,000 Rohingya into Bangladesh, alleged as genocide.

entities.name: Gulf Cooperation Council
entities.summary: Six-member Gulf political and economic union founded in 1981.

entities.name: Kingdom of Bahrain
entities.summary: Gulf island state independent in 1971 and a kingdom since 2002, host to the US Fifth Fleet.

entities.name: State of Kuwait
entities.summary: Oil-rich Gulf emirate independent from Britain in 1961, occupied by Iraq in 1990-91.

entities.name: Anglo-Russian Convention
entities.summary: Agreement dividing Persia into Russian and British spheres of influence.

entities.name: Anglo-Soviet Invasion of Iran
entities.summary: Allied occupation to secure oil and a supply corridor to the USSR, forcing Reza Shah's abdication.

entities.name: Discovery of Oil in Persia
entities.summary: Masjed Soleyman strike led to the Anglo-Persian Oil Company and a century of oil politics.

entities.name: Iran Hostage Crisis
entities.summary: 444-day seizure of the US embassy in Tehran that severed relations with Washington.

entities.name: Iran Nuclear Deal
entities.summary: JCPOA limiting Iran's nuclear programme for sanctions relief, abandoned by the United States in 2018.

entities.name: Iranian Coup of 1953
entities.summary: CIA and MI6 operation that removed Prime Minister Mosaddegh and restored the shah's power.

entities.name: Iranian Green Movement
entities.summary: Mass protests against a disputed presidential election, suppressed by security forces.

entities.name: Iranian Oil Nationalisation
entities.summary: Mosaddegh's nationalisation of the Anglo-Iranian Oil Company, met by boycott and covert action.

entities.name: Iranian Revolution
entities.summary: Mass movement that overthrew the shah and established an Islamic republic under Khomeini.

entities.name: Mahsa Amini Protests
entities.summary: Nationwide 'Woman, Life, Freedom' uprising after a young woman's death in morality police custody.

entities.name: Reign of Mohammad Reza Pahlavi
entities.summary: Last shah: oil nationalisation crisis, the 1953 coup, White Revolution, SAVAK repression and revolution.

entities.name: Persian Constitutional Revolution
entities.summary: Movement that won a constitution and the first Majlis, then was undermined by royal and foreign intervention.

entities.name: Reign of Reza Shah Pahlavi
entities.summary: Army officer turned shah who built railways, unveiled women and was deposed by the Allies in 1941.

entities.name: Russo-Persian Wars
entities.summary: Wars ending in the treaties of Gulistan and Turkmenchay, which ceded the Caucasus to Russia.

entities.name: Tobacco Protest
entities.summary: Nationwide boycott led by clerics that forced cancellation of a British tobacco monopoly.

entities.name: White Revolution
entities.summary: Shah's programme of land reform, literacy and women's suffrage that also displaced rural populations.

entities.name: Emirate of Transjordan
entities.summary: British-mandated Hashemite emirate under Abdullah I, independent as a kingdom in 1946.

entities.name: Reign of King Hussein of Jordan
entities.summary: Forty-six-year reign through the 1967 war, Black September and peace with Israel in 1994.

entities.name: Emirate of Diriyah
entities.summary: First Saudi state, founded on the alliance of Muhammad ibn Saud and Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab, crushed by Egypt.

entities.name: Seizure of the Grand Mosque
entities.summary: Two-week takeover of the Kaaba compound by militants, after which the kingdom hardened religious policy.

entities.name: Unification of Saudi Arabia
entities.summary: Ibn Saud's campaigns from the recapture of Riyadh to the proclamation of the kingdom in 1932.

entities.name: Rule of Mohammed bin Salman
entities.summary: Crown prince driving Vision 2030 reforms, the Yemen war and a crackdown on dissent.

entities.name: Reign of King Abdullah
entities.summary: Cautious reformer who expanded education and faced the Arab Spring.

entities.name: Reign of King Fahd
entities.summary: King during the Gulf War, when US troops were stationed in the kingdom, and the Basic Law of 1992.

entities.name: Reign of King Faisal
entities.summary: Modernising king who led the 1973 oil embargo; assassinated by a nephew.

entities.name: Discovery of Saudi Oil
entities.summary: Dammam strike that made Saudi Arabia the centre of world oil and founded Aramco.

entities.name: Emirate of Nejd
entities.summary: Second Saudi state, based at Riyadh, overthrown by the Rashidis.

entities.name: French Mandate for Syria and Lebanon
entities.summary: French League of Nations mandate that created the borders of modern Syria and Lebanon.

entities.name: Ottoman Syria and the Levant
entities.summary: Four centuries of Ottoman provincial rule over Syria, Lebanon, Palestine and Transjordan.

entities.name: First Republic of Armenia
entities.summary: Independent Armenia after Ottoman collapse, overwhelmed by Turkish and Soviet forces.

entities.name: Azerbaijan Democratic Republic
entities.summary: First secular democratic republic in the Muslim world, sovietised in 1920.

entities.name: Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus
entities.summary: Self-declared state recognised only by Turkey.

entities.name: Turkish Invasion of Cyprus
entities.summary: Turkish intervention after a Greek-backed coup, dividing the island and creating a northern Turkish entity.

entities.name: Democratic Republic of Georgia
entities.summary: Independent Menshevik-led Georgia, invaded and sovietised by the Red Army in 1921.

entities.name: Kingdom of Kartli-Kakheti
entities.summary: Unified eastern Georgian kingdom that sought Russian protection and was annexed by Russia in 1801.

entities.name: Rose Revolution
entities.summary: Peaceful protests that removed Eduard Shevardnadze and brought Mikheil Saakashvili to power.

entities.name: British Mandate for Mesopotamia
entities.summary: British mandate over Iraq established after the Ottoman collapse, resisted in the 1920 revolt.

entities.name: Iraq War
entities.summary: US-led invasion that toppled Saddam Hussein, followed by insurgency, sectarian civil war and occupation.

entities.name: Islamic State Caliphate
entities.summary: Jihadist proto-state that seized Mosul and Raqqa before being destroyed by coalition and local forces.

entities.name: Kingdom of Iraq
entities.summary: Hashemite kingdom independent from 1932, overthrown in the bloody 1958 revolution.

entities.name: Kurdistan Region of Iraq
entities.summary: Autonomous Kurdish region established under no-fly-zone protection and constitutionally recognised in 2005.

entities.name: Rule of Saddam Hussein
entities.summary: Ba'athist dictator: war with Iran, gassing of Kurds, invasion of Kuwait and overthrow by US-led invasion.

entities.name: Israeli Invasion of Lebanon
entities.summary: Invasion to expel the PLO, the siege of Beirut and the Sabra and Shatila massacre.

entities.name: Lebanese Civil War
entities.summary: Fifteen-year multi-sided war with Syrian and Israeli intervention, ending in the Taif Agreement.

entities.name: Emirate of Mount Lebanon
entities.summary: Autonomous Druze and Maronite emirate under Ottoman suzerainty, notably under Fakhr al-Din II.

entities.name: Mount Lebanon Mutasarrifate
entities.summary: Autonomous Christian-governed Ottoman province created after the 1860 civil war under European pressure.

entities.name: Abolition of the Ottoman Sultanate and Caliphate
entities.summary: The sultanate ended in 1922 and the caliphate in 1924, closing six centuries of Ottoman rule.

entities.name: Presidency of Mustafa Kemal Ataturk
entities.summary: Founding president who abolished the caliphate, latinised the alphabet, secularised law and enfranchised women.

entities.name: Erdogan Era
entities.summary: Prime minister then president since 2003: economic growth, Islamic conservatism, the 2016 coup attempt and executive presidency.

entities.name: Presidency of Ismet Inonu
entities.summary: Kept Turkey neutral in the Second World War and permitted the transition to multiparty democracy.

entities.name: Treaty of Lausanne
entities.summary: Settlement recognising the Turkish republic's borders and mandating population exchange with Greece.

entities.name: Turkish Coup Attempt of 2016
entities.summary: Failed military putsch followed by mass purges and a state of emergency.

entities.name: Turkish Military Coups
entities.summary: Interventions in 1960, 1971, 1980 and 1997 that repeatedly reset Turkish politics.

entities.name: Turkish War of Independence
entities.summary: Kemal's nationalist campaign against Greek, Armenian and French forces that saved Anatolian sovereignty.

entities.name: Mutawakkilite Kingdom of Yemen
entities.summary: Zaydi imamate in North Yemen, overthrown in the 1962 revolution.

entities.name: People's Democratic Republic of Yemen
entities.summary: Marxist state based at Aden after British withdrawal, merged with the north in 1990.

entities.name: Yemeni Civil War
entities.summary: Houthi takeover of Sanaa and Saudi-led intervention producing a severe humanitarian crisis.

entities.name: Premiership of David Ben-Gurion
entities.summary: Founding prime minister who built state institutions, absorbed mass immigration and led the 1956 Sinai campaign.

entities.name: Zionist Movement
entities.summary: Political movement founded at Basel by Herzl to establish a Jewish state, realised in 1948.

entities.name: Arab Revolt in Palestine
entities.summary: Palestinian rebellion against British rule and Jewish immigration, suppressed with heavy casualties.

entities.name: Balfour Declaration
entities.summary: British pledge to favour a Jewish national home in Palestine while protecting non-Jewish rights.

entities.name: First Intifada
entities.summary: Palestinian mass uprising in the occupied territories, ended by the Oslo process.

entities.name: Israeli Disengagement from Gaza
entities.summary: Israel withdrew settlers and soldiers from Gaza, which Hamas took over in 2007.

entities.name: Gaza War
entities.summary: War following the Hamas attack of 7 October 2023, with devastating destruction and casualties in Gaza.

entities.name: Mandatory Palestine
entities.summary: British League of Nations mandate under the Balfour Declaration's terms, ending in war and partition.

entities.name: Palestinian Authority
entities.summary: Interim self-governing body in the West Bank and, until 2007, Gaza.

entities.name: Palestine Liberation Organization
entities.summary: Umbrella national movement led by Yasser Arafat from 1969, recognised as the Palestinian representative.

entities.name: Second Intifada
entities.summary: Violent uprising with suicide bombings and Israeli reoccupation, followed by the separation barrier.

entities.name: United Nations Partition Plan for Palestine
entities.summary: Resolution 181 recommended Jewish and Arab states with international status for Jerusalem.

entities.name: Dhofar Rebellion
entities.summary: Leftist insurgency in southern Oman defeated with British and Iranian help.

entities.name: Rule of Bashar al-Assad
entities.summary: Presidency that met the 2011 uprising with war, chemical attacks and displacement, ending in his flight in December 2024.

entities.name: Fall of the Assad Regime
entities.summary: Rebel offensive that captured Damascus in December 2024 and ended 54 years of Assad family rule.

entities.name: Rule of Hafez al-Assad
entities.summary: Thirty years of Ba'athist Alawite-led authoritarian rule, including the 1982 Hama massacre.

entities.name: Syrian Civil War
entities.summary: Uprising turned multi-sided war with Russian, Iranian, Turkish and US involvement and over half a million dead.

entities.name: Reign of Tewodros II
entities.summary: Reunified Ethiopia after the era of princes; died resisting a British expedition at Magdala.

entities.name: Reign of Pedro I of Brazil
entities.summary: Founder of the empire who granted the 1824 constitution and abdicated to claim the Portuguese throne.

entities.name: Reign of Pedro II of Brazil
entities.summary: Long, stable reign of a scholar-emperor: the Paraguayan War, coffee expansion, abolition and deposition.

entities.name: Presidency of Lazaro Cardenas
entities.summary: Land redistribution, support for Spanish republicans and the 1938 nationalisation of oil as Pemex.

entities.name: Cristero War
entities.summary: Catholic rural rebellion against anticlerical enforcement, settled by negotiated modus vivendi.

entities.name: First Mexican Empire
entities.summary: Agustin de Iturbide's brief empire, which included Central America.

entities.name: First Mexican Republic
entities.summary: Federal republic under the 1824 constitution, riven by centralist-federalist conflict.

entities.name: Presidency of Benito Juarez
entities.summary: Zapotec liberal who led resistance to the French intervention and restored the republic.

entities.name: La Reforma
entities.summary: Liberal reforms under Juarez that curbed church and army privilege and produced the 1857 constitution.

entities.name: Mexican Constitution of 1917
entities.summary: Landmark constitution establishing land reform, labour rights and state ownership of subsoil resources.

entities.name: Mexican Democratic Transition
entities.summary: Vicente Fox's victory ended 71 years of PRI presidential rule.

entities.name: Mexican Drug War
entities.summary: Militarised campaign against cartels launched by Felipe Calderon, with well over 300,000 dead.

entities.name: Mexican Oil Expropriation
entities.summary: Cardenas nationalised foreign oil companies and created Pemex, a founding act of economic sovereignty.

entities.name: Mexican Peso Crisis
entities.summary: Currency collapse and US-led bailout known as the Tequila Crisis.

entities.name: Mexican Revolution
entities.summary: Decade of civil war involving Madero, Villa, Zapata, Carranza and Obregon, costing perhaps a million lives.

entities.name: Mexican War of Independence
entities.summary: Eleven-year struggle begun by Hidalgo's Grito de Dolores and completed by Iturbide's Plan of Iguala.

entities.name: Porfiriato
entities.summary: Porfirio Diaz's 35-year rule: railways, foreign investment and repression, ended by the Revolution.

entities.name: Presidency of Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador
entities.summary: Leftist president who built Morena's dominance and expanded social programmes and military infrastructure roles.

entities.name: Presidency of Claudia Sheinbaum
entities.summary: Mexico's first woman president, elected in 2024 as AMLO's successor.

entities.name: Rule of the Institutional Revolutionary Party
entities.summary: Single dominant party governed Mexico for 71 years under a rotating presidential system.

entities.name: War of the Reform
entities.summary: Civil war between liberals and conservatives won by Juarez's liberals.

entities.name: Era of Santa Anna
entities.summary: Antonio Lopez de Santa Anna held the presidency eleven times amid the loss of Texas and the war with the United States.

entities.name: Second Mexican Empire
entities.summary: French-imposed empire of Maximilian of Habsburg, which collapsed when France withdrew; he was executed at Queretaro.

entities.name: Spanish Conquest of the Aztec Empire
entities.summary: Cortes and Indigenous allies destroyed Tenochtitlan, beginning Spanish rule in Mesoamerica.

entities.name: Tlatelolco Massacre
entities.summary: Army killing of student protesters in Mexico City days before the Olympics.

entities.name: United Mexican States
entities.summary: Federal republic of 31 states and a capital, Latin America's second-largest economy.

entities.name: Zapatista Uprising
entities.summary: EZLN indigenous rebellion in Chiapas launched as NAFTA took effect.

entities.name: Chiricahua Apache
entities.summary: Apache band led at various times by Cochise, Victorio and Geronimo, whose resistance ended with imprisonment in Florida and Oklahoma.

entities.name: Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians
entities.summary: Federally recognised Cherokee community in western North Carolina descended from those who avoided removal.

entities.name: Bacon's Rebellion
entities.summary: Backcountry uprising in Virginia against Governor Berkeley and Indigenous neighbours, which hastened the shift to racialised slavery.

entities.name: British North America
entities.summary: English and later British colonial holdings in North America, from Jamestown to the Treaty of Paris that recognised American independence.

entities.name: Colony of Rhode Island and Providence Plantations
entities.summary: Colony founded by Roger Williams on religious liberty and separation of church and state.

entities.name: Colony of Virginia
entities.summary: Oldest of the thirteen colonies, built on tobacco, enslaved labour and the House of Burgesses.

entities.name: Connecticut Colony
entities.summary: Puritan colony governed under the Fundamental Orders, one of the earliest written constitutions in the colonies.

entities.name: Delaware Colony
entities.summary: Lower counties on the Delaware, held under Penn's proprietorship with a separate assembly from 1704.

entities.name: Dominion of New England
entities.summary: Short-lived consolidation of the northern colonies under Governor Andros, overthrown after England's Glorious Revolution.

entities.name: Arrival of the First Africans in Virginia
entities.summary: About twenty captive Africans were sold at Point Comfort, beginning African bondage in English North America.

entities.name: First Great Awakening
entities.summary: Wave of evangelical revival led by Whitefield, Edwards and Tennent that reshaped colonial religion and undermined established churches.

entities.name: French and Indian War
entities.summary: North American theatre of the Seven Years' War in which Britain and its colonists conquered New France, ended by the Treaty of Paris.

entities.name: House of Burgesses
entities.summary: First elected legislative assembly in English America, meeting in Virginia.

entities.name: Jamestown
entities.summary: First permanent English settlement in North America, on the James River in Virginia; survived starvation to become the tobacco colony's capital.

entities.name: King George's War
entities.summary: North American theatre of the War of the Austrian Succession, including the capture and return of Louisbourg.

entities.name: King Philip's War
entities.summary: Devastating war between New England colonists and Wampanoag, Narragansett and Nipmuc forces under Metacom.

entities.name: King William's War
entities.summary: First of the intercolonial wars between English and French colonists and their Indigenous allies.

entities.name: Massachusetts Bay Colony
entities.summary: Puritan colony centred on Boston founded during the Great Migration, notable for congregational churches and Harvard College.

entities.name: Mayflower Compact
entities.summary: Self-government agreement signed by Mayflower passengers before landing, an early instance of consent-based colonial rule.

entities.name: New Haven Colony
entities.summary: Strict Puritan colony on Long Island Sound, absorbed into Connecticut in 1665.

entities.name: New Netherland
entities.summary: Dutch colony on the Hudson and Delaware rivers centred on New Amsterdam, conquered by England in 1664 and ceded in 1667.

entities.name: New Sweden
entities.summary: Small Swedish colony on the lower Delaware River, absorbed by New Netherland in 1655.

entities.name: Pequot War
entities.summary: War in Connecticut in which English colonists and allies destroyed the Pequot, including the Mystic massacre.

entities.name: Plymouth Colony
entities.summary: Separatist Pilgrim colony founded after the Mayflower voyage and governed by the Mayflower Compact; merged into Massachusetts in 1691.

entities.name: Pontiac's War
entities.summary: Pan-Indigenous uprising in the Great Lakes against British rule after the French defeat, prompting the Proclamation of 1763.

entities.name: Royal Proclamation of 1763
entities.summary: British order barring colonial settlement west of the Appalachians, a grievance for land-hungry colonists.

entities.name: Province of Carolina
entities.summary: Original proprietary grant covering the later Carolinas, governed under the Fundamental Constitutions.

entities.name: Province of Georgia
entities.summary: Last of the thirteen colonies, founded by Oglethorpe as a debtors' refuge and military buffer against Spanish Florida.

entities.name: Province of Maryland
entities.summary: Proprietary colony granted to the Calverts as a Catholic refuge, home of the 1649 Act of Toleration.

entities.name: Province of Massachusetts Bay
entities.summary: Royal province combining Massachusetts Bay, Plymouth and Maine; the epicentre of revolutionary resistance.

entities.name: Province of New Hampshire
entities.summary: Northern New England colony of fishing, timber and shipbuilding, long entangled with Massachusetts.

entities.name: Province of New Jersey
entities.summary: Colony divided into East and West Jersey before reuniting as a royal province in 1702.

entities.name: Province of New York
entities.summary: Former New Netherland granted to the Duke of York, a diverse commercial colony centred on New York City.

entities.name: Province of North Carolina
entities.summary: Southern colony of small farms, naval stores and backcountry settlement, split from Carolina in 1712.

entities.name: Province of Pennsylvania
entities.summary: Quaker colony founded by William Penn on religious tolerance and fair dealing with the Lenape; Philadelphia became the largest colonial city.

entities.name: Province of South Carolina
entities.summary: Rice and indigo colony with a Black majority population, centred on Charles Town.

entities.name: Queen Anne's War
entities.summary: North American theatre of the War of the Spanish Succession, ending with British gains at Utrecht.

entities.name: Roanoke Colony
entities.summary: Failed English settlement off North Carolina whose second group of colonists vanished, remembered as the Lost Colony.

entities.name: Salem Witch Trials
entities.summary: Mass witchcraft panic in Essex County, Massachusetts, that executed twenty people and imprisoned scores more.

entities.name: Stono Rebellion
entities.summary: Largest slave revolt in the British mainland colonies, in South Carolina, followed by a harsh Negro Act.

entities.name: Thirteen Colonies
entities.summary: The British colonies on the Atlantic seaboard from New Hampshire to Georgia that united to form the United States.

entities.name: Dakota
entities.summary: Eastern Sioux peoples of Minnesota and the Dakotas, forced from Minnesota after the 1862 war.

entities.name: Beaver Wars
entities.summary: Prolonged Iroquois campaigns for control of the fur trade that shattered Huron, Erie and other nations in the Great Lakes.

entities.name: Cayuga Nation
entities.summary: Haudenosaunee nation of the Finger Lakes region of New York.

entities.name: Mohawk Nation
entities.summary: Easternmost Haudenosaunee nation, 'keepers of the eastern door', in the Mohawk Valley and later Quebec and Ontario.

entities.name: Oneida Nation
entities.summary: Haudenosaunee nation of central New York that largely sided with the Americans in the Revolution.

entities.name: Onondaga Nation
entities.summary: Haudenosaunee nation that hosts the Grand Council fire as the confederacy's capital.

entities.name: Seneca Nation
entities.summary: Largest Haudenosaunee nation, 'keepers of the western door', in western New York.

entities.name: Tuscarora Nation
entities.summary: Iroquoian nation originally of North Carolina that migrated north and became the sixth nation of the confederacy in 1722.

entities.name: Cahokia (Mississippian Phase)
entities.summary: Largest pre-Columbian city north of Mexico, near modern St. Louis, with Monks Mound and perhaps 15,000-20,000 residents at its height.

entities.name: Long Walk of the Navajo
entities.summary: Forced march of thousands of Navajo to Bosque Redondo internment, where many died before the 1868 treaty allowed return.

entities.name: Founding of Quebec City
entities.summary: Samuel de Champlain established the habitation at Quebec, the permanent base of New France.

entities.name: Anglo-Powhatan Wars
entities.summary: Three wars between Virginia colonists and the Powhatan that ended Powhatan independence and confined survivors to reservations.

entities.name: Acoma Pueblo (North America)
entities.summary: Mesa-top Pueblo community in New Mexico, among the oldest continuously inhabited places in the United States.

entities.name: Hopi
entities.summary: Pueblo nation of northern Arizona with continuously inhabited villages including Oraibi, one of the oldest settlements in North America.

entities.name: Pueblo Revolt
entities.summary: Coordinated uprising led by Pope that expelled the Spanish from New Mexico for twelve years.

entities.name: Zuni (North America)
entities.summary: Pueblo nation of western New Mexico with a distinct language, targeted by Coronado's 1540 expedition.

entities.name: Battle of the Alamo
entities.summary: Thirteen-day siege in San Antonio in which Santa Anna's army killed the entire Texian garrison, creating a rallying cry.

entities.name: Abolitionist Movement
entities.summary: Campaign to end American slavery led by figures such as Garrison, Douglass, Tubman and the Grimke sisters.

entities.name: Adams-Onis Treaty
entities.summary: Treaty by which Spain ceded Florida to the United States and fixed the boundary of the Louisiana Purchase.

entities.name: Affordable Care Act
entities.summary: Health reform law expanding insurance coverage through exchanges, subsidies, Medicaid expansion and pre-existing condition protections.

entities.name: AIDS Crisis in the United States
entities.summary: Epidemic that killed hundreds of thousands of Americans and produced militant activism by groups such as ACT UP.

entities.name: Alaska Purchase
entities.summary: US purchase of Alaska from Russia for $7.2 million, derided at the time as 'Seward's Folly'.

entities.name: Alaska Territory
entities.summary: Organised US territory in the far northwest, admitted as the 49th state in 1959.

entities.name: Alien and Sedition Acts
entities.summary: Federalist laws restricting immigration and criminalising criticism of the government, provoking the Virginia and Kentucky Resolutions.

entities.name: American Civil War
entities.summary: War between the Union and eleven seceding slave states, the deadliest in US history, ending slavery and preserving the Union.

entities.name: American Imperialism
entities.summary: Period of overseas expansion producing colonies and protectorates in the Caribbean and Pacific, including Puerto Rico and the Philippines.

entities.name: American Indian Wars
entities.summary: Four centuries of warfare between Euro-American colonists and later the United States and Indigenous nations across the continent.

entities.name: American Revolutionary War
entities.summary: War of independence in which the thirteen colonies, aided by France, defeated Britain; ended by the Treaty of Paris recognising US sovereignty.

entities.name: Americans with Disabilities Act
entities.summary: Law barring discrimination against disabled people and mandating accessibility in employment and public life.

entities.name: Angel Island Immigration Station
entities.summary: West Coast immigration station in San Francisco Bay where Asian arrivals, especially Chinese, faced prolonged detention.

entities.name: Antebellum Period
entities.summary: Decades before the Civil War marked by market revolution, westward expansion, slavery's growth and intensifying sectional crisis.

entities.name: Apache Wars
entities.summary: Decades of conflict in the Southwest with Chiricahua and other Apache bands, ending with Geronimo's surrender.

entities.name: Nuclear Arms Race
entities.summary: US-Soviet buildup of nuclear arsenals and delivery systems, shaped by deterrence doctrine and arms control treaties.

entities.name: Articles of Confederation
entities.summary: First US constitution, ratified in 1781, creating a weak central Confederation government without power to tax; replaced by the Constitution in 1789.

entities.name: Assassination of John F. Kennedy
entities.summary: Kennedy was shot in Dallas; Lee Harvey Oswald was charged and the Warren Commission investigated.

entities.name: Assassination of Abraham Lincoln
entities.summary: John Wilkes Booth shot Lincoln at Ford's Theatre days after Appomattox, elevating Andrew Johnson.

entities.name: Banana Wars
entities.summary: Series of US military interventions and occupations in Central America and the Caribbean protecting commercial and strategic interests.

entities.name: Bay of Pigs Invasion
entities.summary: Failed CIA-sponsored landing of Cuban exiles intended to topple Fidel Castro.

entities.name: Berlin Airlift
entities.summary: US and British air supply of West Berlin during the Soviet blockade, a defining early Cold War operation.

entities.name: Bill of Rights
entities.summary: First ten amendments to the Constitution, guaranteeing speech, religion, arms, due process and other individual and state protections.

entities.name: Black Hawk War
entities.summary: Brief war in Illinois and Wisconsin against Sauk and Meskwaki led by Black Hawk, ending at Bad Axe.

entities.name: Black Lives Matter Movement
entities.summary: Movement against police violence and racial injustice that produced the largest protests in US history in 2020.

entities.name: Black Power Movement
entities.summary: Militant turn in Black politics stressing self-determination, community control and racial pride, associated with SNCC's later phase and the Black Panther Party.

entities.name: Bleeding Kansas
entities.summary: Guerrilla warfare between proslavery and free-state settlers over Kansas's status, a prelude to civil war.

entities.name: Bonus Army March
entities.summary: Veterans' encampment in Washington demanding early bonus payment, dispersed by the Army under MacArthur.

entities.name: Boston Massacre
entities.summary: British soldiers fired into a Boston crowd, killing five and giving Patriots a propaganda cause.

entities.name: Boston Tea Party
entities.summary: Sons of Liberty dumped East India Company tea into Boston Harbor, provoking the Coercive Acts.

entities.name: Boxer Rebellion Intervention
entities.summary: US participation in the eight-nation expedition that relieved the Beijing legations during the Boxer uprising.

entities.name: Massive Resistance
entities.summary: Southern campaign of school closures, private academies and interposition laws to defy Brown v. Board of Education.

entities.name: Brown v. Board of Education
entities.summary: Unanimously held racially segregated public schools unconstitutional, overturning Plessy and catalysing the civil rights movement.

entities.name: Bush v. Gore
entities.summary: Halted the Florida recount, effectively deciding the 2000 presidential election for George W. Bush.

entities.name: California Gold Rush
entities.summary: Discovery at Sutter's Mill drew some 300,000 migrants to California, accelerating statehood and devastating Native communities.

entities.name: Camp David Accords
entities.summary: Carter-brokered framework leading to the Egypt-Israel peace treaty.

entities.name: Cherokee Nation v. Georgia
entities.summary: Held the Cherokee were a 'domestic dependent nation' lacking standing to sue Georgia in the Supreme Court.
aliases: Cherokee Nation v. State of Georgia

entities.name: Chinese Exclusion Act
entities.summary: First US law barring immigration by an entire nationality, prohibiting Chinese labourers for ten years and later extended.

entities.name: Citizens United v. FEC
entities.summary: Held that corporate and union independent political spending is protected speech, reshaping campaign finance.

entities.name: Civil Rights Act of 1875
entities.summary: Reconstruction law barring discrimination in public accommodations, struck down by the Supreme Court in 1883.

entities.name: Civil Rights Act of 1964
entities.summary: Landmark law banning discrimination in public accommodations, employment and federally funded programmes.

entities.name: Civil Rights Cases
entities.summary: Struck down the Civil Rights Act of 1875, holding the Fourteenth Amendment did not reach private discrimination.

entities.name: Civil Rights Movement
entities.summary: Mass campaign against segregation and disenfranchisement, from Brown v. Board and the Montgomery bus boycott to the Civil Rights and Voting Rights Acts.

entities.name: Closing of the American Frontier
entities.summary: Census finding that no continuous frontier line remained, framed by Frederick Jackson Turner as the end of an era.

entities.name: Slavery in Colonial and Antebellum America
entities.summary: Institution of chattel slavery in what became the United States, from the first Africans in Virginia to the Thirteenth Amendment.

entities.name: Compromise of 1850
entities.summary: Package of laws admitting California free, organising Utah and New Mexico by popular sovereignty and toughening the Fugitive Slave Act.

entities.name: Compromise of 1877
entities.summary: Bargain resolving the disputed 1876 election by seating Hayes in exchange for ending federal Reconstruction.

entities.name: Constitutional Convention
entities.summary: Philadelphia convention that drafted the US Constitution, resolving representation through the Great Compromise.

entities.name: Continental Congress
entities.summary: Governing assembly of the rebelling colonies and then of the United States, spanning the First and Second Congresses and the Confederation Congress.

entities.name: 1960s Counterculture
entities.summary: Youth rebellion against mainstream norms featuring antiwar protest, rock music, communal living and drug experimentation.

entities.name: Court-Packing Plan
entities.summary: Roosevelt's failed proposal to add Supreme Court justices after the Court struck down New Deal laws.

entities.name: Creek War
entities.summary: War against the Red Stick Creeks in Alabama, won by Andrew Jackson at Horseshoe Bend and ending in massive land cessions.

entities.name: American Culture Wars
entities.summary: Ongoing political conflict over abortion, religion, sexuality, race, guns, education and national identity.

entities.name: Dakota War of 1862
entities.summary: Uprising of Dakota Sioux in Minnesota, followed by the largest mass execution in US history at Mankato.

entities.name: Dawes Act
entities.summary: Allotment policy dividing tribal lands into individual parcels, costing Indigenous nations about ninety million acres.

entities.name: Declaration of Independence
entities.summary: Continental Congress declared the thirteen colonies free of British rule in a document drafted chiefly by Thomas Jefferson.

entities.name: Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization
entities.summary: Overruled Roe v. Wade, returning abortion regulation to the states.

entities.name: Dominican Republic Intervention
entities.summary: US military intervention in the Dominican civil war, sending over 20,000 troops to prevent a feared communist takeover.

entities.name: Dot-Com Boom and Bust
entities.summary: Internet-driven stock bubble and subsequent crash that reshaped the American technology economy.

entities.name: Dred Scott v. Sandford
entities.summary: Held Black Americans could not be citizens and that Congress could not bar slavery in the territories, inflaming the sectional crisis.

entities.name: Dust Bowl
entities.summary: Severe drought and soil erosion on the southern Plains that displaced hundreds of thousands of farm families.

entities.name: Early Republic (United States)
entities.summary: Formative decades of the constitutional United States, from Washington's inauguration through the War of 1812.

entities.name: Eighteenth Amendment
entities.summary: Amendment prohibiting the manufacture, sale and transport of intoxicating liquors, implemented by the Volstead Act.

entities.name: Election of 1800
entities.summary: Contested election resolved by the House that produced the first peaceful transfer of power between parties.

entities.name: Election of 1860
entities.summary: Four-way contest won by Lincoln with under 40 percent of the vote, prompting southern secession.

entities.name: Election of 1876
entities.summary: Disputed election between Hayes and Tilden resolved by an electoral commission and the Compromise of 1877.

entities.name: Election of 1932
entities.summary: Roosevelt's landslide over Hoover that created the New Deal coalition and realigned American politics.

entities.name: Election of 2000
entities.summary: Election decided by 537 Florida votes after a recount halted by the Supreme Court.

entities.name: Ellis Island Immigration Station
entities.summary: Principal US immigrant inspection station in New York Harbor, through which about twelve million people passed.

entities.name: Emancipation Proclamation
entities.summary: Lincoln's executive order declaring enslaved people in rebel territory free and authorising Black enlistment in the Union army.

entities.name: Embargo Act of 1807
entities.summary: Jefferson's ban on American exports intended to coerce Britain and France, which devastated US commerce instead.

entities.name: American Environmental Movement
entities.summary: Wave of ecological activism sparked by Silent Spring, producing Earth Day, the EPA, the Clean Air Act and the Endangered Species Act.

entities.name: Equal Rights Amendment Campaign
entities.summary: Congressional passage and ultimately failed state ratification drive for a constitutional guarantee of sex equality.

entities.name: Era of Good Feelings
entities.summary: Period of one-party nationalism after the War of 1812, associated with James Monroe's presidency and the Monroe Doctrine.

entities.name: Erie Canal
entities.summary: 363-mile canal linking the Hudson to Lake Erie, slashing freight costs and making New York the nation's leading port.

entities.name: Ex parte Milligan
entities.summary: Held that military tribunals cannot try civilians where civil courts are open, limiting wartime executive power.

entities.name: Fair Housing Act
entities.summary: Law prohibiting discrimination in the sale, rental and financing of housing, passed days after Martin Luther King Jr.'s assassination.

entities.name: Fall of Saigon
entities.summary: North Vietnamese capture of Saigon and the chaotic US evacuation, ending the Vietnam War.

entities.name: Federal Reserve Act
entities.summary: Law creating the Federal Reserve System as the nation's central bank.

entities.name: Federal Writers' Project Slave Narratives
entities.summary: WPA programme that recorded more than 2,300 interviews with formerly enslaved people.

entities.name: Federalist Era
entities.summary: Period of Federalist Party dominance under Washington and John Adams, marked by Hamilton's financial system and partisan conflict.

entities.name: The Federalist Papers
entities.summary: Eighty-five essays by Hamilton, Madison and Jay arguing for ratification of the Constitution.

entities.name: Fifteenth Amendment
entities.summary: Amendment barring denial of the vote on grounds of race, colour or previous condition of servitude.

entities.name: First Barbary War
entities.summary: US naval campaign against Tripoli and other Barbary states over tribute demands and captured sailors.

entities.name: First Continental Congress
entities.summary: Twelve colonies met in Philadelphia to coordinate resistance to the Intolerable Acts through boycott and petition.

entities.name: First Seminole War
entities.summary: Jackson's invasion of Spanish Florida against Seminoles and maroons, which precipitated the US acquisition of Florida.

entities.name: Fourteenth Amendment
entities.summary: Amendment granting birthright citizenship and guaranteeing due process and equal protection against state action.

entities.name: Gadsden Purchase
entities.summary: Purchase of southern Arizona and New Mexico land from Mexico for a southern railroad route.

entities.name: Gettysburg Address
entities.summary: Lincoln's brief speech dedicating the Soldiers' National Cemetery, redefining the war as a struggle for democratic equality.

entities.name: GI Bill
entities.summary: Law providing veterans with college tuition, job training, unemployment pay and subsidised home loans, expanding the middle class.

entities.name: Gibbons v. Ogden
entities.summary: Established broad federal authority over interstate commerce, striking down a New York steamboat monopoly.

entities.name: Gideon v. Wainwright
entities.summary: Guaranteed appointed counsel to indigent defendants in state felony cases.

entities.name: Gilded Age
entities.summary: Era of rapid industrialisation, railroads, immigration, urban growth, machine politics and extreme inequality named after a Twain novel.

entities.name: Age of Mass Immigration
entities.summary: Arrival of over twenty million immigrants, mostly from southern and eastern Europe, processed largely at Ellis Island.

entities.name: Great Depression
entities.summary: Worst economic collapse in US history, beginning with the 1929 crash and producing mass unemployment, bank failures and the New Deal.

entities.name: Great Migration
entities.summary: Movement of about six million African Americans from the rural South to northern, midwestern and western cities.

entities.name: Great Sioux War of 1876
entities.summary: War over the Black Hills including the Lakota-Cheyenne victory at Little Bighorn and subsequent US reconquest.

entities.name: Great Society
entities.summary: Lyndon Johnson's sweeping domestic programme creating Medicare, Medicaid, federal education aid, immigration reform and civil rights enforcement.

entities.name: Gulf War
entities.summary: US-led coalition war that expelled Iraqi forces from Kuwait through Operations Desert Shield and Desert Storm.

entities.name: Harlem Renaissance
entities.summary: Flowering of African American literature, music and art centred in Harlem, with figures such as Hughes, Hurston and Ellington.

entities.name: Territory of Hawaii
entities.summary: US territory from annexation until statehood as the 50th state in 1959.

entities.name: Haymarket Affair
entities.summary: Chicago rally bombing and mass trial that set back the eight-hour movement and became a global labour symbol.

entities.name: World War II Home Front
entities.summary: Wartime mobilisation of the US economy and society, with rationing, war bonds, women in industry and Japanese American incarceration.

entities.name: Homestead Act
entities.summary: Law granting 160 acres of public land to settlers who improved it for five years, accelerating western settlement.

entities.name: Hurricane Katrina
entities.summary: Storm that flooded New Orleans, killed over 1,800 people and exposed failures in federal and local emergency response.

entities.name: Immigration Act of 1924
entities.summary: Law imposing national-origin quotas that sharply cut southern and eastern European immigration and barred most Asians.

entities.name: Immigration and Nationality Act of 1965
entities.summary: Law abolishing national-origin quotas and reshaping the sources of American immigration.

entities.name: Impeachment of Andrew Johnson
entities.summary: First presidential impeachment, over violation of the Tenure of Office Act; Johnson survived by one Senate vote.

entities.name: Impeachment of Bill Clinton
entities.summary: House impeachment for perjury and obstruction arising from the Lewinsky investigation; the Senate acquitted him.

entities.name: Impeachments of Donald Trump
entities.summary: Two House impeachments, over Ukraine aid in 2019 and incitement of the January 6 attack in 2021; the Senate acquitted both times.

entities.name: Indian Citizenship Act
entities.summary: Law conferring US citizenship on all Native Americans born within the country's territory.

entities.name: Indian Removal Act
entities.summary: Law authorising treaties to relocate eastern Indigenous nations west of the Mississippi, leading to forced removals.

entities.name: Indian Reorganization Act
entities.summary: New Deal law ending allotment and restoring tribal self-government and land bases.

entities.name: Indian Self-Determination and Education Assistance Act
entities.summary: Law allowing tribes to contract and administer federal programmes themselves, ending the termination era.

entities.name: Indian Termination Policy
entities.summary: Federal effort to dissolve tribal status and relocate Native people to cities, later reversed by self-determination policy.

entities.name: Indian Territory
entities.summary: Federal territory in present-day Oklahoma set aside for removed Indigenous nations, dissolved at Oklahoma statehood.

entities.name: American Industrial Revolution
entities.summary: Shift from agrarian craft production to mechanised factory industry, from Slater's mill to steel and electricity.

entities.name: Interstate Commerce Act
entities.summary: First major federal regulation of private industry, creating the Interstate Commerce Commission to oversee railroads.

entities.name: Federal-Aid Highway Act of 1956
entities.summary: Law funding the 41,000-mile Interstate Highway System, transforming American mobility and suburban growth.

entities.name: Sunbelt Migration
entities.summary: Long shift of population, industry and political power from the Northeast and Midwest to the South and Southwest.

entities.name: Intolerable Acts
entities.summary: Punitive British laws closing Boston's port and altering Massachusetts government, which united the colonies in resistance.

entities.name: Invasion of Grenada
entities.summary: US-led invasion that removed the revolutionary government of Grenada after a coup.

entities.name: Invasion of Panama
entities.summary: US invasion that ousted and captured Manuel Noriega.

entities.name: Iran-Contra Affair
entities.summary: Scandal over secret US arms sales to Iran with proceeds diverted to Nicaraguan Contras in defiance of a congressional ban.

entities.name: Iran Hostage Crisis
entities.summary: Seizure of the US embassy in Tehran and 444-day detention of 52 Americans, which crippled Carter's presidency.

entities.name: Iraq War
entities.summary: US-led invasion that toppled Saddam Hussein, followed by insurgency, sectarian civil war and the 2007 surge.

entities.name: Jacksonian Era
entities.summary: Age of mass democracy, spoils politics, Indian removal and the Second Party System, named for Andrew Jackson.

entities.name: January 6 Capitol Attack
entities.summary: Mob storming of the Capitol seeking to block certification of the 2020 election results.

entities.name: Japanese American Incarceration
entities.summary: Forced removal and confinement of about 120,000 people of Japanese descent under Executive Order 9066.

entities.name: Jazz Age
entities.summary: Prosperous, culturally exuberant 1920s of jazz, flappers, radio, automobiles and Prohibition-era nightlife.

entities.name: Jeffersonian Era
entities.summary: Period of Democratic-Republican ascendancy featuring the Louisiana Purchase, the War of 1812 and the Era of Good Feelings.

entities.name: Jim Crow Era
entities.summary: Long period of legally enforced racial segregation and Black disenfranchisement in the South, ended by civil rights legislation.

entities.name: John Brown's Raid on Harpers Ferry
entities.summary: Abolitionist John Brown's failed attempt to spark a slave insurrection by seizing a federal armoury; his execution deepened sectional fear.

entities.name: Judiciary Act of 1789
entities.summary: Statute establishing the federal court system and the office of Attorney General.

entities.name: Kansas-Nebraska Act
entities.summary: Law repealing the Missouri Compromise line in favour of popular sovereignty, igniting Bleeding Kansas and creating the Republican Party.

entities.name: Korematsu v. United States
entities.summary: Upheld the wartime exclusion of Japanese Americans from the West Coast; repudiated by the Court in 2018.

entities.name: Kosovo Intervention
entities.summary: NATO air campaign led by the United States against Yugoslavia over the expulsion of Kosovar Albanians.

entities.name: First Ku Klux Klan
