entities.summary: Postwar white terrorist organisation that attacked Black voters and Republicans until suppressed by the Enforcement Acts.

entities.name: Second Ku Klux Klan
entities.summary: Revived mass Klan of the 1920s, nativist and anti-Catholic as well as racist, with millions of members before collapsing in scandal.

entities.name: American Labor Movement
entities.summary: Long struggle for union recognition, shorter hours and workplace safety, from the National Labor Union through the AFL-CIO.

entities.name: Lend-Lease
entities.summary: Programme supplying about $50 billion in war material to Britain, the Soviet Union and other Allies before and during US belligerency.

entities.name: Lewis and Clark Expedition
entities.summary: Corps of Discovery's overland journey to the Pacific and back, mapping the Louisiana Purchase and beyond.

entities.name: Lincoln-Douglas Debates
entities.summary: Seven Illinois Senate debates over slavery in the territories that made Lincoln a national figure.

entities.name: Lochner v. New York
entities.summary: Struck down maximum-hours legislation on freedom-of-contract grounds, defining an era of judicial resistance to regulation.

entities.name: Lost Generation
entities.summary: Cohort of American writers and expatriates disillusioned by World War I, including Hemingway and Fitzgerald.

entities.name: Louisiana Purchase
entities.summary: Acquisition of 828,000 square miles from France for about $15 million, doubling the size of the United States.

entities.name: Loving v. Virginia
entities.summary: Struck down state bans on interracial marriage as violations of equal protection and due process.

entities.name: Manifest Destiny
entities.summary: Ideology holding that the United States was destined to expand across North America, used to justify Texas annexation, Oregon and the Mexican-American War.

entities.name: Mapp v. Ohio
entities.summary: Applied the exclusionary rule for illegally seized evidence to state criminal prosecutions.

entities.name: Marbury v. Madison
entities.summary: Chief Justice Marshall's ruling establishing judicial review, the Court's power to strike down unconstitutional laws.

entities.name: Market Revolution
entities.summary: Transformation of the American economy by canals, railroads, textile mills and wage labour.

entities.name: McCarthyism
entities.summary: Senator Joseph McCarthy's aggressive and largely unsubstantiated hunt for communists in government, discredited after the 1954 Army-McCarthy hearings.

entities.name: McCulloch v. Maryland
entities.summary: Upheld the constitutionality of the national bank and broad implied federal powers while barring state taxation of federal institutions.

entities.name: McGirt v. Oklahoma
entities.summary: Supreme Court ruling that much of eastern Oklahoma remains Indian country for criminal jurisdiction purposes.

entities.name: MeToo Movement
entities.summary: Mass reckoning with sexual harassment and assault that toppled prominent figures across industries.

entities.name: Creation of Medicare and Medicaid
entities.summary: Great Society amendments to Social Security establishing federal health insurance for the elderly and poor.

entities.name: Mexican-American War
entities.summary: War with Mexico that ended in the Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo, transferring California and the Southwest to the United States.

entities.name: Miranda v. Arizona
entities.summary: Required police to warn suspects of their rights to silence and counsel before custodial interrogation.

entities.name: Missouri Compromise
entities.summary: Congressional bargain admitting Missouri as a slave state and Maine as free, and barring slavery north of 36 degrees 30 minutes in the Louisiana Territory.

entities.name: Monroe Doctrine
entities.summary: Declaration that the Americas were closed to further European colonisation, becoming a pillar of US foreign policy.

entities.name: North American Free Trade Agreement
entities.summary: Trade pact eliminating most tariffs among the United States, Canada and Mexico; replaced by the USMCA in 2020.

entities.name: Nat Turner's Rebellion
entities.summary: Slave uprising in Southampton County, Virginia, that killed about sixty whites and triggered severe repression.

entities.name: Founding of NATO
entities.summary: US-led creation of the North Atlantic Treaty Organization as a collective defence alliance against the Soviet Union.

entities.name: American Isolationism
entities.summary: Interwar retreat from European commitments, expressed in Senate rejection of the League and the Neutrality Acts.

entities.name: New Deal
entities.summary: Franklin Roosevelt's programme of relief, recovery and reform, creating Social Security, the SEC, the TVA and federal work relief agencies.

entities.name: New Left
entities.summary: Radical student and intellectual movement centred on SDS, participatory democracy and opposition to the Vietnam War.

entities.name: Nez Perce War
entities.summary: Fighting retreat of Chief Joseph's band across 1,170 miles toward Canada before surrender in the Bear Paw Mountains.

entities.name: Nineteenth Amendment
entities.summary: Amendment guaranteeing women the right to vote after a seventy-year suffrage campaign.

entities.name: Nixon's Visit to China
entities.summary: Nixon's week in Beijing that reopened US-Chinese relations after twenty-two years of estrangement.

entities.name: Resignation of Richard Nixon
entities.summary: First resignation of a US president, following the Supreme Court tapes ruling and imminent impeachment.

entities.name: Northwest Indian War
entities.summary: Conflict between the United States and a confederacy of Ohio Country nations, ended by Fallen Timbers and the Treaty of Greenville.

entities.name: Northwest Ordinance
entities.summary: Confederation Congress law organising the Northwest Territory, banning slavery there and setting the process for admitting new states.

entities.name: Nullification Crisis
entities.summary: South Carolina's attempt to void federal tariffs, defused by Jackson's Force Bill and a compromise tariff.

entities.name: Obergefell v. Hodges
entities.summary: Held that same-sex couples have a constitutional right to marry nationwide.

entities.name: US Occupation of Haiti
entities.summary: Nineteen-year Marine occupation of Haiti that reorganised its finances and provoked the Caco rebellion.

entities.name: Oklahoma Land Rush
entities.summary: Series of land runs opening former Indian Territory to non-Native settlement.

entities.name: Oregon Treaty
entities.summary: Anglo-American agreement dividing the Oregon Country at the 49th parallel.

entities.name: Pacific Railway Acts
entities.summary: Laws chartering and subsidising the first transcontinental railroad, completed at Promontory Summit in 1869.

entities.name: Construction of the Panama Canal
entities.summary: US engineering project that cut a shipping route across the isthmus after acquiring rights from newly independent Panama.

entities.name: Pancho Villa Expedition
entities.summary: Punitive expedition led by John J. Pershing into Mexico after Villa's raid on Columbus, New Mexico.

entities.name: Panic of 1837
entities.summary: Financial crisis and prolonged depression following speculation, the Specie Circular and British credit contraction.

entities.name: Panic of 1873
entities.summary: Railroad and banking collapse that began the Long Depression and undermined Reconstruction.

entities.name: Panic of 1893
entities.summary: Severe depression with mass unemployment, railroad bankruptcies and violent labour conflict.

entities.name: Philippine-American War
entities.summary: Brutal counterinsurgency against the Philippine Republic following US annexation of the islands.

entities.name: US Rule in the Philippines
entities.summary: American colonial administration of the Philippines from the Spanish cession to independence in 1946.

entities.name: Plessy v. Ferguson
entities.summary: Upheld 'separate but equal' racial segregation, constitutional cover for Jim Crow for fifty-eight years.

entities.name: Populist Movement
entities.summary: Agrarian revolt against railroads, banks and the gold standard that produced the People's Party and Bryan's 1896 campaign.

entities.name: Postwar Boom
entities.summary: Era of sustained prosperity, suburbanisation, the baby boom, the GI Bill and mass consumer culture.

entities.name: Presidency of Abraham Lincoln
entities.summary: Sixteenth president; led the Union through the Civil War, issued the Emancipation Proclamation and was assassinated days after Confederate surrender.

entities.name: Presidency of Andrew Jackson
entities.summary: Seventh president; destroyed the Second Bank, faced down South Carolina's nullification and forced Indian removal along the Trail of Tears.

entities.name: Presidency of Andrew Johnson
entities.summary: Seventeenth president; clashed bitterly with Radical Republicans over Reconstruction and was impeached and acquitted by one vote.

entities.name: Presidency of Barack Obama
entities.summary: Forty-fourth president and first African American president; enacted the Affordable Care Act and stimulus recovery and normalised relations with Cuba.

entities.name: Presidency of Benjamin Harrison
entities.summary: Twenty-third president; signed the Sherman Antitrust Act and the high McKinley Tariff and admitted six western states.

entities.name: Presidency of Bill Clinton
entities.summary: Forty-second president; presided over budget surpluses, NAFTA and welfare reform, and was impeached and acquitted in 1998-99.

entities.name: Presidency of Calvin Coolidge
entities.summary: Thirtieth president; presided over 1920s prosperity with tax cuts and minimal government activism.

entities.name: Presidency of Chester A. Arthur
entities.summary: Twenty-first president; a former spoilsman who surprised critics by signing the Pendleton Civil Service Act.

entities.name: First Presidency of Donald Trump
entities.summary: Forty-fifth president; cut taxes, reshaped the judiciary, was impeached twice and managed the initial COVID-19 response.

entities.name: Second Presidency of Donald Trump
entities.summary: Forty-seventh president; returned to office in 2025 after a non-consecutive gap, pursuing tariffs, immigration enforcement and federal restructuring.

entities.name: Presidency of Dwight D. Eisenhower
entities.summary: Thirty-fourth president; ended the Korean War, built the Interstate Highway System and sent troops to enforce desegregation at Little Rock.

entities.name: Presidency of Franklin D. Roosevelt
entities.summary: Thirty-second president and only four-term president; enacted the New Deal and led the Allied war effort until his death in April 1945.

entities.name: Presidency of Franklin Pierce
entities.summary: Fourteenth president; his support for the Kansas-Nebraska Act ignited Bleeding Kansas and shattered the Democratic coalition.

entities.name: Presidency of George H. W. Bush
entities.summary: Forty-first president; managed the end of the Cold War and German reunification and led the coalition that won the Gulf War.

entities.name: Presidency of George W. Bush
entities.summary: Forty-third president; responded to the September 11 attacks with the wars in Afghanistan and Iraq, and left office amid the financial crisis.

entities.name: Presidency of George Washington
entities.summary: First president; set precedents for the office, established the cabinet and federal finance, suppressed the Whiskey Rebellion and urged neutrality in his Farewell Address.

entities.name: Presidency of Gerald Ford
entities.summary: Thirty-eighth president and the only one never elected to either national office; pardoned Nixon and battled inflation and recession.

entities.name: First Presidency of Grover Cleveland
entities.summary: Twenty-second president; fiscally conservative Democrat who vetoed pension bills and fought tariffs before losing the 1888 electoral vote.

entities.name: Second Presidency of Grover Cleveland
entities.summary: Twenty-fourth president; the only non-consecutive second term, dominated by the Panic of 1893 and the Pullman Strike.

entities.name: Presidency of Harry S. Truman
entities.summary: Thirty-third president; authorised the atomic bombings, launched the Marshall Plan, NATO and containment, and committed forces to Korea.

entities.name: Presidency of Herbert Hoover
entities.summary: Thirty-first president; the 1929 crash and Great Depression overwhelmed his limited relief efforts, and he lost in a 1932 landslide.

entities.name: Presidency of James A. Garfield
entities.summary: Twentieth president; shot by Charles Guiteau four months into his term and died in September 1881.

entities.name: Presidency of James Buchanan
entities.summary: Fifteenth president; failed to halt sectional collapse or secession, widely ranked among the least successful presidents.

entities.name: Presidency of James K. Polk
entities.summary: Eleventh president; expansionist who settled the Oregon boundary and won the Mexican-American War, adding the Southwest and California.

entities.name: Presidency of James Madison
entities.summary: Fourth president; led the nation through the War of 1812 and the burning of Washington, then presided over postwar nationalism.

entities.name: Presidency of James Monroe
entities.summary: Fifth president; oversaw the Era of Good Feelings, the acquisition of Florida, the Missouri Compromise and the Monroe Doctrine.

entities.name: Presidency of Jimmy Carter
entities.summary: Thirty-ninth president; brokered the Camp David Accords but was hampered by stagflation, the energy crisis and the Iran hostage crisis.

entities.name: Presidency of Joe Biden
entities.summary: Forty-sixth president; passed infrastructure and climate legislation, withdrew from Afghanistan and backed Ukraine against Russia.

entities.name: Presidency of John Adams
entities.summary: Federalist second president; navigated the Quasi-War with France, signed the Alien and Sedition Acts and lost re-election in 1800.

entities.name: Presidency of John F. Kennedy
entities.summary: Thirty-fifth president; faced the Bay of Pigs and Cuban Missile Crisis, launched the Moon programme and was assassinated in Dallas.

entities.name: Presidency of John Quincy Adams
entities.summary: Sixth president, elected by the House in the disputed 1824 contest; promoted internal improvements but was blocked by Jacksonian opposition.

entities.name: Presidency of John Tyler
entities.summary: Tenth president and first to succeed on a death; expelled from the Whig Party, he secured the annexation of Texas.

entities.name: Presidency of Lyndon B. Johnson
entities.summary: Thirty-sixth president; passed the Civil Rights and Voting Rights Acts and the Great Society, but was undone by the Vietnam War.

entities.name: Presidency of Martin Van Buren
entities.summary: Eighth president; his term was consumed by the Panic of 1837 depression and the continuing Second Seminole War.

entities.name: Presidency of Millard Fillmore
entities.summary: Thirteenth president; signed the Compromise of 1850 including the Fugitive Slave Act, and opened Japan via the Perry expedition.

entities.name: Presidency of Richard Nixon
entities.summary: Thirty-seventh president; opened relations with China, pursued detente and withdrew from Vietnam before resigning over Watergate.

entities.name: Presidency of Ronald Reagan
entities.summary: Fortieth president; cut taxes, expanded the military, weathered the Iran-Contra affair and negotiated arms reductions with Gorbachev.

entities.name: Presidency of Rutherford B. Hayes
entities.summary: Nineteenth president; took office via the Compromise of 1877, withdrew federal troops from the South and pursued civil service reform.

entities.name: Presidency of Theodore Roosevelt
entities.summary: Twenty-sixth president; trust-busting Progressive who championed conservation, the Pure Food and Drug Act and the Panama Canal.

entities.name: Presidency of Thomas Jefferson
entities.summary: Third president; completed the Louisiana Purchase, sent Lewis and Clark west, fought the Barbary pirates and imposed the Embargo Act.

entities.name: Presidency of Ulysses S. Grant
entities.summary: Eighteenth president; enforced Reconstruction and prosecuted the Klan while his administration was marred by financial scandals and the Panic of 1873.

entities.name: Presidency of Warren G. Harding
entities.summary: Twenty-ninth president; promised a 'return to normalcy' and died in office in 1923 as the Teapot Dome scandal emerged.

entities.name: Presidency of William Henry Harrison
entities.summary: Ninth president; died of illness thirty-one days after inauguration, the shortest presidency in US history.

entities.name: Presidency of William Howard Taft
entities.summary: Twenty-seventh president; pursued more antitrust suits than Roosevelt but split the Republican Party and lost the 1912 election.

entities.name: Presidency of William McKinley
entities.summary: Twenty-fifth president; won the Spanish-American War, annexed Hawaii and the Philippines and was assassinated in Buffalo in 1901.

entities.name: Presidency of Woodrow Wilson
entities.summary: Twenty-eighth president; created the Federal Reserve, led the US into World War I and championed the League of Nations.

entities.name: Presidency of Zachary Taylor
entities.summary: Twelfth president; Mexican War hero who died of illness sixteen months into his term amid the crisis over slavery in the new territories.

entities.name: Presidential Reconstruction
entities.summary: Andrew Johnson's lenient restoration policy for the ex-Confederate states, which produced Black Codes and provoked congressional backlash.

entities.name: Progressive Era Amendments
entities.summary: Cluster of four amendments creating the income tax, direct senatorial election, Prohibition and women's suffrage.

entities.name: Progressive Era
entities.summary: Reform period targeting trusts, corruption, unsafe food and labour conditions, producing antitrust action, direct election of senators and suffrage momentum.

entities.name: Prohibition
entities.summary: Nationwide ban on alcoholic beverages under the Eighteenth Amendment and Volstead Act, repealed by the Twenty-first Amendment.

entities.name: Puerto Rico under US Rule
entities.summary: Caribbean island ceded by Spain in 1898, an unincorporated US territory whose residents are citizens without presidential votes.

entities.name: Pullman Strike
entities.summary: National railway boycott broken by federal troops and injunction, making Eugene Debs a socialist leader.

entities.name: Quasi-War
entities.summary: Undeclared naval war with revolutionary France in the Caribbean, ended by the Convention of 1800.

entities.name: Reagan Revolution
entities.summary: Conservative realignment of tax cuts, deregulation, military buildup and confrontation with the Soviet Union.

entities.name: Reconstruction
entities.summary: Postwar rebuilding of the South, with federal military occupation, Black political participation and the Fourteenth and Fifteenth Amendments; ended by the Compromise of 1877.

entities.name: Red Cloud's War
entities.summary: Lakota, Cheyenne and Arapaho campaign against forts on the Bozeman Trail, won at the Treaty of Fort Laramie.

entities.name: Red Power Movement
entities.summary: Native activist movement including the Alcatraz occupation, AIM and Wounded Knee 1973, which won self-determination reforms.

entities.name: Red River War
entities.summary: Army campaign that broke Comanche, Kiowa and Southern Cheyenne resistance on the southern Plains.

entities.name: First Red Scare
entities.summary: Postwar panic over anarchism and Bolshevism, marked by the Palmer Raids, mass deportations and suppression of radical labour.

entities.name: Second Red Scare
entities.summary: Cold War anticommunist campaign of loyalty oaths, blacklists and congressional investigations into alleged subversion.

entities.name: Redemption
entities.summary: Campaign by white Democratic 'Redeemers' to overthrow Reconstruction governments in the South, often by paramilitary violence.

entities.name: Regents of the University of California v. Bakke
entities.summary: Barred racial quotas in university admissions while permitting race as one factor in pursuing diversity.

entities.name: Roe v. Wade
entities.summary: Recognised a constitutional right to abortion; overruled in 2022 by Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization.

entities.name: Schenck v. United States
entities.summary: Upheld Espionage Act convictions and introduced the 'clear and present danger' test for speech.

entities.name: Secession Winter
entities.summary: Departure of eleven southern states from the Union following Lincoln's election, culminating in the firing on Fort Sumter.

entities.name: Second Barbary War
entities.summary: Short US naval expedition under Decatur that ended Algerine attacks on American shipping.

entities.name: Second Great Awakening
entities.summary: Protestant revival movement of camp meetings and reform societies that fuelled abolition, temperance and women's activism.

entities.name: Second Seminole War
entities.summary: Longest and costliest of the Indian removal wars, fought in Florida swamps against Seminoles under Osceola.

entities.name: Second-Wave Feminism
entities.summary: Women's movement for legal and economic equality, producing NOW, Title IX, Roe v. Wade and the failed Equal Rights Amendment campaign.

entities.name: Sectional Crisis
entities.summary: Escalating North-South conflict over slavery's extension, from the Wilmot Proviso to secession.

entities.name: Seneca Falls Convention
entities.summary: First US women's rights convention, which issued the Declaration of Sentiments demanding equality including the vote.

entities.name: Seventeenth Amendment
entities.summary: Amendment providing for direct popular election of United States senators.

entities.name: Shays' Rebellion
entities.summary: Debtor farmers' armed revolt in western Massachusetts that exposed the weakness of the Articles of Confederation.

entities.name: Sherman Antitrust Act
entities.summary: Landmark law outlawing monopolistic combinations and restraints of trade.

entities.name: Sixteenth Amendment
entities.summary: Amendment authorising a federal income tax without apportionment among the states.

entities.name: Social Security Act
entities.summary: New Deal law creating old-age pensions, unemployment insurance and aid to dependent children.

entities.name: Somalia Intervention
entities.summary: US humanitarian and military mission in Somalia that ended after the Battle of Mogadishu.

entities.name: Space Race
entities.summary: US-Soviet competition in spaceflight, from Sputnik through the Apollo Moon landings and Apollo-Soyuz.

entities.name: Spanish-American War
entities.summary: Brief war that expelled Spain from Cuba and gave the United States Puerto Rico, Guam and the Philippines.

entities.name: Stagflation Era
entities.summary: Decade of simultaneous high inflation and unemployment triggered by oil shocks and ended by Volcker's tight money policy.

entities.name: Stamp Act Crisis
entities.summary: Colonial resistance to Parliament's direct tax on printed materials, producing the Stamp Act Congress and repeal.

entities.name: Admission of the States
entities.summary: Process by which fifty states joined the Union, from Delaware's ratification to Alaska and Hawaii in 1959.

entities.name: Stonewall Riots
entities.summary: Uprising against a police raid on a Greenwich Village gay bar, conventionally the start of the modern LGBT rights movement.

entities.name: Temperance Movement
entities.summary: Long campaign against alcohol led by the WCTU and Anti-Saloon League, culminating in national Prohibition.

entities.name: Tet Offensive
entities.summary: Coordinated communist attacks across South Vietnam that were militarily repulsed but shattered US public confidence.

entities.name: Third Seminole War
entities.summary: Final campaign to expel remaining Seminoles from Florida.

entities.name: Thirteenth Amendment
entities.summary: Constitutional amendment abolishing slavery and involuntary servitude except as criminal punishment.

entities.name: Trail of Tears
entities.summary: Forced removals of Cherokee, Choctaw, Chickasaw, Creek and Seminole nations to Indian Territory, killing thousands en route.

entities.name: Transatlantic Slave Trade to North America
entities.summary: Forced transport of enslaved Africans to the mainland colonies and the United States, banned by federal law in 1808.

entities.name: Completion of the Transcontinental Railroad
entities.summary: Union Pacific and Central Pacific rails met at Promontory Summit, joining the coasts by rail.

entities.name: Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo
entities.summary: Treaty ending the Mexican-American War, ceding California, Nevada, Utah and more to the United States for $15 million.

entities.name: Treaty of Paris (1783)
entities.summary: Anglo-American peace treaty recognising US independence and setting borders to the Mississippi River.

entities.name: Triangle Shirtwaist Factory Fire
entities.summary: Fire that killed 146 garment workers in New York and spurred landmark workplace safety laws.

entities.name: Truman Doctrine
entities.summary: Pledge to support free peoples resisting subjugation, beginning the containment policy with aid to Greece and Turkey.

entities.name: Twenty-first Amendment
entities.summary: Amendment repealing Prohibition, the only amendment to nullify a previous one.

entities.name: Twenty-fourth Amendment
entities.summary: Amendment abolishing poll taxes in federal elections.

entities.name: Twenty-second Amendment
entities.summary: Amendment limiting presidents to two elected terms, a response to Franklin Roosevelt's four victories.

entities.name: Twenty-sixth Amendment
entities.summary: Amendment lowering the voting age to eighteen amid the Vietnam War draft.

entities.name: Publication of Uncle Tom's Cabin
entities.summary: Harriet Beecher Stowe's antislavery novel sold hundreds of thousands of copies and hardened sectional opinion.

entities.name: Underground Railroad
entities.summary: Clandestine network of routes and safe houses helping enslaved people escape to free states and Canada.

entities.name: United States v. Nixon
entities.summary: Held that executive privilege does not shield evidence in a criminal case, forcing release of the Watergate tapes.

entities.name: United States Constitution
entities.summary: Supreme law of the United States, ratified in 1788 and effective in 1789, creating a federal government of three branches.

entities.name: USA PATRIOT Act
entities.summary: Post-9/11 law greatly expanding federal surveillance, detention and financial-tracking powers.

entities.name: Utah War
entities.summary: Largely bloodless confrontation between the federal government and Mormon settlers in Utah Territory.

entities.name: Voting Rights Act of 1965
entities.summary: Law banning literacy tests and imposing federal oversight of elections in jurisdictions with histories of discrimination.

entities.name: National Labor Relations Act
entities.summary: Law guaranteeing private-sector collective bargaining and creating the National Labor Relations Board.

entities.name: Wall Street Crash of 1929
entities.summary: October stock market collapse that wiped out fortunes and signalled the onset of the Great Depression.

entities.name: Intervention against ISIS
entities.summary: US-led coalition campaign of airstrikes and advisers that destroyed the Islamic State's territorial caliphate in Iraq and Syria.

entities.name: War in Afghanistan
entities.summary: America's longest war, begun to destroy al-Qaeda and topple the Taliban and ended by the 2021 withdrawal and Taliban return.

entities.name: War of 1812
entities.summary: War with Britain over impressment, trade restrictions and western expansion; included the burning of Washington and Jackson's victory at New Orleans.

entities.name: War on Poverty
entities.summary: Johnson administration antipoverty campaign launched by the Economic Opportunity Act, creating Head Start, Job Corps, VISTA and community action agencies.

entities.name: Watergate Scandal
entities.summary: Break-in at Democratic headquarters and the Nixon administration cover-up that led to the president's resignation in August 1974.

entities.name: Westward Expansion
entities.summary: Century of US territorial and settler expansion from the Louisiana Purchase to the closing of the frontier.

entities.name: Whiskey Rebellion
entities.summary: Armed tax revolt by western Pennsylvania distillers, suppressed by a federalised militia led personally by President Washington.

entities.name: Women's Suffrage Movement
entities.summary: Campaign from Seneca Falls to the Nineteenth Amendment for women's voting rights, led by Stanton, Anthony, Catt and Paul.

entities.name: Worcester v. Georgia
entities.summary: Ruled Georgia law had no force in Cherokee territory, a decision the Jackson administration declined to enforce.

entities.name: World War I (United States)
entities.summary: US entry into the Great War, sending two million troops of the AEF to France and turning the Western Front against Germany.

entities.name: World War II (United States)
entities.summary: US involvement from Pearl Harbor to the surrender of Japan, fighting in Europe, North Africa and the Pacific and developing the atomic bomb.

entities.name: Wounded Knee Massacre
entities.summary: US cavalry killed roughly 250-300 Lakota, mostly noncombatants, at Wounded Knee Creek, conventionally closing the Indian Wars.

entities.name: British Hong Kong
entities.summary: Crown colony ceded in 1842 and leased in 1898 that became a global financial centre.

entities.name: Handover of Hong Kong
entities.summary: Transfer of sovereignty to China on 1 July 1997 under 'one country, two systems'.

entities.name: Hong Kong Protests of 2019
entities.summary: Mass movement against an extradition bill, answered by Beijing's national security law.

entities.name: Belt and Road Initiative
entities.summary: Global infrastructure and lending programme announced by Xi Jinping in 2013.

entities.name: Reform and Opening Up
entities.summary: Market reforms that lifted hundreds of millions from poverty and made China a manufacturing superpower.

entities.name: Cultural Revolution
entities.summary: Mao's mass campaign against 'revisionists' that closed schools, destroyed heritage and killed over a million.

entities.name: Deng Xiaoping Era
entities.summary: Reform and opening: household farming, special economic zones, and the Tiananmen crackdown.

entities.name: Great Leap Forward
entities.summary: Forced collectivisation and industrial campaign that caused a famine killing tens of millions.

entities.name: Hu Jintao Era
entities.summary: Rapid growth, the 2008 Beijing Olympics and stimulus after the global financial crisis.

entities.name: Jiang Zemin Era
entities.summary: Consolidation after Tiananmen, WTO accession and the Hong Kong and Macau handovers.

entities.name: Mao Era
entities.summary: Land reform, Korean War, Great Leap Forward famine and Cultural Revolution under Mao Zedong.

entities.name: One-Child Policy
entities.summary: Coercive birth-limitation programme that reshaped China's demography.

entities.name: Tiananmen Square Protests and Massacre
entities.summary: Seven weeks of pro-democracy protests ended by military force on 3-4 June 1989.

entities.name: Xi Jinping Era
entities.summary: Anti-corruption campaign, Belt and Road, term-limit abolition, Xinjiang repression and zero-COVID.

entities.name: February 28 Incident
entities.summary: Nationalist suppression of a Taiwanese uprising, followed by the White Terror.

entities.name: Japanese Taiwan
entities.summary: Fifty years of Japanese colonial rule that industrialised the island.

entities.name: Nanjing Decade
entities.summary: Decade of Nationalist state-building interrupted by communist insurgency and Japanese encroachment.

entities.name: Republic of China on Taiwan
entities.summary: Nationalist government relocated to Taipei in 1949; now a democracy claimed by the PRC.

entities.name: Taiwanese Martial Law Period
entities.summary: Thirty-eight years of one-party Kuomintang rule under martial law and the White Terror.

entities.name: Taiwanese Democratisation
entities.summary: Lifting of martial law, party competition and the first direct presidential election in 1996.

entities.name: Rule of Yuan Shikai
entities.summary: First president who dissolved parliament and briefly proclaimed himself emperor in 1916.

entities.name: Sakoku
entities.summary: Policy of closed borders permitting only limited Dutch, Chinese, Korean and Ryukyuan contact.

entities.name: Shimabara Rebellion
entities.summary: Christian and peasant revolt in Kyushu whose suppression sealed the proscription of Christianity.

entities.name: Meiji Constitution
entities.summary: Prussian-inspired constitution granting a Diet while vesting sovereignty in the emperor.

entities.name: Meiji Era
entities.summary: Reign of Emperor Meiji: abolition of the samurai class, conscription, industry, constitution and imperial expansion.

entities.name: Taisho Era
entities.summary: Reign of Emperor Taisho: party cabinets, universal male suffrage, rice riots and the 1923 Kanto earthquake.

entities.name: Gwangju Uprising
entities.summary: Pro-democracy revolt crushed by paratroopers under Chun Doo-hwan with hundreds killed.

entities.name: Rule of Kim Il-sung
entities.summary: Founding leader who built the juche system and a hereditary personality cult.

entities.name: Rule of Kim Jong-il
entities.summary: Ruled through the 1990s famine and the first nuclear test, under 'military first' policy.

entities.name: Rule of Kim Jong-un
entities.summary: Third-generation leader who expanded the nuclear and missile programmes and met US and South Korean leaders.

entities.name: June Democratic Struggle
entities.summary: Mass protests that forced direct presidential elections and the end of military rule.

entities.name: Miracle on the Han River
entities.summary: Transformation from postwar poverty to an advanced industrial economy led by chaebol conglomerates.

entities.name: North Korean Famine
entities.summary: Famine after Soviet aid ended that killed hundreds of thousands.

entities.name: Rule of Park Chung-hee
entities.summary: Military strongman who drove export-led industrialisation under the repressive Yushin system; assassinated in 1979.

entities.name: Presidency of Syngman Rhee
entities.summary: Authoritarian founding president, ousted by the April Revolution.

entities.name: Czechoslovak Coup of 1948
entities.summary: Communist seizure of power in February 1948 that ended postwar pluralism.

entities.name: Presidency of Tomas Masaryk
entities.summary: Founding president who made interwar Czechoslovakia central Europe's most durable democracy.

entities.name: Prague Spring
entities.summary: Dubcek's 'socialism with a human face', crushed by a Warsaw Pact invasion in August 1968.

entities.name: Sudeten Crisis and Annexation
entities.summary: German-speaking borderlands ceded under the Munich Agreement, followed by occupation in March 1939.

entities.name: Velvet Divorce
entities.summary: Peaceful split of Czechoslovakia into the Czech Republic and Slovakia on 1 January 1993.

entities.name: Velvet Revolution
entities.summary: Non-violent mass protests that ended communist rule and made Vaclav Havel president.

entities.name: Bismarck's Chancellorship
entities.summary: Otto von Bismarck governed the new empire, building alliances abroad and social insurance and anti-socialist laws at home.

entities.name: Reign of Wilhelm I
entities.summary: First German emperor, whose reign under Bismarck saw unification, the Kulturkampf and the first welfare state.

entities.name: Reign of Wilhelm II
entities.summary: Last German emperor: naval race, Weltpolitik, the First World War and abdication in November 1918.

entities.name: Year of the Three Emperors
entities.summary: Wilhelm I, Friedrich III and Wilhelm II all reigned in 1888; Friedrich III ruled only 99 days.

entities.name: Allied Occupation of Germany
entities.summary: Four-power division of Germany, denazification, the Nuremberg trials and the Berlin airlift, ending with two German states.

entities.name: Anschluss
entities.summary: German annexation of Austria in March 1938, endorsed by a rigged plebiscite.

entities.name: Austro-Prussian War
entities.summary: Seven Weeks' War in which Prussia's victory at Koniggratz excluded Austria from Germany.

entities.name: Berlin Blockade and Airlift
entities.summary: Soviet closure of land routes to West Berlin, defeated by an eleven-month Western airlift.

entities.name: Berlin Wall
entities.summary: Fortified barrier sealing West Berlin from 1961, the Cold War's central symbol, opened on 9 November 1989.

entities.name: Brandenburg-Prussia
entities.summary: Hohenzollern union of Brandenburg and Prussia built into a military-bureaucratic state by the Great Elector.

entities.name: Chancellorship of Angela Merkel
entities.summary: First woman chancellor; steered Germany through the eurozone crisis, the 2015 refugee influx and COVID-19.

entities.name: Chancellorship of Friedrich Merz
entities.summary: CDU chancellor from 2025 heading a coalition with the Social Democrats.

entities.name: Chancellorship of Gerhard Schroder
entities.summary: SPD-Green government: Kosovo deployment, Agenda 2010 labour reforms, refusal to join the Iraq war.

entities.name: Chancellorship of Helmut Kohl
entities.summary: Longest-serving postwar chancellor; delivered reunification in 1990 and pushed the euro at Maastricht.

entities.name: Chancellorship of Helmut Schmidt
entities.summary: Managed oil shocks, the Red Army Faction's German Autumn and NATO's missile deployment.

entities.name: Chancellorship of Konrad Adenauer
entities.summary: First West German chancellor: Western integration, NATO entry, reconciliation with France and Israel.

entities.name: Chancellorship of Kurt Georg Kiesinger
entities.summary: Led the first grand coalition of CDU and SPD.

entities.name: Chancellorship of Ludwig Erhard
entities.summary: Architect of the social market economy who succeeded Adenauer as chancellor.

entities.name: Chancellorship of Olaf Scholz
entities.summary: Led a three-party coalition through the Zeitenwende response to Russia's invasion of Ukraine and an energy crisis.

entities.name: Chancellorship of Willy Brandt
entities.summary: Social Democrat who pursued Ostpolitik, knelt at the Warsaw Ghetto memorial and won the Nobel Peace Prize.

entities.name: Confederation of the Rhine
entities.summary: Napoleonic client league of German states whose creation ended the Holy Roman Empire.

entities.name: German Democratic Republic (East Germany)
entities.summary: Communist state in the Soviet zone, ruled by the SED, dissolved when it acceded to the Federal Republic in 1990.

entities.name: Federal Republic of Germany
entities.summary: Reunified democratic Germany, the European Union's largest economy, with its capital returned to Berlin.

entities.name: Frankfurt Parliament
entities.summary: First freely elected all-German assembly; drafted a liberal constitution that Prussia's king refused.

entities.name: German Confederation
entities.summary: Loose association of 39 German states created at Vienna under Austrian presidency, dissolved after the 1866 war.

entities.name: German Reunification
entities.summary: On 3 October 1990 the GDR acceded to the Federal Republic under the Two Plus Four Treaty.

entities.name: German Revolution of 1918-19
entities.summary: Naval mutiny and workers' councils toppled the monarchy and produced the Weimar Republic amid failed communist risings.

entities.name: German Unification of 1871
entities.summary: Proclamation of the German Empire at Versailles on 18 January 1871, completing Bismarck's unification by war and diplomacy.

entities.name: Holy Roman Empire (Early Modern)
entities.summary: Loose confederation of hundreds of German states under an elected emperor, dissolved by Napoleon in 1806.

entities.name: Kingdom of Prussia
entities.summary: Hohenzollern kingdom that rose to great-power status, led German unification and dominated the German Empire.

entities.name: Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact
entities.summary: Nazi-Soviet non-aggression pact with secret protocols dividing Eastern Europe, signed days before war.

entities.name: North German Confederation
entities.summary: Prussian-dominated federal state that became the framework for the German Empire.

entities.name: Nuremberg Trials
entities.summary: International Military Tribunal that tried surviving Nazi leaders and established modern precedents for crimes against humanity.

entities.name: Treaty of Brest-Litovsk
entities.summary: Bolshevik peace with Germany that surrendered Ukraine, the Baltics and Poland, annulled in November 1918.

entities.name: Zollverein
entities.summary: Prussian-led customs union that economically integrated Germany ahead of political unification.

entities.name: Reign of Joseph II
entities.summary: Radical enlightened absolutist who abolished serfdom and issued the Patent of Toleration.

entities.name: Reign of Maria Theresa
entities.summary: Only female ruler of the Habsburg lands: survived the succession war, lost Silesia and reformed the state.

entities.name: Austro-Hungarian Compromise of 1867
entities.summary: Agreement creating the Dual Monarchy with separate Austrian and Hungarian governments under one emperor-king.

entities.name: Austro-Hungarian Annexation of Bosnia
entities.summary: Formal annexation of Bosnia-Herzegovina, inflaming Serbian nationalism and Russian rivalry.

entities.name: Reign of Charles I of Austria
entities.summary: Last Habsburg emperor, whose peace efforts failed and whose empire dissolved in 1918.

entities.name: Reign of Franz Joseph I
entities.summary: Sixty-eight-year reign spanning 1848, the Compromise of 1867, and the outbreak of the First World War.

entities.name: Peace of Augsburg
entities.summary: Settlement letting each German prince choose Lutheranism or Catholicism for his territory, cuius regio eius religio.

entities.name: Hitler's Rule of Germany
entities.summary: Adolf Hitler as chancellor and Fuhrer held dictatorial power from 1933 until his suicide in Berlin in April 1945.

entities.name: Kristallnacht
entities.summary: November 1938 pogrom that destroyed synagogues and Jewish businesses across Germany and Austria.

entities.name: Nuremberg Laws
entities.summary: Racial laws stripping German Jews of citizenship and criminalising intermarriage.

entities.name: Beer Hall Putsch
entities.summary: Hitler's failed Munich coup, after which he wrote Mein Kampf in prison.

entities.name: German Hyperinflation of 1923
entities.summary: Currency collapse that destroyed savings and discredited the young republic before the Rentenmark stabilisation.

entities.name: Constitution of 3 May 1791
entities.summary: Europe's first modern codified constitution, an attempt at reform that provoked partition.

entities.name: The Deluge
entities.summary: Swedish and Russian invasions that devastated Poland-Lithuania and began its long decline.

entities.name: Presidency of Dmitry Medvedev
entities.summary: Interim presidency with Putin as premier; the 2008 Georgia war and the financial crisis.

entities.name: Rule of Vladimir Putin
entities.summary: President from 2000 (prime minister 2008-12), centralising power, curbing media and pursuing war in Ukraine.

entities.name: Presidency of Boris Yeltsin
entities.summary: First Russian president: market shock therapy, the 1993 constitutional crisis, Chechnya and the 1998 default.

entities.name: Decembrist Revolt
entities.summary: Failed liberal officers' coup at Nicholas I's accession, followed by decades of repression.

entities.name: Emancipation of the Serfs
entities.summary: Alexander II's manifesto freeing some 23 million serfs, with land redemption payments.

entities.name: Pugachev's Rebellion
entities.summary: Massive Cossack and peasant revolt suppressed by Catherine II, hardening noble control over serfs.

entities.name: Reign of Alexander I of Russia
entities.summary: Tsar who defeated Napoleon's invasion, entered Paris and shaped the Holy Alliance at Vienna.

entities.name: Reign of Alexander II
entities.summary: Tsar-liberator who emancipated the serfs and reformed law and local government; assassinated in 1881.

entities.name: Reign of Alexander III
entities.summary: Counter-reforming tsar of Russification, pogroms and rapid railway-led industrialisation.

entities.name: Reign of Nicholas I
entities.summary: Autocracy of orthodoxy and censorship, the 'gendarme of Europe', ending in defeat in the Crimean War.

entities.name: Reign of Nicholas II
entities.summary: Last tsar: defeat by Japan, the 1905 revolution, the Duma, war in 1914 and abdication in 1917.

entities.name: Russian Revolution of 1905
entities.summary: Bloody Sunday, mass strikes and mutinies forced Nicholas II to grant the October Manifesto and a Duma.

entities.name: Andropov and Chernenko Interregnum
entities.summary: Two brief, ailing general secretaries between Brezhnev and Gorbachev.

entities.name: Brezhnev Era
entities.summary: Stagnation and stability: Prague Spring suppression, detente, oil-funded consumerism and the Afghan invasion.

entities.name: Chernobyl Disaster
entities.summary: Reactor explosion on 26 April 1986 that spread radiation across Europe and discredited Soviet secrecy.

entities.name: Gorbachev Era
entities.summary: Perestroika, glasnost and arms control that ended the Cold War and unintentionally dissolved the USSR.

entities.name: Great Patriotic War
entities.summary: Soviet war against Germany from Barbarossa to Berlin, with roughly 27 million Soviet dead.

entities.name: Great Purge
entities.summary: Stalin's terror: show trials, mass executions of some 700,000 people and destruction of the party and army leadership.

entities.name: Gulag System
entities.summary: Vast network of forced-labour camps that held millions of prisoners, wound down after Stalin's death.

entities.name: Khrushchev Era
entities.summary: De-Stalinisation, the Secret Speech, Sputnik, the Virgin Lands and the Cuban missile crisis, ending in his ouster.

entities.name: Khrushchev Thaw
entities.summary: Relative cultural and political liberalisation after the denunciation of Stalin's crimes.

entities.name: New Economic Policy
entities.summary: Partial market restoration in agriculture and small trade that revived the economy after war communism.

entities.name: August Coup
entities.summary: Failed hardline putsch against Gorbachev that accelerated the union's collapse and Yeltsin's rise.

entities.name: Soviet Collectivisation
entities.summary: Forced collectivisation of agriculture and dekulakisation, causing famine across Ukraine, Kazakhstan and Russia.

entities.name: Reign of Umberto I
entities.summary: King during colonial expansion in Eritrea and the defeat at Adwa; assassinated by an anarchist in 1900.

entities.name: Reign of Victor Emmanuel II
entities.summary: First king of united Italy, who annexed Venetia in 1866 and Rome in 1870.

entities.name: Reign of Victor Emmanuel III
entities.summary: King who took Italy into the First World War, appointed Mussolini, dismissed him in 1943 and abdicated in 1946.

entities.name: Reign of Charles III of Spain
entities.summary: Enlightened absolutist who reformed the empire, expelled the Jesuits and modernised Madrid.

entities.name: Reign of Charles II of Spain
entities.summary: Last Habsburg king of Spain, childless, whose death triggered the War of the Spanish Succession.

entities.name: Reign of Philip II of Spain
entities.summary: Height of Spanish power: Lepanto, annexation of Portugal, the Dutch Revolt and the Armada's failure.

entities.name: Reign of Philip III of Spain
entities.summary: Reign of truce with the Dutch and the expulsion of the Moriscos.

entities.name: Reign of Philip IV of Spain
entities.summary: Golden-age culture amid decline: loss of the Dutch and Portugal, Catalan revolt and defeat by France.

entities.name: Reign of Charles XII of Sweden
entities.summary: Warrior king whose victories ended at Poltava in 1709; killed besieging Fredriksten.

entities.name: Reign of George I of Greece
entities.summary: Long-reigning Danish-born king who gained the Ionian Islands, Thessaly and Macedonia; assassinated in 1913.

entities.name: Reign of Otto of Greece
entities.summary: Bavarian prince installed as first king of Greece, deposed by a military revolt.

entities.name: The Danelaw
entities.summary: The area of eastern and northern England under Danish law and settlement after the Treaty of Alfred and Guthrum, gradually reconquered by the West Saxon kings.

entities.name: The Heptarchy
entities.summary: Conventional label for the seven principal Anglo-Saxon kingdoms of Wessex, Mercia, Northumbria, Kent, East Anglia, Essex and Sussex. The scheme is a later historiographical construct.

entities.name: Kingdom of East Anglia
entities.summary: Kingdom of the North and South Folk, home of the Sutton Hoo burial and the Wuffing dynasty, later part of the Danelaw. Dates are first-attestation approximations.

entities.name: Kingdom of Essex
entities.summary: Kingdom of the East Saxons, including London for a time, absorbed by Wessex in 825. Dates are received tradition.

entities.name: Kingdom of Kent
entities.summary: Earliest recorded Anglo-Saxon kingdom, traditionally founded by Hengist, first to be converted by Augustine's mission in 597. Foundation date is received tradition.

entities.name: Kingdom of Mercia
entities.summary: Midland kingdom dominant in the eighth century under Aethelbald and Offa, absorbed into the English realm after 918. Foundation date is first-attestation rather than calendar.

entities.name: Kingdom of Northumbria
entities.summary: Northern kingdom formed by the union of Bernicia and Deira, a centre of Insular learning, later a Viking kingdom of York. Dates are received from chronicle tradition.

entities.name: Kingdom of Sussex
entities.summary: Kingdom of the South Saxons, traditionally founded by AElle, annexed by Wessex in the ninth century. Foundation date is received tradition.

entities.name: Kingdom of Wessex
entities.summary: Kingdom of the West Saxons, founded according to tradition by Cerdic and Cynric, which under Alfred and his heirs became the nucleus of England. Foundation date is received tradition.

entities.name: Viking invasions of Britain
entities.summary: Two and a half centuries of Scandinavian raiding, settlement and conquest, from Lindisfarne to Stamford Bridge. Start date received from the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle.

entities.name: Oliver Cromwell as Lord Protector
entities.summary: Head of state of the Protectorate over England, Scotland and Ireland after dissolving the Rump Parliament; refused the crown in 1657.

entities.name: Richard Cromwell as Lord Protector
entities.summary: Succeeded his father but lacked army support and resigned in May 1659, opening the way to the Restoration.

entities.name: The Protectorate
entities.summary: Constitutional regime under the Instrument of Government in which Oliver and then Richard Cromwell governed as Lord Protector.

entities.name: Bourbon Restoration
entities.summary: Constitutional monarchy under Louis XVIII and Charles X, ended by the July Revolution.

entities.name: Edict of Nantes
entities.summary: Henry IV's grant of limited toleration and fortified towns to French Protestants, revoked in 1685.

entities.name: First French Empire
entities.summary: Napoleon I's empire, dominant over continental Europe until defeat in Russia, Leipzig and finally Waterloo.

entities.name: Franco-Prussian War
entities.summary: Prussian-led German victory that destroyed the Second Empire, annexed Alsace-Lorraine and completed German unification.

entities.name: Free France
entities.summary: De Gaulle's government-in-exile and its forces, which rallied the empire and the Resistance against Vichy and Germany.

entities.name: French Colonial Empire
entities.summary: Two successive empires spanning the Americas, Africa, Indochina and the Pacific, largely dissolved between 1954 and 1962.

entities.name: French Consulate
entities.summary: Napoleon Bonaparte ruled as First Consul, creating the Bank of France, the Concordat and the Civil Code.

entities.name: French Fifth Republic
entities.summary: De Gaulle's semi-presidential republic, France's current constitutional order since 1958.

entities.name: French First Republic
entities.summary: Republic proclaimed after the fall of the monarchy, passing through Convention, Terror, Directory and Consulate before Napoleon's empire.

entities.name: French Fourth Republic
entities.summary: Unstable parliamentary republic that rebuilt the economy and began European integration but foundered on Indochina and Algeria.

entities.name: Provisional Government of the French Republic
entities.summary: De Gaulle-led government that restored republican legality, nationalised key industries and gave women the vote.

entities.name: French Second Republic
entities.summary: Republic born of the February Revolution, introduced universal male suffrage, ended by Louis-Napoleon's coup.

entities.name: French Third Republic
entities.summary: Longest-lived French republic: secular laicite laws, colonial expansion, victory in 1914-18, defeat in 1940.

entities.name: French Wars of Religion
entities.summary: Eight civil wars between Catholics and Huguenots that devastated France and ended with Henry IV's conversion and the Edict of Nantes.

entities.name: The Fronde
entities.summary: Series of aristocratic and parlementaire revolts during Louis XIV's minority that hardened his commitment to absolutism.

entities.name: The Hundred Days
entities.summary: Napoleon's return from Elba, restored rule of about a hundred days, and final defeat at Waterloo.

entities.name: July Monarchy
entities.summary: Bourgeois constitutional monarchy of Louis-Philippe, the 'citizen king', toppled in February 1848.

entities.name: July Revolution
entities.summary: Three days of Parisian fighting in July 1830 that replaced Charles X with Louis-Philippe.

entities.name: Kingdom of France (Early Modern)
entities.summary: Valois and Bourbon monarchy that centralised the French state, fought the Italian and Religious wars, and built Europe's leading absolutist power before the Revolution abolished it.

entities.name: Napoleonic Code
entities.summary: Civil Code of 1804 that codified French private law and became a model across Europe and Latin America.

entities.name: Paris Commune
entities.summary: Radical revolutionary government of Paris from March to May 1871, crushed in the semaine sanglante.

entities.name: Revocation of the Edict of Nantes
entities.summary: Edict of Fontainebleau outlawed Protestantism and drove several hundred thousand Huguenots into exile.

entities.name: Second French Empire
entities.summary: Napoleon III's authoritarian then liberal empire: Haussmann's Paris, Crimea, Italy, Mexico, and collapse at Sedan.

entities.name: St Bartholomew's Day Massacre
entities.summary: Mass killing of Huguenots in Paris and the provinces beginning 24 August 1572, a turning point in the Wars of Religion.

entities.name: Vichy France
entities.summary: Authoritarian French State under Marshal Petain that collaborated with Nazi Germany after the 1940 armistice.

entities.name: Irish Civil War
entities.summary: Conflict between pro- and anti-Treaty forces over the settlement with Britain, won by the Free State government.

entities.name: Act of Settlement
entities.summary: Vested the succession in Sophia of Hanover and her Protestant heirs and secured judicial tenure.

entities.name: Act of Supremacy
entities.summary: Statute declaring Henry VIII Supreme Head on earth of the Church of England.

entities.name: AEthelred the Unready (restored)
entities.summary: Second reign of AEthelred after Sweyn's death, ending with his own death in London amid Cnut's invasion. Regnal dates are those received from the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle and later chronicles and may be uncertain by a year or more.

entities.name: AEthelred the Unready
entities.summary: Long reign dominated by renewed Viking invasions, Danegeld payments and the St Brice's Day massacre; driven out by Sweyn Forkbeard in 1013. Regnal dates are those received from the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle and later chronicles and may be uncertain by a year or more.

entities.name: AEthelstan
entities.summary: First king to rule all England, victor at Brunanburh in 937 and a major legislator. Regnal dates are those received from the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle and later chronicles and may be uncertain by a year or more.

entities.name: Anglo-Spanish War
entities.summary: Undeclared war with Philip II including the Armada of 1588 and Drake's raids, settled by the Treaty of London.

entities.name: Founding of the Bank of England
entities.summary: Chartered to fund the war with France, creating the basis of the national debt and modern public finance.

entities.name: Bill of Rights
entities.summary: Statute limiting royal power, requiring frequent parliaments and free elections and barring Catholics from the throne.

entities.name: Black Death in England
entities.summary: Plague that killed perhaps a third to a half of the population, transforming labour, wages and land tenure.

entities.name: First Book of Common Prayer
entities.summary: Cranmer's English liturgy, introduced by the Act of Uniformity and provoking the Western Rising.

entities.name: Caroline Era
entities.summary: Reign of Charles I before the Civil War, with Laudian church reform and personal rule.

entities.name: Charles I of England
entities.summary: Rule by personal prerogative and religious policy provoked the Civil Wars; tried and executed in Whitehall in January 1649.

entities.name: Charles II of England
entities.summary: Restored Stuart king whose reign covered the Great Plague, the Fire of London, the Popish Plot and the Exclusion Crisis.

entities.name: Simon de Montfort's Parliament
entities.summary: First English parliament to include elected burgesses from the towns as well as knights of the shire.

entities.name: Dissolution of the Monasteries
entities.summary: Suppression of religious houses and transfer of their vast wealth to the Crown and its supporters.

entities.name: Domesday Book
entities.summary: William I's great survey of landholding and resources in England, the most detailed record of its kind in medieval Europe.

entities.name: Eadred
entities.summary: King who finally ended the Norse kingdom of York with the death of Eric Bloodaxe in 954. Regnal dates are those received from the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle and later chronicles and may be uncertain by a year or more.

entities.name: Eadwig
entities.summary: Teenage king whose reign saw conflict with Dunstan and the loss of Mercia and Northumbria to his brother Edgar. Regnal dates are those received from the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle and later chronicles and may be uncertain by a year or more.

entities.name: Edgar the AEtheling
entities.summary: Last male of the house of Wessex, proclaimed king in London after Hastings but never crowned; submitted to William at Berkhamsted.

entities.name: Edgar the Peaceful
entities.summary: King associated with the Benedictine reform, monetary reform and a famous imperial coronation at Bath in 973. Regnal dates are those received from the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle and later chronicles and may be uncertain by a year or more.

entities.name: Edmund I
entities.summary: Half-brother of AEthelstan who recovered the Five Boroughs from Norse rule; murdered at Pucklechurch. Regnal dates are those received from the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle and later chronicles and may be uncertain by a year or more.

entities.name: Edmund Ironside
entities.summary: Warrior son of AEthelred who fought Cnut to a partition of England at Olney and died months later. Dates are received from chronicle tradition.

entities.name: Edward I
entities.summary: Conqueror of Wales, campaigner in Scotland and summoner of the Model Parliament of 1295.

entities.name: Edward II
entities.summary: Defeated at Bannockburn and dominated by favourites; deposed in 1327 and died at Berkeley Castle.

entities.name: Edward III
entities.summary: Claimed the French throne and opened the Hundred Years War, won Crecy and Poitiers, and ruled through the Black Death.

entities.name: Edward IV (first reign)
entities.summary: Yorkist king who seized the throne after Towton and was driven out in 1470 by Warwick and the Lancastrians.

entities.name: Edward IV (second reign)
entities.summary: Restored Yorkist rule, stabilised royal finances and reigned in comparative peace until his sudden death in 1483.

entities.name: Edward the Confessor
entities.summary: Restored king of the house of Wessex, builder of Westminster Abbey, whose childless death triggered the succession crisis of 1066. Dates received from chronicles.

entities.name: Edward the Martyr
entities.summary: Young king murdered at Corfe in 978 and swiftly venerated as a saint. Regnal dates are those received from the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle and later chronicles and may be uncertain by a year or more.

entities.name: Edward V
entities.summary: Boy king deposed after eleven weeks by his uncle Richard of Gloucester; one of the Princes in the Tower, never crowned.

entities.name: Edward VI
entities.summary: Boy king under Somerset and Northumberland whose reign pushed England towards full Protestantism and the Books of Common Prayer.

entities.name: Edwardian conquest of Wales
entities.summary: Edward I's campaigns ending Welsh independence with the death of Llywelyn ap Gruffudd and a great programme of castle building.

entities.name: Elizabethan Era
entities.summary: Golden age of English drama and seafaring under Elizabeth I, with Shakespeare, Marlowe, Drake and the Armada.

entities.name: Elizabethan Religious Settlement
entities.summary: Acts of Supremacy and Uniformity establishing a Protestant church with the monarch as Supreme Governor.

entities.name: Empress Matilda
entities.summary: Daughter of Henry I who controlled England briefly in 1141 as Lady of the English but was never crowned queen.

entities.name: English Reformation
entities.summary: Break with Rome under Henry VIII, doctrinal change under Edward VI, Marian reversal and the Elizabethan settlement.

entities.name: Exclusion Crisis
entities.summary: Attempts to bar the Catholic James from the succession, giving rise to the Whig and Tory parties.

entities.name: First Barons' War
entities.summary: Rebellion against King John after Magna Carta, involving a French invasion, ended by the reissue of the charter under Henry III.

entities.name: First English Civil War
entities.summary: War between King and Parliament from Edgehill to Naseby and the surrender of Oxford.

entities.name: Glorious Revolution
entities.summary: Deposition of James II and accession of William and Mary on parliamentary terms, establishing constitutional monarchy.

entities.name: Great Fire of London
entities.summary: Fire that destroyed much of the medieval City, prompting rebuilding in brick and Wren's churches.

entities.name: Great Plague of London
entities.summary: Last major English bubonic plague epidemic, killing perhaps a quarter of London's population.

entities.name: Gunpowder Plot
entities.summary: Catholic conspiracy to blow up the Palace of Westminster, foiled on 5 November 1605.

entities.name: Habeas Corpus Act
entities.summary: Statute strengthening the writ against unlawful detention, a landmark of personal liberty.

entities.name: Harold Godwinson
entities.summary: Last crowned Anglo-Saxon king of England; won at Stamford Bridge and was killed at Hastings on 14 October 1066.

entities.name: Harold Harefoot
entities.summary: Son of Cnut who ruled England, first as regent then as king, against the claims of his half-brother Harthacnut. Dates received from chronicles.

entities.name: Harthacnut
entities.summary: Son of Cnut and Emma who united the English and Danish crowns briefly and died suddenly at Lambeth. Dates received from chronicles.

entities.name: Henry I
entities.summary: Youngest son of the Conqueror who took England and Normandy, issued the Charter of Liberties and left a disputed succession after his son's death.

entities.name: Henry II
entities.summary: First Plantagenet king, ruler of a vast Angevin domain, reformer of English common law and antagonist of Thomas Becket.

entities.name: Henry III
entities.summary: Boy king whose long reign saw baronial reform, the Provisions of Oxford, the Second Barons' War and the rebuilding of Westminster Abbey.

entities.name: Henry IV
entities.summary: First Lancastrian king, who usurped Richard II and spent his reign suppressing rebellion including Glyndwr's rising and the Percys.

entities.name: Henry V
entities.summary: Victor of Agincourt in 1415 whose Treaty of Troyes made him heir to France; died of dysentery in 1422.

entities.name: Henry VI
entities.summary: Inherited England and the French claim as an infant; his incapacity and factionalism led to the loss of France and the Wars of the Roses.

entities.name: Henry VI (restoration)
entities.summary: Brief Lancastrian restoration engineered by the Earl of Warwick, ending with Barnet, Tewkesbury and Henry's death in the Tower.

entities.name: Henry VII
entities.summary: First Tudor king, who won at Bosworth, married Elizabeth of York and restored royal finances and authority.

entities.name: High Medieval England
entities.summary: Era of Norman and Angevin consolidation, castle and cathedral building, common law, and population and town growth.

entities.name: House of Blois
entities.summary: The single-reign dynasty of King Stephen, whose disputed rule produced the Anarchy.

entities.name: House of Denmark (Knytlinga) in England
entities.summary: The Danish kings Sweyn, Cnut, Harold Harefoot and Harthacnut who ruled England as part of a North Sea empire. Dates received from chronicles.

entities.name: House of Lancaster
entities.summary: The cadet Plantagenet line of Henry IV, Henry V and Henry VI, symbolised by the red rose.

entities.name: House of Normandy
entities.summary: The Norman dynasty of William I, William II, Henry I and Stephen of Blois that transformed English land tenure, law and architecture.

entities.name: House of Orange-Nassau in Britain
entities.summary: The reign of William III, the only Dutch monarch of the British kingdoms, ruling first jointly with Mary II.

entities.name: House of Plantagenet
entities.summary: The Angevin and Plantagenet kings from Henry II to Richard III, under whom Parliament, common law and the Hundred Years War took shape.

entities.name: House of Tudor
entities.summary: The Welsh-descended dynasty of Henry VII to Elizabeth I, spanning the English Reformation and the growth of the Tudor state.

entities.name: House of Wessex
entities.summary: The Cerdicing dynasty of West Saxon kings who became kings of the English, ending with Edward the Confessor and Edgar the AEtheling. Foundation date is received tradition.

entities.name: House of York
entities.summary: The rival Plantagenet line of Edward IV, Edward V and Richard III, symbolised by the white rose.

entities.name: Hundred Years' War
entities.summary: Dynastic struggle between England and France over the French crown and Gascony, including Crecy, Poitiers, Agincourt and eventual English expulsion.

entities.name: Jacobean Era
entities.summary: Reign of James I, marked by the King James Bible, Jacobean drama and early colonisation of Virginia.

entities.name: James I of England and VI of Scotland
entities.summary: First Stuart king of England, uniting the English and Scottish crowns in his person and sponsoring the Authorised Version of the Bible.

entities.name: James II of England and VII of Scotland
entities.summary: Catholic king deposed by the Glorious Revolution after alienating the political nation; fled to France in December 1688.

entities.name: Lady Jane Grey
entities.summary: Proclaimed queen for nine to thirteen days in July 1553 under Northumberland's scheme; deposed by Mary I and later executed.

entities.name: John
entities.summary: Lost Normandy to Philip II, quarrelled with the papacy and was forced to seal Magna Carta in 1215.

entities.name: Late Medieval England
entities.summary: Period of famine, plague, French war, peasant revolt and dynastic conflict.

entities.name: Laws in Wales Acts
entities.summary: Tudor statutes annexing Wales to the realm of England, creating Welsh counties and parliamentary representation and making English the language of the courts.

entities.name: Long Parliament
entities.summary: Parliament summoned in 1640 that abolished the prerogative courts, tried Strafford and led the war against the king.

entities.name: Magna Carta
entities.summary: Charter sealed by King John at Runnymede limiting royal arbitrariness and guaranteeing due process; reissued and enshrined in later law.

entities.name: Mary I
entities.summary: Restored Roman Catholicism, married Philip II of Spain and presided over the Marian persecutions.

entities.name: Mary II
entities.summary: Joint sovereign with her husband William III after the Glorious Revolution; died of smallpox in 1694.
aliases: William II and Mary II of Scotland

entities.name: Model Parliament
entities.summary: Edward I's assembly of lords, clergy, knights and burgesses, later seen as the pattern for Parliament.

entities.name: Norman Conquest
entities.summary: William of Normandy's invasion, victory at Hastings and subsequent subjugation of England, including the Harrying of the North.

entities.name: Peasants' Revolt
entities.summary: Rising against the poll tax and serfdom led by Wat Tyler and John Ball, suppressed after the confrontation at Smithfield.

entities.name: Personal Rule of Charles I
entities.summary: Eleven years of government without Parliament, financed by ship money and marked by Laudian church policy.

entities.name: Petition of Right
entities.summary: Parliamentary statement against non-parliamentary taxation, arbitrary imprisonment and billeting.

entities.name: Philip of Spain as King of England
entities.summary: Jure uxoris king alongside Mary I under the terms of their marriage treaty; his title lapsed on her death.

entities.name: Pilgrimage of Grace
entities.summary: Northern rising against religious change and Cromwell's government, the greatest Tudor rebellion.

entities.name: Provisions of Oxford
entities.summary: Baronial reform programme imposed on Henry III establishing a council of fifteen and regular parliaments.

entities.name: Provisions of Westminster
entities.summary: Further baronial reforms addressing local administration and legal grievances.

entities.name: Trial and execution of Charles I
entities.summary: The king was tried by a High Court of Justice and beheaded outside the Banqueting House on 30 January 1649.

entities.name: Restoration of the Monarchy
entities.summary: Charles II returned under the Declaration of Breda, restoring monarchy, Lords and the Church of England.

entities.name: Restoration Era
entities.summary: Period of restored monarchy, Restoration comedy, the Royal Society, plague and fire.

entities.name: Richard I the Lionheart
entities.summary: Crusader king who spent almost his entire reign abroad on the Third Crusade and in continental war, dying at Chalus.

entities.name: Richard II
entities.summary: Faced the Peasants' Revolt as a boy and later ruled autocratically; deposed by Henry Bolingbroke in 1399.

entities.name: Richard III
entities.summary: Last Yorkist and last Plantagenet king, killed at Bosworth in 1485; his remains were found in Leicester in 2012.

entities.name: Second Barons' War
entities.summary: Rising led by Simon de Montfort against Henry III, producing the parliament of 1265 before defeat at Evesham.

entities.name: Second English Civil War
entities.summary: Royalist and Scottish risings crushed at Preston, leading directly to the king's trial.

entities.name: Somerset v Stewart
entities.summary: Mansfield's judgment that slavery had no positive law in England, freeing James Somerset.

entities.name: Statute of Labourers
entities.summary: Post-plague attempt to cap wages and bind labourers, a grievance behind the Peasants' Revolt.

entities.name: Stephen
entities.summary: Nephew of Henry I whose contested accession produced the civil war known as the Anarchy; agreed to be succeeded by Henry of Anjou.

entities.name: Sweyn Forkbeard
entities.summary: Danish king who conquered England in 1013 and reigned for a few weeks before dying at Gainsborough. Dates are received from chronicle tradition.

entities.name: The Anarchy
entities.summary: Civil war between Stephen and Empress Matilda over the succession to Henry I, ended by the Treaty of Wallingford.

entities.name: Third English Civil War
entities.summary: Campaigns in Ireland and Scotland ending with Cromwell's victory at Worcester and Charles II's flight.

entities.name: Unification of England under AEthelstan
entities.summary: AEthelstan's takeover of Northumbria created a single kingdom of the English. Date received from chronicle tradition.

entities.name: Wars of the Roses
entities.summary: Dynastic wars between Lancaster and York from St Albans to Stoke Field, ending with Tudor rule.

entities.name: William II Rufus
entities.summary: Second Norman king, quarrelsome with the Church and killed by an arrow in the New Forest.

entities.name: William III
entities.summary: Dutch stadtholder invited to rule jointly with Mary II; accepted the Bill of Rights and led the Grand Alliance against Louis XIV.

entities.name: Acts of Union 1707
entities.summary: Parallel Acts of the English and Scottish parliaments creating one Kingdom of Great Britain with a single parliament.

entities.name: British Agricultural Revolution
entities.summary: Enclosure, crop rotation, selective breeding and improved yields that fed a rapidly growing urban population.

entities.name: Anne, Queen of Great Britain
entities.summary: First sovereign of the united Kingdom of Great Britain, whose reign saw the War of the Spanish Succession and Marlborough's victories.

entities.name: Augustan Age
entities.summary: Literary and political era of Pope, Swift and Addison, and of Whig oligarchy under Walpole.

entities.name: William Cavendish, Duke of Devonshire
entities.summary: Caretaker premier of the Pitt-Devonshire ministry during the crisis after the loss of Minorca.

entities.name: Augustus FitzRoy, Duke of Grafton
entities.summary: Led a divided ministry through the Wilkes affair and rising American discontent.

entities.name: Thomas Pelham-Holles, Duke of Newcastle (first ministry)
entities.summary: Succeeded his brother Henry Pelham but proved unable to manage the opening disasters of the Seven Years War.

entities.name: Duke of Newcastle (second ministry)
entities.summary: Partnership with Pitt the Elder that produced the victories of the annus mirabilis of 1759.

entities.name: William Cavendish-Bentinck, Duke of Portland (first ministry)
entities.summary: Figurehead of the Fox-North coalition, dismissed by George III over the India Bill.

entities.name: John Stuart, Earl of Bute
entities.summary: Favourite of George III who concluded the Peace of Paris and resigned amid intense unpopularity.

entities.name: William Pitt the Elder, Earl of Chatham
entities.summary: Architect of victory in the Seven Years War who as premier was incapacitated by illness.

entities.name: William Petty, Earl of Shelburne
entities.summary: Concluded the Peace of Paris recognising American independence.

entities.name: Spencer Compton, Earl of Wilmington
entities.summary: Nominal head of the ministry that succeeded Walpole, with real power held by Carteret and the Pelhams.

entities.name: French Revolutionary Wars
entities.summary: British participation in the coalitions against revolutionary France, including naval victories at the Nile and Camperdown.

entities.name: George Grenville
entities.summary: Premier responsible for the Stamp Act and the prosecution of John Wilkes.

entities.name: George I
entities.summary: Elector of Hanover who succeeded under the Act of Settlement; his reign saw the 1715 Jacobite rising and the South Sea Bubble.

entities.name: George II
entities.summary: Last British monarch to lead troops in battle, at Dettingen in 1743; his reign covered the 1745 rising and the Seven Years War's opening.

entities.name: George III
entities.summary: Reigned through the loss of the American colonies, the union with Ireland and the wars with France, and suffered recurrent mental illness.

entities.name: Georgian Era
entities.summary: Age of the four Georges and William IV, spanning agricultural improvement, empire, industrialisation and classical architecture.

entities.name: Gordon Riots
entities.summary: Anti-Catholic riots that overwhelmed London for a week, the worst civil disorder of the century.

entities.name: Henry Pelham
entities.summary: Whig premier who ended the War of the Austrian Succession, reduced the debt and presided over the Broad Bottom ministry.

entities.name: Jacobite rising of 1715
entities.summary: The Fifteen, led by the Earl of Mar for the Old Pretender, halted at Sheriffmuir and Preston.

entities.name: Jacobite rising of 1719
entities.summary: Spanish-backed attempt defeated at Glen Shiel.

entities.name: Jacobite rising of 1745
entities.summary: The Forty-Five, in which Charles Edward Stuart advanced to Derby before annihilation at Culloden.

entities.name: Frederick North, Lord North
entities.summary: Premier throughout the American War of Independence, resigning after Yorktown.

entities.name: Charles Watson-Wentworth, Marquess of Rockingham (first ministry)
entities.summary: Whig ministry that repealed the Stamp Act while passing the Declaratory Act.

entities.name: Marquess of Rockingham (second ministry)
entities.summary: Short second ministry that opened peace negotiations with America and passed Irish legislative independence; ended with his death.

entities.name: Robert Walpole
entities.summary: Regarded as the first prime minister, Whig dominator of politics for two decades who kept Britain out of war until Jenkins' Ear.

entities.name: Septennial Act
entities.summary: Extended the maximum life of a parliament from three years to seven.

entities.name: Seven Years' War
entities.summary: Global war in which Britain took Canada, expelled France from India and emerged as the leading colonial power.

entities.name: South Sea Bubble
entities.summary: Speculative collapse in South Sea Company shares that discredited ministers and elevated Walpole.

entities.name: War of the Austrian Succession
entities.summary: British participation against France and Prussia, including George II's victory at Dettingen.

entities.name: War of the Spanish Succession
entities.summary: European war in which Marlborough won Blenheim and Ramillies, ending with the Treaty of Utrecht and the acquisition of Gibraltar.

entities.name: William Pitt the Younger (first ministry)
entities.summary: Youngest prime minister at 24, reformer of finance and administration who led Britain into the French revolutionary wars; resigned over Catholic emancipation.

entities.name: Cromwellian conquest of Ireland
entities.summary: Parliamentarian reconquest marked by the sieges of Drogheda and Wexford and massive land confiscation.

entities.name: Easter Rising
