entities.summary: Republican insurrection in Dublin, suppressed within a week, whose executions transformed Irish public opinion.

entities.name: Great Famine in Ireland
entities.summary: Potato blight and government policy produced about a million deaths and a million emigrants, halving Ireland's population over decades.

entities.name: Irish Rebellion of 1798
entities.summary: United Irishmen rising inspired by revolutionary France, suppressed with great bloodshed and leading to the Union of 1801.

entities.name: Irish War of Independence
entities.summary: Guerrilla war between the IRA and Crown forces including the Black and Tans, ended by truce and the Anglo-Irish Treaty.

entities.name: Nine Years' War in Ireland
entities.summary: Rebellion of Hugh O'Neill against Tudor rule, ending at Kinsale and Mellifont and opening the way to the Ulster plantation.

entities.name: Plantation of Ulster
entities.summary: Organised settlement of English and Scottish Protestants on confiscated Ulster land, with enduring consequences.

entities.name: Williamite War in Ireland
entities.summary: War between Jacobite and Williamite forces including the Siege of Derry, the Boyne and Aughrim, ending with the Treaty of Limerick.

entities.name: Aed
entities.summary: Brief-reigning king of Alba, killed after about a year. Dates are those received from later Scottish chronicle and king-list tradition and are not securely attested.

entities.name: Alexander I
entities.summary: King who ruled southern Scotland while his brother David held the south-west; patron of the reformed Church.

entities.name: Alexander II
entities.summary: Settled the border by the Treaty of York in 1237 and extended royal power into the west.

entities.name: Alexander III
entities.summary: Won the Hebrides by the Treaty of Perth in 1266; his death without an heir precipitated the succession crisis.

entities.name: Amlaib
entities.summary: Brother of Cuilen recorded as briefly ruling Alba in opposition to Kenneth II. Dates are those received from later Scottish chronicle and king-list tradition and are not securely attested.

entities.name: Anne, Queen of Scots
entities.summary: Last monarch of an independent Kingdom of Scotland before the Union of 1707.

entities.name: Bishops' Wars
entities.summary: Scottish Covenanter resistance to Charles I's prayer book, whose cost forced him to recall Parliament.

entities.name: Claim of Right
entities.summary: Scottish counterpart to the Bill of Rights, declaring the throne forfeited by James VII.

entities.name: Constantine I
entities.summary: King of Alba during heavy Viking pressure; killed fighting Norse raiders. Dates are those received from later Scottish chronicle and king-list tradition and are not securely attested.

entities.name: Constantine II (Kingdom of Scotland)
entities.summary: Long-reigning king who fought AEthelstan and lost at Brunanburh, later retiring to St Andrews. Dates are those received from later Scottish chronicle and king-list tradition and are not securely attested.

entities.name: Constantine III
entities.summary: Short-reigning king of Alba killed in the continuing dynastic feud. Dates are those received from later Scottish chronicle and king-list tradition and are not securely attested.

entities.name: Cuilen
entities.summary: King of Alba killed by the men of Strathclyde. Dates are those received from later Scottish chronicle and king-list tradition and are not securely attested.

entities.name: David I

entities.name: House of Bruce

entities.name: House of Dunkeld

entities.name: James IV of Scotland

entities.summary: Allied failure to force the Dardanelles, a formative event for Turkish, Australian and New Zealand identity.

entities.name: Ottoman Decline and Reform
entities.summary: Territorial losses to Russia and Austria, Janissary revolts, and the reforming reigns of Selim III and Mahmud II.

entities.name: Ottoman Empire (Early Modern)
entities.summary: Height of Ottoman power from Selim I's conquests to the Treaty of Karlowitz, spanning three continents.

entities.name: Ottoman Entry into the First World War
entities.summary: Alliance with Germany brought campaigns at Gallipoli, in Mesopotamia, the Caucasus and Palestine.

entities.name: First Ottoman Constitutional Era
entities.summary: Brief constitutional government under the 1876 Kanun-i Esasi, suspended by Abdulhamid II.

entities.name: Sultanate of Women
entities.summary: Period when imperial mothers and consorts exercised great political power in the Ottoman court.

entities.name: Reign of Abdulhamid II
entities.summary: Autocratic sultan of railways and pan-Islamism who suspended parliament and was deposed by the Young Turks.

entities.name: Reign of Mahmud II
entities.summary: Destroyed the Janissaries in 1826 and began sweeping military and administrative Westernisation.

entities.name: Reign of Selim I
entities.summary: Conquered the Mamluk sultanate and the Hejaz, bringing the caliphate and holy cities under Ottoman rule.

entities.name: Reign of Suleiman the Magnificent
entities.summary: Longest-reigning sultan: conquest of Belgrade, Rhodes and Hungary, legal codification and the siege of Vienna.

entities.name: Tanzimat
entities.summary: Reform era of legal equality, codified law, conscription and centralisation.

entities.name: Treaty of Karlowitz
entities.summary: First treaty in which the Ottomans ceded major territory, giving Hungary to the Habsburgs.

entities.name: Treaty of Sevres
entities.summary: Punitive partition treaty rejected by the Turkish nationalists and superseded by Lausanne.

entities.name: Young Turk Revolution
entities.summary: Committee of Union and Progress forced the restoration of the constitution and parliament.

entities.name: Comecon
entities.summary: Soviet-led economic organisation coordinating the planned economies of the Eastern bloc.

entities.name: Detente
entities.summary: Easing of superpower tension with SALT, the Helsinki Accords and expanded trade, ended by Afghanistan.

entities.name: Second Cold War
entities.summary: Renewed confrontation after Afghanistan, with missile deployments, SDI and heightened nuclear risk.

entities.name: Warsaw Pact
entities.summary: Soviet-led military alliance of Eastern bloc states, dissolved in 1991.

entities.name: Inchon Landing
entities.summary: MacArthur's amphibious envelopment that recaptured Seoul and reversed the North Korean advance.

entities.name: Colony of New Zealand
entities.summary: British colony that gained self-government in 1852 and fought the New Zealand Wars over land.

entities.name: Cook's Circumnavigation of New Zealand
entities.summary: Cook charted both main islands, opening sustained European contact with Maori.

entities.name: Dominion of New Zealand
entities.summary: Self-governing dominion from 1907, fully sovereign under the 1947 adoption of the Statute of Westminster.

entities.name: Musket Wars
entities.summary: Inter-iwi wars transformed by trade muskets, causing large casualties and migrations before colonisation.

entities.name: New Zealand Nuclear-Free Policy
entities.summary: Ban on nuclear-armed and nuclear-powered ships that suspended New Zealand's ANZUS obligations.

entities.name: New Zealand Wars
entities.summary: Conflicts between the Crown, settlers and Maori over sovereignty and land, followed by large confiscations.

entities.name: New Zealand Women's Suffrage
entities.summary: First self-governing country to grant women the parliamentary vote.

entities.name: Treaty of Waitangi
entities.summary: Agreement between the Crown and Maori chiefs, with differing English and Maori texts, New Zealand's founding document.

entities.name: Waitangi Tribunal
entities.summary: Body established to investigate Crown breaches of the Treaty of Waitangi and recommend redress.

entities.name: Vietnamese August Revolution
entities.summary: Viet Minh seizure of power and Ho Chi Minh's declaration of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam.

entities.name: Battle of Dien Bien Phu
entities.summary: Viet Minh victory over the French garrison that ended French rule in Indochina.

entities.name: Doi Moi
entities.summary: Market-oriented reforms that transformed Vietnam into a fast-growing export economy.

entities.name: Fall of Saigon
entities.summary: North Vietnamese capture of Saigon on 30 April 1975 ended the war.

entities.name: French Conquest of Vietnam
entities.summary: Campaigns from Saigon to Tonkin that made Vietnam a French colony and protectorates.

entities.name: Leadership of Ho Chi Minh
entities.summary: Founder of Vietnamese communism and president of North Vietnam until his death.

entities.name: Later Le Dynasty and Trinh-Nguyen Division
entities.summary: Nominal Le kings with real power split between the Trinh lords in the north and the Nguyen in the south.

entities.name: Democratic Republic of Vietnam
entities.summary: Communist northern state under Ho Chi Minh, which won the war and unified the country in 1976.

entities.name: Socialist Republic of Vietnam
entities.summary: Unified communist state since 1976, market-reforming since doi moi in 1986.

entities.name: Republic of Vietnam
entities.summary: Anti-communist southern state under Diem then Thieu, which collapsed with the fall of Saigon.

entities.name: Tet Offensive
entities.summary: Coordinated communist attacks that failed militarily but broke American public support for the war.

entities.name: Aceh War
entities.summary: Long Dutch war to subdue the Aceh sultanate, one of the colonial era's most costly campaigns.

entities.name: Indonesian Mass Killings of 1965-66
entities.summary: Army-led massacre of at least half a million alleged communists after a failed coup.

entities.name: Indonesian National Awakening
entities.summary: Rise of nationalist organisations from Budi Utomo to Sukarno's PNI and the 1928 Youth Pledge.

entities.name: Indonesian National Revolution
entities.summary: Four-year struggle after the 17 August 1945 proclamation that forced Dutch recognition of independence.

entities.name: Reformasi
entities.summary: Democratisation after Suharto's fall, with decentralisation and direct presidential elections.

entities.name: Japanese Occupation of the Dutch East Indies
entities.summary: Three years of Japanese rule that destroyed Dutch authority and armed Indonesian nationalists.

entities.name: Java War
entities.summary: Diponegoro's revolt against Dutch rule, ending in his exile and the cultivation system.

entities.name: New Order
entities.summary: Suharto's authoritarian developmental regime, ended by the Asian financial crisis and mass protest.

entities.name: Presidency of Sukarno
entities.summary: Founding president: Pancasila, Bandung Conference, Guided Democracy and confrontation with Malaysia.

entities.name: Leadership of Ali Khamenei
entities.summary: Supreme leader since 1989, presiding over nuclear disputes, sanctions and protest movements.

entities.name: Leadership of Ruhollah Khomeini
entities.summary: Founder and first supreme leader, who institutionalised clerical rule and led the war with Iraq.

entities.name: Reign of Shah Abbas I
entities.summary: Reformed the army, retook lands from the Ottomans and Uzbeks, and rebuilt Isfahan.

entities.name: Surrender at Appomattox
entities.summary: Lee's surrender to Grant at Appomattox Court House, effectively ending the Civil War.

entities.name: Battle of Antietam
entities.summary: Bloodiest single day in American history; the strategic Union result let Lincoln issue the Emancipation Proclamation.

entities.name: Battle of Gettysburg
entities.summary: Three-day Union victory in Pennsylvania that turned back Lee's second invasion of the North.

entities.name: Battle of Shiloh
entities.summary: Bloody two-day Union victory in Tennessee that revealed the war's likely cost.

entities.name: First Battle of Bull Run
entities.summary: First major land battle of the Civil War, a Confederate victory that shattered hopes of a quick Union win.

entities.name: Sherman's March to the Sea
entities.summary: Union campaign of destruction from Atlanta to Savannah intended to break southern will to fight.

entities.name: Siege of Vicksburg
entities.summary: Grant's siege that captured the last Confederate stronghold on the Mississippi, splitting the Confederacy.

entities.name: Battle of Bunker Hill
entities.summary: Costly British victory on the Charlestown heights outside Boston that showed colonial militia could stand against regulars.

entities.name: Battles of Lexington and Concord
entities.summary: First shots of the Revolutionary War, as Massachusetts militia turned back British regulars sent to seize colonial arms.

entities.name: Battles of Saratoga
entities.summary: Decisive American victory that destroyed Burgoyne's army and brought France into the war as an ally.

entities.name: Siege of Yorktown
entities.summary: Franco-American siege that forced Cornwallis's surrender and effectively ended the Revolutionary War.

entities.name: Valley Forge Encampment
entities.summary: Winter camp where Washington's army endured privation and was retrained under von Steuben.

entities.name: Assassination of Martin Luther King Jr.
entities.summary: King's murder in Memphis triggered unrest in over a hundred cities and hastened the Fair Housing Act.

entities.name: Freedom Summer
entities.summary: Mississippi voter registration campaign marked by the murders of three activists and the challenge of the MFDP.

entities.name: Little Rock Integration Crisis
entities.summary: Eisenhower sent federal troops to escort nine Black students into Central High School after the governor blocked desegregation.

entities.name: March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom
entities.summary: Mass rally of about 250,000 people where Martin Luther King Jr. delivered the 'I Have a Dream' speech.

entities.name: Montgomery Bus Boycott
entities.summary: Year-long boycott sparked by Rosa Parks's arrest that desegregated Montgomery buses and elevated Martin Luther King Jr.

entities.name: Selma to Montgomery Marches
entities.summary: Voting rights marches including 'Bloody Sunday' at the Edmund Pettus Bridge, which spurred the Voting Rights Act.

entities.name: Battle of the Little Bighorn
entities.summary: Lakota, Cheyenne and Arapaho warriors annihilated Custer's detachment of the 7th Cavalry in Montana.

entities.name: Agricultural Adjustment Administration
entities.summary: New Deal agency that paid farmers to cut production in order to raise crop prices.

entities.name: Civilian Conservation Corps
entities.summary: New Deal work relief agency that employed three million young men on forestry, parks and erosion projects.

entities.name: National Recovery Administration
entities.summary: New Deal agency setting industrial codes on prices and wages, struck down by the Supreme Court in 1935.

entities.name: Tennessee Valley Authority
entities.summary: New Deal public corporation that built dams, generated power and modernised the Tennessee Valley.

entities.name: Works Progress Administration
entities.summary: Largest New Deal agency, employing 8.5 million people on public works, arts and writing projects.

entities.name: Black Codes
entities.summary: Southern state laws restricting freedpeople's labour, movement and rights, which provoked congressional Reconstruction.

entities.name: Freedmen's Bureau
entities.summary: Federal agency providing relief, labour contracts, courts and schools to freedpeople and refugees in the postwar South.
aliases: Bureau of Refugees, Freedmen, and Abandoned Lands

entities.name: First Human Spaceflight
entities.summary: Yuri Gagarin orbited the Earth on 12 April 1961 aboard Vostok 1.

entities.name: Launch of Sputnik 1
entities.summary: First artificial satellite, launched by the USSR on 4 October 1957, opening the space age.

entities.name: Battle of New Orleans
entities.summary: Jackson's lopsided victory over British regulars, fought after the peace treaty was signed, made him a national hero.

entities.name: Battle of Tippecanoe
entities.summary: Harrison's attack on Prophetstown that broke Tenskwatawa's confederacy and helped precipitate the War of 1812.

entities.name: Burning of Washington
entities.summary: British forces captured the capital and burned the Capitol and White House in retaliation for raids in Canada.

entities.name: Western Front of the First World War
entities.summary: Four years of trench stalemate in France and Belgium, with battles such as Verdun, the Somme and Passchendaele.

entities.name: Atomic Bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki
entities.summary: US atomic attacks that killed well over 100,000 people and preceded Japan's surrender.
entities.qualified_name: Atomic Bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki (World War II (United States))

entities.name: Attack on Pearl Harbor
entities.summary: Japanese surprise attack on the Pacific Fleet in Hawaii that brought the United States into World War II.
entities.qualified_name: Attack on Pearl Harbor (World War II (United States))

entities.name: Battle of Iwo Jima
entities.summary: Costly Marine assault on a fortified Japanese island, immortalised by the flag-raising on Mount Suribachi.

entities.name: Battle of Midway
entities.summary: Decisive US naval victory that destroyed four Japanese carriers and turned the Pacific war.

entities.name: Battle of Stalingrad
entities.summary: Soviet encirclement and destruction of a German army, the turning point on the Eastern Front.

entities.name: Normandy Landings
entities.summary: Allied invasion of northwest Europe on 6 June 1944 that opened the western front against Germany.

entities.name: Manhattan Project
entities.summary: Secret Allied programme led by the United States that built the first nuclear weapons at Los Alamos, Oak Ridge and Hanford.

entities.name: Operation Barbarossa
entities.summary: German invasion of the Soviet Union, the largest land offensive in history and the war's decisive theatre.

entities.name: Abolition of the Han
entities.summary: Domains replaced by prefectures, ending feudal decentralisation.

entities.name: Satsuma Rebellion
entities.summary: Last samurai revolt, led by Saigo Takamori and crushed by the conscript army.

entities.name: East German Uprising of 1953
entities.summary: Workers' strikes and protests on 17 June 1953 crushed by Soviet tanks.

entities.name: Reign of Frederick the Great
entities.summary: Frederick II seized Silesia, survived the Seven Years' War and made Prussia a great power while patronising the Enlightenment.

entities.name: Roman Britain
entities.summary: The Roman province of Britannia, from the Claudian invasion of AD 43 to the effective end of imperial administration around 410.

entities.name: Kingdom of York (Jorvik)
entities.summary: Norse kingdom centred on York, ruled by Viking kings until Eric Bloodaxe's expulsion and death in 954. Dates are received from chronicles.

entities.name: Gregorian mission of Augustine
entities.summary: Augustine's arrival in Kent began the conversion of the Anglo-Saxons and the founding of the see of Canterbury. Date received from Bede.

entities.name: Kingdom of Bernicia
entities.summary: Northern Anglian kingdom between the Tees and the Forth, later joined with Deira to form Northumbria. Dates are received tradition.

entities.name: Kingdom of Deira
entities.summary: Anglian kingdom in what became Yorkshire, absorbed into Northumbria in the seventh century. Dates are received tradition.

entities.name: Synod of Whitby
entities.summary: Northumbrian council that adopted Roman rather than Irish practice for Easter and the tonsure. Date received from Bede.

entities.name: AElfweard of Wessex
entities.summary: Son of Edward the Elder who may have reigned in Wessex for a few weeks in 924; his kingship is disputed. Dates are received from chronicle tradition.

entities.name: Alfred the Great
entities.summary: King of the West Saxons who resisted the Viking Great Heathen Army, secured the Danelaw frontier and promoted learning and law. Regnal dates are those received from the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle and later chronicles and may be uncertain by a year or more.

entities.name: Edward the Elder
entities.summary: Son of Alfred who conquered much of the southern Danelaw and extended West Saxon overlordship over Mercia. Regnal dates are those received from the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle and later chronicles and may be uncertain by a year or more.

entities.name: Treaty of Alfred and Guthrum
entities.summary: Agreement partitioning England between English and Danish rule along the Watling Street line. Dating is uncertain and received.

entities.name: May 1968 in France
entities.summary: Student revolt and general strike of ten million workers that shook de Gaulle's government.

entities.name: Presidency of Charles de Gaulle
entities.summary: Founding president of the Fifth Republic: Algerian independence, nuclear force de frappe, NATO withdrawal, and resignation after 1968.

entities.name: Presidency of Emmanuel Macron
entities.summary: Centrist president elected 2017 and re-elected 2022, facing gilets jaunes protests, COVID-19 and pension reform.

entities.name: Presidency of Francois Hollande
entities.summary: Socialist president who legalised same-sex marriage and led France through the 2015 terror attacks and COP21.

entities.name: Presidency of Francois Mitterrand
entities.summary: First Socialist president of the Fifth Republic; nationalisations then austerity, abolition of the death penalty, Maastricht.

entities.name: Presidency of Georges Pompidou
entities.summary: Gaullist president who oversaw industrial modernisation and accepted British entry into the EEC; died in office.

entities.name: Presidency of Valery Giscard d'Estaing
entities.summary: Centrist president who liberalised social law, legalised abortion and helped create the European Monetary System.

entities.name: Presidency of Jacques Chirac
entities.summary: Gaullist president who ended conscription, adopted the euro and opposed the 2003 Iraq war.

entities.name: Presidency of Nicolas Sarkozy
entities.summary: Presidency marked by the 2008 financial crisis, NATO reintegration and the Libya intervention.

entities.name: French Directory
entities.summary: Five-man executive governing France between the Terror and Bonaparte's Brumaire coup.

entities.name: Reign of Terror
entities.summary: Robespierre and the Committee of Public Safety executed tens of thousands until Thermidor ended the Jacobin dictatorship.

entities.name: Dreyfus Affair
entities.summary: Wrongful conviction of a Jewish officer for treason that split France over antisemitism, army and republic.

entities.name: French Law on the Separation of Church and State
entities.summary: 1905 law establishing laicite by ending state recognition and funding of religions.

entities.name: Reign of Louis-Philippe I
entities.summary: Orleanist king of the French whose narrow franchise and refusal of reform ended in the February Revolution.

entities.name: Reign of Charles IX of France
entities.summary: Ruled under his mother Catherine de' Medici; his reign saw the St Bartholomew's Day massacre of Huguenots in 1572.

entities.name: Reign of Francis I of France
entities.summary: Renaissance king who fought Charles V in Italy, patronised Leonardo and Chambord, and made French the language of administration in 1539.

entities.name: Reign of Francis II of France
entities.summary: Teenage king married to Mary Stuart whose brief reign was dominated by the Guise faction.

entities.name: Reign of Henry II of France
entities.summary: Ended the Italian Wars at Cateau-Cambresis in 1559 and died in a tournament accident, leaving power to Catherine de' Medici.

entities.name: Reign of Henry III of France
entities.summary: Last Valois king, caught between the Catholic League and Henry of Navarre; assassinated in 1589.

entities.name: Reign of Henry IV of France
entities.summary: First Bourbon king; converted to Catholicism, issued the Edict of Nantes in 1598 and rebuilt the kingdom before his assassination.

entities.name: Reign of Louis XIII
entities.summary: Reign dominated by Cardinal Richelieu, who broke Huguenot autonomy and entered the Thirty Years' War against the Habsburgs.

entities.name: Reign of Louis XIV
entities.summary: Seventy-two-year reign of the Sun King: Versailles, absolutism, revocation of the Edict of Nantes and near-continuous European war.

entities.name: Reign of Louis XV
entities.summary: Long reign marked by regency, the War of the Austrian Succession, and the loss of New France and India in the Seven Years' War.

entities.name: Reign of Louis XVI
entities.summary: Fiscal crisis and the summoning of the Estates-General led to revolution; deposed in 1792 and guillotined in 1793.

entities.name: Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen
entities.summary: Foundational statement of natural rights adopted by the National Assembly in August 1789.

entities.name: Storming of the Bastille
entities.summary: Parisian crowds seized the royal fortress-prison on 14 July 1789, the symbolic start of the Revolution.

entities.name: Reign of Napoleon III
entities.summary: Emperor whose modernising rule ended in capture at Sedan and the fall of the empire.

entities.name: Disaster Year of 1672
entities.summary: French, English and German attack that nearly destroyed the Republic and brought William III to power.

entities.name: Reign of Queen Beatrix
entities.summary: Queen for 33 years, abdicating in favour of her son in 2013.

entities.name: Reign of Queen Juliana
entities.summary: Queen during Indonesian independence, the 1953 North Sea flood and postwar reconstruction.

entities.name: Reign of Queen Wilhelmina
entities.summary: Queen through both world wars who led resistance broadcasts from London exile.

entities.name: Reign of King Willem-Alexander
entities.summary: Dutch king since 2013.

entities.name: Reign of William I of the Netherlands
entities.summary: First Dutch king; lost Belgium in 1830-39 and abdicated in 1840.

entities.name: American War of Independence
entities.summary: Loss of the thirteen American colonies after Saratoga and Yorktown, recognised at the Peace of Paris.

entities.name: Founding of the modern Commonwealth
entities.summary: The London Declaration made the Commonwealth a free association of equal states with the King as its head.

entities.name: Decolonisation of the British Empire
entities.summary: Withdrawal from India in 1947 through African independence in the 1960s to the handover of Hong Kong in 1997.

entities.name: First Boer War
entities.summary: Transvaal war of independence ending in British defeat at Majuba Hill.

entities.name: Independence and partition of India
entities.summary: British withdrawal created India and Pakistan, with mass displacement and communal violence.

entities.name: Malayan Emergency
entities.summary: Long counter-insurgency campaign against communist guerrillas in Malaya.

entities.name: Mau Mau Uprising
entities.summary: Kenyan rebellion against colonial land policy, suppressed with mass detention and violence.

entities.name: Navigation Acts
entities.summary: Series of laws reserving colonial trade to English and British shipping, a pillar of mercantilism until repeal.

entities.name: Second Boer War
entities.summary: Long South African war involving sieges, guerrilla resistance, farm burning and concentration camps, ending at Vereeniging.

entities.name: Second British Empire
entities.summary: The eastward-facing empire centred on India, Africa and the settler dominions, at its greatest extent after the First World War.

entities.name: Slavery Abolition Act
entities.summary: Abolished slavery across most of the empire from 1834, with apprenticeship and compensation to slave owners.

entities.name: Statute of Westminster
entities.summary: Recognised legislative independence for the dominions, converting empire into Commonwealth.

entities.name: War of 1812
entities.summary: Anglo-American war fought in Canada and at sea, including the burning of Washington, settled by the Treaty of Ghent.

entities.name: Bloody Sunday
entities.summary: Paratroopers shot dead thirteen civil rights marchers in Derry on 30 January 1972, with a fourteenth dying later.

entities.name: Good Friday Agreement
entities.summary: Settlement establishing power-sharing devolution, cross-border bodies and consent for constitutional change.

entities.name: The Troubles
entities.summary: Three decades of conflict in Northern Ireland between republicans, loyalists and the British state, ending with the Good Friday Agreement.

entities.name: Building of the Antonine Wall
entities.summary: Turf frontier across the Forth-Clyde isthmus, occupied for barely a generation.

entities.name: Boudican revolt
entities.summary: Iceni rising led by Boudica that destroyed Camulodunum, Londinium and Verulamium before defeat at Watling Street.

entities.name: Division of Britannia into provinces
entities.summary: Severus divided Britain into Britannia Superior and Inferior; Diocletian later subdivided it further into a diocese of four or five provinces.

entities.name: End of Roman rule in Britain
entities.summary: Withdrawal of the last field armies and the traditional Rescript of Honorius telling the cities to look to their own defence. Dating is received tradition.

entities.name: Building of Hadrian's Wall
entities.summary: Frontier wall from Tyne to Solway begun under Hadrian, later Rome's northern boundary in Britain.

entities.name: Roman conquest of Britain
entities.summary: Campaigns from Aulus Plautius' landing in AD 43 to Agricola's victory at Mons Graupius, bringing most of Britain under Rome.

entities.name: Languages
entities.summary: The languages of the world, arranged by descent. Families and their subgroups contain the languages that descend from them; isolates and unclassified languages sit apart, since no descent can be shown for them.

entities.name: Isolates
entities.summary: A language isolate has no demonstrable relatives. That is a statement about the evidence, not about the language: Basque, Korean and Sumerian are isolates.

entities.name: Disputed Groupings
entities.summary: Reconstructions of families that are proposed rather than accepted. Altaic, Amerind and Nostratic are the famous cases: each has been argued for and none commands agreement, so Glottolog recognises no such family and there is no clade for the reconstruction to sit at the root of. Recorded because the proposal is part of the history of the field.

entities.name: Unclassified
entities.summary: Attested too thinly to place in any family. Distinct from an isolate, where the evidence is good and the relatives simply are not there.

entities.name: Haida
entities.summary: Northwest Coast nation of Haida Gwaii and southern Alaska, celebrated for monumental cedar carving and canoes.

entities.name: Egyptian
entities.summary: Attested across four thousand years, from hieroglyphs to Coptic, the longest documented history of any language.

entities.name: Eastern Timor
entities.summary: A subgroup within the Austronesian family. No language in this roster is placed directly here; it exists to keep the descent path intact.

entities.name: Latin
entities.summary: Ancestor of the Romance languages and the learned language of western Europe long after it stopped being anyone's first.

entities.name: Tetunic
entities.summary: A subgroup within the Austronesian family. No language in this roster is placed directly here; it exists to keep the descent path intact.

entities.name: Aramaic
entities.summary: Administrative language of the Achaemenid Empire and still spoken by small communities today.

entities.name: Ajami Hausa
entities.date_note: Start estimated between 1600 CE and 1650 CE.

entities.name: Akkadian
entities.date_note: Start estimated between 2600 BCE and 2350 BCE. End estimated between 500 BCE and 100 CE.
entities.summary: The first Semitic language written down, and the diplomatic language of the Bronze Age Near East.

entities.name: Amharic (Early Amharic royal songs)
entities.date_note: Start estimated between 1300 CE and 1400 CE. End estimated between 1600 CE and 1700 CE.

entities.name: Ammonite
entities.date_note: Start estimated between 900 BCE and 800 BCE. End estimated between 500 BCE and 400 BCE.

entities.name: Amorite
entities.date_note: Start estimated between 2100 BCE and 2000 BCE. End estimated between 2000 BCE and 1000 BCE.

entities.name: Ancient Greek (Attic)
entities.date_note: Start estimated between 500 BCE and 440 BCE. End estimated between 300 BCE and 285 BCE.
entities.summary: Written first in Linear B, then in the alphabet that carried Homer, tragedy and Greek philosophy.

entities.name: Ancient Macedonian
entities.date_note: Start estimated between 1000 BCE and 417 BCE. End estimated between 300 BCE and 100 CE.

entities.name: Apabhramsha
entities.date_note: Start estimated between 500 CE and 600 CE. End estimated between 1200 CE and 1300 CE.

entities.name: Aquitanian
entities.date_note: Start estimated between 100 BCE and 1 CE. End estimated between 400 CE and 600 CE.

entities.name: Ardhamagadhi Prakrit
entities.date_note: Start estimated between 500 BCE and 260 BCE. End estimated between 600 CE and 900 CE.

entities.name: Avestan
entities.date_note: Start estimated between 1500 BCE and 1000 BCE.
entities.summary: Language of the Zoroastrian liturgy, preserved orally for centuries before it was written.

entities.name: Awadhi
entities.date_note: Start estimated between 1375 CE and 1379 CE. End estimated between 1700 CE and 1900 CE.

entities.name: Bactrian
entities.date_note: Start estimated between 300 BCE and 100 CE. End estimated between 700 CE and 1000 CE.

entities.name: Berber (Old Tuareg / Tifinagh-era Libyco-Berber)
entities.date_note: Start estimated between 1000 BCE and 200 BCE. End estimated between 300 CE and 700 CE.

entities.name: Biblical Hebrew
entities.date_note: Start estimated between 1000 BCE and 900 BCE. End estimated between 70 CE and 200 CE.

entities.name: Burgundian
entities.date_note: Start estimated between 1 CE and 100 CE. End estimated between 534 CE and 600 CE.

entities.name: Carian
entities.date_note: Start estimated between 700 BCE and 600 BCE. End estimated between 300 BCE and 200 BCE.

entities.name: Caucasian Albanian
entities.date_note: Start estimated between 400 CE and 600 CE. End estimated between 700 CE and 800 CE.

entities.name: Celtiberian
entities.date_note: Start estimated between 200 BCE and 100 BCE. End estimated between 100 CE and 200 CE.

entities.name: Chorasmian
entities.date_note: Start estimated between 550 BCE and 200 BCE. End estimated between 1100 CE and 1300 CE.

entities.name: Church Slavonic
entities.date_note: Start estimated between 1050 CE and 1100 CE.

entities.name: Classical Arabic
entities.date_note: Start estimated between 600 CE and 700 CE. End estimated between 1850 CE and 1900 CE.

entities.name: Classical Armenian (Grabar)
entities.date_note: End estimated between 1100 CE and 1200 CE.

entities.name: Classical Aymara
entities.date_note: Start estimated between 1500 CE and 1603 CE. End estimated between 1700 CE and 1800 CE.

entities.name: Classical Chinese (Literary Chinese / wenyanwen)
entities.date_note: Start estimated between 500 BCE and 479 BCE. End estimated between 200 CE and 220 CE.

entities.name: Classical Hawaiian
